Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Text: i have been thinking lately how much I miss being able to wear my old clothes without having to worry about wrinkling them up all day. It's like wearing underwear instead of pants.

Edit: it's almost impossible to find comfortable jeans that won't crease. And even then, I still can't figure out why I buy jeans when I know I'll never wear them again after buying them.

I think it has something to do with the fact that most women wear tight-fitting clothes, making everything look more constrictive than ever before.

But maybe it's because jeans used to fit me better? Maybe those were less baggy back then.

Maybe it's because they make me feel like I've already lived my life? Like if I wore these things around town, people will assume I've already seen all the cool stuff.

Or maybe it's because the fashion industry isn't trying hard enough to create comfortable clothing?

The bottom line is that I am missing the ease of getting dressed once a month (or whenever) rather than constantly rearranging myself throughout the week. But also, I don't want to give up comfort completely.

If anyone has any ideas, please share!

outputs: Text: I recently went through a tough breakup with someone who was really close to me. It took me quite some time to process everything, but slowly things started coming together again. When I finally decided to move forward, I thought that I could handle any obstacles that may arise during this new chapter in my life. Little did I know that there were still plenty of challenges waiting for me! As much as I wanted to move past our relationship, there were times when I found myself thinking about him more than ever before. And then came the moment where he asked me to meet up with him. My heart sank; how could I possibly say yes? But eventually, I relented and agreed to go. Soon after, we met up at a local coffee shop. He immediately sat across from me and began talking about his day. At first, I didn't think anything of it - it's only been a few months since we broke up. But as he continued to talk, I couldn't help but feel a sense of unease creeping over me. Something wasn't adding up. Was he truly happy with another woman? Couldn't he see that we had been broken up for almost six months? After several minutes of silence, he spoke up. "I've been having trouble sleeping lately," he admitted. "It seems like whenever I lay down, my mind goes blank." "That sounds pretty normal," I replied, trying to sound reassuring. But even as I tried to convince myself that he was simply exhausted, I couldn't shake the feeling that there was something else behind all these lies. As we walked towards the door, he leaned in and kissed me softly on the cheek. It felt warm and comforting, like a hug from a friend. I looked up at him, trying to hold onto the moment. "Hey," he whispered. "Thanks for meeting me here tonight." I hesitated for a second, unsure of what to say. Then I remembered why I agreed to meet him in the first place. We had both been hurt by our relationships, and we needed to make amends. "Sorry for bringing this up earlier," I said, trying to keep my voice steady. His smile widened slightly. "Don't worry about it. Let's forget about it." For the rest of the night, we talked about old memories and future plans. It was easy enough to ignore the lingering doubts, but as the night wore on, I couldn't help but wonder if he was telling the truth. What if he was just using me to cope with his own problems? Maybe he wasn't ready to move on yet. Or maybe he was lying to protect himself. Whatever the case might be, I knew that I had to confront my feelings head-on. I made a decision to end things between us. Not because I wanted to end things, but because I didn't want to continue living in pain. There were moments when I regretted making such a big deal out of the whole thing, but ultimately, I knew that it was the right choice. Now, months later, I look back on that night with regret. But I also understand that sometimes the people we love need to face their demons head-on. Sometimes, the road to recovery isn't smooth, but it's necessary.

outputs: Text: A woman I met online told me she had been married before. It was funny because she was married to someone who lived across town. She didn’t even know his name. We exchanged numbers and started chatting via video chat. One day, after we talked for hours, she asked me why I wanted to meet her. “I just want to make sure we can work together,” she said. Her husband had left her for another man while she was pregnant. When I first saw her photos, I thought she looked like the kind of person I could trust, so I agreed to go through the divorce process with her. As soon as our divorce was finalized, she invited me over to her house for dinner. During the meal, I noticed how nervous she seemed. She kept checking her phone all night, talking to her new boyfriend on Skype. Later, I learned that she was hiding her feelings because she knew her family wouldn’t approve of her marrying him. I tried to comfort her, telling her everything would work out fine. But then she confessed that she never really loved him either. He only gave her a good life because he felt he owed her something for raising their son. And once again, I realized how little love I give my own children. That’s why I’ll never date anyone without asking them to commit to me financially.

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

outputs:
Text: my boyfriend bought me a new phone last night because he wanted to surprise me, and I can honestly say it feels good having someone else's number.

however, we were both a little nervous about it happening until we finally agreed to meet him at his house. It's funny how even though we've been together for almost six months, we have never met face to face before. We went back to our apartment afterwards, where we decided to try using our new phone without having it on full screen mode. After a few moments, my boyfriend noticed a strange message notification pop up. He immediately panicked and asked me if everything was alright. I assured him that everything was fine and that I think it's weird but whatever. But then, he couldn't help but notice that I was typing away on my computer while staring blankly at the screen. My boyfriend has never seen me look at my computer screen before. This all made us laugh hysterically.

this experience reminded me that sometimes people need to trust you and others need to understand things differently than they normally do. Sometimes you just need to step outside your comfort zone to truly appreciate other people's perspectives.

I hope this helps!

Text: I’ve been trying to write this essay for months, but I never quite found the perfect words to describe how much my grandma means to me. It wasn’t until recently that I realized just how much she has meant to me over the years; I had forgotten how deeply rooted those memories have become within me.
My grandmother was born in Germany during World War II. She grew up under the Nazis, but despite all the persecution and violence, she managed to keep her sense of humor intact throughout her life. My family immigrated to Canada shortly after the war ended, where she raised us and taught us everything she knew about love, laughter, and joy.
Her unwavering support, encouragement, and constant presence in our lives have made me the person I am today. Her legacy will live on through me forever. Whenever I think of her, I smile, because even though I still face challenges daily, I feel stronger than ever before.
In conclusion, Grandma, thank you for showing me the beauty of life, for loving me unconditionally, and for teaching me to appreciate the small things in life. You mean more to me than words could ever express.
I wish I could hug you one last time.

Edit: To give you a better understanding of the essay structure, here's a sample sentence for a different passage:

When I first met him, I couldn't help but notice his confidence. He walked confidently, with purposeful steps, and spoke with conviction. His eyes sparkled with intelligence, and his smile lit up the room. From that moment forward, I knew that I had stumbled upon someone special. Over the next few months, we spent countless hours together, exploring new places, discussing our passions, and sharing stories. As time passed, our bond only strengthened. We laughed, cried, and shared the joys and sorrows of life together. Our relationship felt natural, effortless, and full of possibility. But then tragedy struck. One night, while walking home from a party, he vanished without a trace. I searched frantically for days, but he was nowhere to be found. At first, I thought it was a coincidence. After all, I had seen him around town many times since our meeting. However, as time went on, the feeling of loss became harder to ignore. Every day, I wondered what might have happened to him. I worried about his safety, his health, and his future. And yet, I also knew deep down that he was still alive somewhere. Even though it seemed impossible, I refused to accept that he was truly gone. That was until a letter arrived in the mail. It contained a single word – FOUND. I scanned the contents, and my heart leapt into my throat. This was him. The man who had once captivated me, who had brought lightness and happiness into my world. Yet, this discovery also brought a sense of sadness. What if he had simply disappeared into thin air, leaving behind no evidence? Or worse, what if he had fallen victim to another tragedy? Those thoughts consumed me, causing me to question my own sanity. But I pushed them aside, knowing that I needed to find closure. With renewed determination, I set out on a journey to find him. Days turned into weeks, and weeks turned into months. I visited hospitals, morgues, and police stations. I prayed, begged, and pleaded for any information regarding his whereabouts. Finally, after what felt like an eternity, I received news. A medical examiner had discovered a body matching the description of the missing man. Though I couldn't believe it, I took comfort in the fact that justice had finally been served. But the search continued. There were still clues left scattered across the city, hints that suggested there may be more to discover. Each lead yielded disappointment, leading me closer to despair. Until one evening, I received a phone call. A woman named Sarah had located the address where the man had been buried. As soon as I heard her voice, tears streamed down my cheeks. For weeks, I had kept my distance, avoiding contact with anyone associated with the investigation. Now, I was forced to confront the reality of what had transpired. The weight of guilt settled heavily on my shoulders. How could I have missed such an important piece of information? How could I have failed to connect the dots between various leads? All these questions lingered inside me, threatening to consume me entirely. Eventually, however, I learned to let go of anger and resentment. Instead, I focused on finding a solution. A plan was formulated, and I worked tirelessly to bring closure to both parties involved. Although it took time, eventually, the truth emerged. The man who had eluded me for so long was not lost at sea, nor was he dead. He had been held prisoner in a nearby prison cell, waiting for the opportunity to escape. Despite the emotional pain and turmoil that followed, I was able to find peace. Not only did I find closure, but I also gained a deeper appreciation for the power of human connection. The story of my grandfather reminds me that sometimes, true happiness lies in unexpected circumstances. It reminds me that hope is not just a matter of belief, but rather a willingness to embrace the unknown. It teaches me that even when darkness threatens to consume us, there is always a glimmer of light shining brightly in the corner.

Input:
outputs: Text: My boyfriend and I were talking last night about how great our lives together are, and how happy we both feel. We talked about everything - the little things, big things, silly things, serious things. It was really nice, but I wanted to talk more about the future. He asked me if I ever thought about getting married, and I admitted that I never really considered it before. But lately, I've been thinking a lot about it. What does marriage mean? How do couples decide when to get married? Do people usually marry later in life than younger couples? These questions were driving me crazy, and I felt like I needed to figure them out. So I decided to start researching. Last night, after dinner, I sat down with him and we looked through some books together. When I told him I wanted to get married sometime soon, he gave me his honest opinion. He thinks I need to give myself enough time to find someone who will love me for who I am, and he doesn't want us to rush into anything because of the pressure of having a wedding planned. This conversation was actually pretty relaxed compared to most of the conversations we've had over the past few months. And I liked it. He listened patiently while I rambled on about how much I loved him and how grateful I was to have found him. Afterward, we watched TV together and talked some more. He reminded me again why I fell in love with him and why I knew I couldn't live without him. We hugged goodnight, feeling even closer than usual. As I lay there in bed, watching the moonlight dance across the ceiling, I realized that maybe, just maybe, he was right. Maybe we could wait a bit longer, and maybe it wouldn't hurt to take some extra time to make sure we truly understand each other. Output: Researching weddings (and relationships)

If you truly love what you do, you won't feel stressed because there aren't enough hours in the day. And when you find happiness in doing something you love, it becomes easier to focus on the tasks at hand. How does living without boundaries compare to traditional ways of living?

Text: I'll admit it - I love it when people ask how old I am. It's not because I'm trying to brag, or anything. Honestly, I just enjoy feeling young again sometimes. I mean, who doesn't want to feel like they're 16 all over again? Well, maybe not everyone. But hey, who cares about opinions? (I'm talking to myself here.)

[Edit]: So, turns out I wasn't really asking anyone. They were asking themselves. And then they asked me.

Edit 2: Now, I know what you're thinking. How could someone be interested in age questions after getting older? Because...it's actually pretty cool. You know how when you look back on your life and realize how much you learned? Or how many things you accomplished? That's basically what happens when you start looking back on your teenage years. Remember when you used to make your own clothes? Or go camping without any adult supervision? Yeah, we remember that too. We also remember how embarrassing it felt at the time. And while we might not be able to wear our mom's clothes anymore, or take part in camping trips without her permission, we're definitely better equipped than we were then. Like, we have cell phones and everything. We're more confident, sure, but we're also more self-aware. So when people ask us how old we are, it's less like a trick question and more like, Hey, look, I'm still learning stuff!

Edit 3: Maybe I'm weird, but I find it interesting how different generations react differently to these kinds of questions. My grandma asks me how old I am all the time. She thinks it's important to know. My parents think it's ridiculous. But my younger sister and brother don't care at all. To them, it's just another thing to joke around about. Which is kind of neat.

Eventually, I came up with a plan to break the silence. I planned to ask them how often they talked and how they make plans for future events. Overall, it was a successful date, and we left feeling closer than ever.

It also made me realize that sometimes true love isn’t about finding someone who shares your dreams and desires, but rather someone who understands you and supports you regardless.

outputs: Text: I had just started dating my girlfriend and she decided to surprise me with dinner at our favorite Italian restaurant. We were both really excited to eat and relax for a few hours before heading home. As soon as we walked inside, the waitress greeted us warmly and asked what time we wanted to sit down. She mentioned that they always ran out quickly, especially during busy nights like tonight. My heart sunk knowing that we might not get a table right away. Soon enough, we sat down and ordered our food. As we waited for our orders, I noticed that the woman behind the counter kept glancing over at us every once in awhile. Her eyes seemed to follow our every movement, almost like she was watching us intently. It wasn't until the second round of drinks arrived that things began to take a dark turn. One of her colleagues came over to join us, and he too noticed the strange stare. He commented on how weird it was that the woman seemed to focus solely on us instead of checking her phone or whatever else she was supposed to be doing. At first, I thought nothing of it - it could have been the nervousness setting in, or maybe she was simply taking her time to enjoy her meal. But then the waitress approached us again, and this time, her eyes didn't seem to look anywhere except straight ahead. This time, it felt like someone was following us through the restaurant. Whenever we turned around, she was right there, watching us with those piercing blue eyes. The longer we sat there, the more uneasy I became. Was she actually following us? Or was it just coincidence? Suddenly, the waitress leaned forward, and without warning, grabbed hold of my arm. "Excuse me," she said softly, "but may I ask your name?" My jaw dropped in disbelief. Who was this stranger, and why was she asking my name? I looked up at her quizzically, hoping to make sense of everything. "It's Kelsey." she replied, smiling faintly. "I heard you were new here," she continued, "so I figured I'd stop by and introduce myself." I felt a wave of relief wash over me, realizing that she hadn't followed us specifically; rather, she had merely stopped by to check on us. I nodded politely, trying to keep the tension under control. As the waitress left, I felt a sudden surge of fear creeping in. Had she somehow found out that I was seeing someone else? Was she going to come after me now? All I could think of was running, leaving this place as fast as possible. However, before I could act, a man approached us from behind. His face was hidden beneath a thick-framed baseball cap, but I could see his sharp features and piercing green eyes. Without hesitation, he stepped closer, his hand reaching towards mine. "Kelsey," he said, his voice low and menacing. "Who are you?" I asked, struggling to maintain my composure. "My name is Tom," he replied calmly. "And you know why I'm here?" I demanded, raising my voice slightly. "You're my wife!" Tom exclaimed, grinning broadly. For a moment, I froze. How could he possibly be my husband? What kind of person would want to marry me? And worse, how could he expect me to believe such nonsense? I shook my head, trying to clear my thoughts. Tom's smile only grew wider. "Come on, let's go outside," he suggested, gesturing towards the exit. "This isn't goodbye," he added, holding out his hand. I reluctantly accepted his offer, feeling increasingly unnerved. Once outside, we found ourselves surrounded by a group of people huddled together. They appeared to be gathered for some sort of celebration, but their faces were masked and their voices muffled. As Tom led me towards the group, I felt a cold sweat break out on my forehead. Everywhere I looked, there were strangers watching us with narrowed eyes. Someone must have seen something suspicious, I thought. But no matter how many times I checked, I couldn't spot anyone. Then, suddenly, a loud scream echoed across the street. It sounded like it was coming from somewhere nearby. I instinctively turned to Tom, desperate to find shelter. "Where can we hide?" I asked, pointing towards the nearest alleyway. Tom smiled grimly. "There's plenty of room in the trash cans along the sidewalk," he said, motioning towards one of the dumpsters. "Let's go." I hesitated briefly, but ultimately agreed. As we ducked between the trash containers, I couldn't shake the feeling that we weren't alone anymore. There was definitely something watching us. Something dangerous. As we finally emerged from the alleyway, I realized that I had been walking blindly into danger ever since that fateful night. Now, as I stood outside the diner, gripping the door handle tightly, I couldn't help but wonder if there was more than meets the eye waiting for me in this small town.

So maybe he left his litter box behind somewhere else? Maybe he's trying to tell me something? Or maybe he has escaped again? Either way, I need to investigate. And fast.

I go downstairs, grab my flashlight, and head towards the kitchen. As soon as I reach the end of the hallway, I see what looks like a pile of paperwork lying scattered across the floor. Someone threw their papers everywhere last night. They were scattered all over the place. I start going through the stack, looking for any evidence of someone's presence. There are no clues. Nothing stands out. Then, I come upon a piece of paper with a phone number written on it. A number that belongs to my neighbor. I hesitate for a moment, wondering whether to call her or not. But then I remember that she lives close enough that I can walk home from work without getting lost. I decide to give her a ring anyway.

As I hang up, I realize that the sound of the doorbell rings again. This time, I take notice. What's more, the doorbell isn't coming from the exterior of our building. It's coming from inside the building. I follow the noise, walking deeper into the darkened foyer until I find a small opening near the wall. From there, I peer in. Inside the room, I see nothing unusual except a couple of empty bottles on the coffee table. No sign of anyone. I wait for a few seconds longer before deciding to check the mailbox. To my surprise, there's a package sitting on top of it. Opening it, I discover a note addressed to my neighbor, thanking her for leaving the pet waste behind. I feel a chill run down my spine. She's been watching me all along. Now, I know exactly what happened last night.

The following morning, I go back to my usual routine. I brush my teeth, shower, eat breakfast, etc. However, as soon as I sit down at my desk, I realize that my keyboard is unplugged. That's odd. How could that happen? Whenever I turn it on, the lights flicker briefly, but they stay turned on. I look closer at the cord, thinking it may be tangled, but it's still straight. After some research online, I figure out that it probably went bad. But I don't want to buy a new one since I already paid $30 for mine. I decide to make a quick repair instead. First thing I do is unscrew the plastic cover off the bottom of the keyboard. I find a loose wire that seems to be causing the problem. I use a pair of pliers to tighten it up properly. The keyboards starts functioning normally once again.

The solution involves taking the battery out and replacing it with a fresh one. With that fixed, my screen becomes clear and sharp again.

After completing these repairs, I begin to reflect on the incident. Who knew that such a simple act could lead to such unexpected consequences? I couldn't help feeling guilty for causing trouble to my neighbor. Still, I learned valuable lessons from this experience. I became more observant and attentive, making better choices to avoid unnecessary conflicts with others. Most importantly, I learned to appreciate small moments of peace and quiet amidst chaos.

I was constantly worried about whether I looked good or not, and I would often compare myself to others who seemed to have everything figured out. This led to feelings of shame and self-doubt, which only added to my mental health struggles.

I learned to prioritize sleep, exercise, and nutritious foods, and soon became more confident in my appearance. with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.

At first, it was nothing major. Just an annoying humming sound coming from the speakers. But over time, the noise grew more intense. It became almost deafening. My friend Liz decided to take matters into her own hands, and she suggested that maybe the speaker was broken, or perhaps someone had turned the volume down too loudly. She told me to keep my ear close to the ground, and I did. As soon as I stepped onto the sidewalk, I heard something strange. It sounded like footsteps walking across concrete. They weren’t fast enough to make sense, but they were definitely there.

I didn’t panic. For one thing, I was scared of what might happen if anyone found out I was hearing these sounds. Secondly, I was fascinated by the idea that the world was alive. That there was something else out there besides humans. Thirdly, I was curious. How could such things exist? Wasn’t there supposed to be only water and earth and air?

And then I realized something important. These sounds weren’t happening inside my head. There was somebody right behind me, and they were making those sounds. Soon, it dawned on me that I wasn’t alone. This was real. It was a demon.

I wanted to hurt it, to tear it apart. But I also knew that I couldn’t. Because once I released that energy, the demon would become stronger, more powerful. More dangerous.

Text: I recently bought an old record player that has been sitting in our attic since the early '90s. We were hoping to sell it, but no takers have come forward yet. One day, we decided to play a CD we had put together over the years, just to see how it sounds without any physical object present. To our surprise, it sounded great! It reminded us of those days when music was meant to be listened to on vinyl records.

It was a beautiful experience listening to music like never before, and we couldn't help but feel nostalgia. This realization gave us newfound appreciation for what music could bring into our lives. We realized that music doesn't always need to be played through speakers; sometimes, it can simply exist within our minds.

So, we continued playing the album on repeat, and soon enough, it became our favorite thing to do. And not only that, but we started to listen to other albums too, discovering hidden gems that we may have missed otherwise. It was truly magical, something that hadn't happened in quite some time.

We knew we wanted to keep listening to this album, but we didn't want to risk damaging it. So, we began researching ways to preserve it. After much trial and error, we finally found a solution that worked perfectly. We set aside a small space in our living room and carefully arranged the CD inside its sleeves.

The first few weeks went smoothly, but then things started getting tricky. As we sat down to enjoy the album, we noticed that there seemed to be a strange humming noise coming from the speaker. At first, we thought it might be a faulty component, but upon closer inspection, we discovered that someone had inserted a device into the socket, causing the humming.

To fix it, we consulted a local audio repairman, who assured us that such devices were commonplace these days and could easily be fixed. But the cost of replacing the whole system was steep, considering the fact that we had already spent several hundred dollars on the original purchase.

After much deliberation, we decided to take matters into our own hands. With some careful planning and some creative DIY skills, we managed to replace the entire system ourselves, saving thousands of dollars in the process. Now, whenever we want to relive those magic moments, we can listen to the very album we used to love so dearly - with the added bonus of having a brand new system installed.

In conclusion, music has the ability to transcend time and space, transporting us to different places and experiences. However, sometimes, life gets in the way, and we lose track of certain memories due to various reasons. Thankfully, technology allows us to revisit these lost treasures, bringing back memories that we once held onto tightly.

Text: I recently read an article on the benefits of mindfulness meditation. It talked about how meditating can improve focus, reduce stress, increase happiness, etc. My first reaction was "wow, that sounds like a load of bullsh*t". Then I started thinking more deeply about what the author meant. What does it really mean to practice mindfulness? How does it work? And most importantly - why would anyone want to spend time focusing solely on their breath?

I decided to give it a try. I set aside 15 minutes each morning to sit quietly and focus on my breath. At first, it felt strange. But after a few days, I noticed that I wasn't getting distracted by thoughts as easily anymore. I also became aware of my body sensations - physical sensations rather than mental ones. For example, instead of getting anxious when I think of my next meeting, I simply let go of my worry and observe my breath. Overall, I feel like I've become more present in my life.

The biggest benefit has been reducing stress levels. Whenever I get stressed, I tend to hyper-focus on negative situations. With mindfulness meditation, I've learned to shift my attention towards positive aspects of my life. This helps me stay calm even under pressure.

One thing I love about mindfulness is that it doesn't require any special training or skills. Anyone can learn to meditate. All it takes is setting aside a few minutes each day to sit quietly and focus on our breath.

This experience has taught me that sometimes we need to take a step back and look at ourselves from a different perspective. By practicing mindfulness, I've gained a newfound appreciation for the simple joys of living. Whether it's sitting down to eat dinner with loved ones, taking a walk outside, or reading a book, these activities don't come without effort, but they bring us closer to who we truly are.

In conclusion, I highly recommend giving mindfulness meditation a try. Even if you're not interested in spending hours sitting cross-legged on a mat, it's easy enough to incorporate into your daily routine. Plus, research shows that regular meditation leads to significant improvements in mood, anxiety, and overall wellbeing. So why not give it a shot? You might just discover a new sense of peace inside yourself.

Text: I went to see a therapist last night. She said she wants to work on helping me understand why I feel like I can never catch up to her in life.

I felt embarrassed by what she said, knowing that she has no idea who I really am. It makes me wonder if anyone does. Maybe she just needs someone to talk to about their insecurities too. Or maybe she thinks she knows everything about me already.

The next few days, I spent every free moment thinking about how different our lives could be if only we could communicate without barriers. If only I could truly love myself unconditionally. But deep down, I knew I wasn’t ready to give up on finding true happiness yet. So instead, I started practicing self-love, and slowly but surely things began to shift.

It wasn’t easy. There were moments where I questioned whether I was even worthy of loving myself anymore. But over time, I realized that true love isn’t about winning approval from others; it’s about giving yourself permission to be your own person. And that’s exactly what I’ve done.

Now, whenever I’m feeling lost or unsure, I remember these words. They remind me that I am capable of achieving anything I set my mind to. That I’m deserving of happiness, regardless of what others may think. And most importantly, that I will always hold onto them tightly, no matter what challenges come my way.

Text: Today I went for a walk outside with my dog. As soon as I started walking, she ran ahead and didn't come back. I thought maybe she fell or lost her way somewhere. So I followed her trail until I saw her lying on the ground. It turns out she had broken her leg and needed surgery. Her owner came over to see what was happening and we both cried together. We took her to the vet who said it was very unlikely she could recover fully from the injury. She has since recovered, but will never be able to run like she once did.

I felt terrible watching her suffer. It breaks your heart to watch animals suffer. My dog is my world and everything else just feels trivial compared to her. This experience made me realize how lucky I am to have such a loyal companion by my side.

In conclusion, losing my beloved pet is a tragedy, but it makes me appreciate life even more.

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Input: Text: obligatory comment about this not actually happening today, and this being a throwaway account.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: I recently lost a job due to the economy. I know what you're thinking - "How could he lose a job? He has a great resume." Well, it turns out I was fired because of a miscommunication between my supervisor and HR department. 

I received a letter from HR stating that I would receive severance pay based on my salary during the last six months of employment. However, when I went to pick up my checks, I found out that the total amount of my severance pay would be $800 more than my actual salary! That's a huge difference! So, I called HR again to ask why my salary wasn't listed correctly on my severance paperwork.

It turned out that the company had incorrectly calculated my annual salary for tax purposes, meaning that I wouldn't even receive a fraction of the severance payment I deserved. It's frustrating knowing that someone else benefited financially from your mistake. 

So, I filed a complaint against the company with our local labor board. They will investigate and hopefully take corrective action to prevent similar situations from occurring in the future. 

In other news, I've started a new career path. My previous position was working as a marketing manager for a small startup company. While it was challenging work, I loved every minute of it. But, I felt that it was time for a change. After many discussions with friends and coworkers, we decided to pivot towards a creative industry. We formed a business plan and began searching for funding opportunities.

We were lucky enough to secure a grant from a local government agency. With this funding, we can hire our first employee who will handle social media and public relations. This means that I won't need to worry about running errands or dealing with customer service issues anymore! 

The next step is to find investors to finance our growth. If we raise enough capital, we can expand our team and reach new markets. Our goal is to become a leader in the art world through innovative design and cutting-edge technology. 

This journey may seem daunting, but I believe that with determination and hard work, anything is possible. I hope that my story inspires others to follow their dreams no matter where they lead them.

outputs: Text: So I recently bought a brand new laptop and I wanted to install Windows 8. But I didn't know what driver to download because I don't really care about Microsoft's operating system. I thought downloading the drivers would solve everything. After installing them (I mean, who cares?), my computer started running like garbage. It took forever to boot up and then once it booted up, I realized that my computer wasn't working properly anymore. I had no internet connection and my mouse wouldn't work. Whenever I pressed any button, nothing happened. I called customer service and they told me to reinstall the OS. They said they would send someone to check it out. A few days passed and they never showed up. Finally, after several frustrating phone calls, I found out that the problem was with my motherboard. I sent it back to their store, paid for shipping and waited a month before receiving it. Meanwhile, my computer died completely. This isn't even halfway through my review yet! My only consolation is that I finally have a functioning computer again.

Text: I love to cook! One night, I decided to try making homemade chicken parmesan. I had bought some boneless skinless chicken breasts and made sure they were fresh. While I waited for them to roast, I whipped up a batch of pasta sauce using some canned tomatoes and some vegetable broth (from a leftover rotisserie chicken), and then mixed everything together.

As soon as the chicken came out of the oven, I set it aside and started working on the pasta dough. This involved mixing flour, salt, sugar, egg yolk, and water until the dough formed a ball. I kneaded it vigorously and rolled it out onto a floured surface until it was thin and pliable.

I then cut the dough into circles and placed each circle onto a preheated skillet. I sprinkled breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan cheese over the top, pressing down gently to adhere the crumbs and cheese. Cooking time varied depending on the size of your pan, but I guessed right for these small ones. After each round was done, I turned the pan upside down to remove the bottom layer of pasta, letting the excess oil drip off.

Once all the layers were removed, I spooned the melted marinara sauce over the top of the chicken, spreading it evenly with a pastry brush dipped in water. Once it reached the edges, I added sliced olives and red pepper flakes.

Bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown and heated through. Serve hot with garlic knots.

Instructions:

Ingredients:
- 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, trimmed and chopped into bite-size pieces
- 8 cups canned tomato sauce
- 1 can vegetable broth (use store-bought or homemade)
- Salt and black pepper, to taste
- Olive oil, for coating
- Garlic powder, salt, and red pepper flakes, for seasoning
- Flour, for dusting
- Pasta dough, for rolling out
- Breadcrumbs, for topping
- Grated Parmesan cheese, for serving

Cooking Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Grease a large cast iron skillet or line it with nonstick aluminum foil. Set aside.

2. In a medium bowl, combine the chicken, tomato sauce, vegetable broth, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and red pepper flakes. Mix thoroughly until the chicken is fully coated in the mixture.

3. Use a kitchen torch or grill to heat the skillet over high heat. Carefully add a few tablespoons of the chicken mixture to the center of the skillet. Using tongs, carefully transfer the skillet to the oven. Bake for 15 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 165°F.

4. Remove the skillet from the oven and allow it to cool slightly before removing the chicken and placing it onto a plate. Let it rest for 5 minutes.

5. Dust the chicken generously with flour. Shake off any excess flour. Heat a second skillet over medium heat. Add a tablespoon of olive oil and swirl to coat the pan. Place the chicken back into the skillet, flat side down. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side or until browned. Remove the chicken from the skillet and keep it warm.

6. To assemble the pasta, arrange the prepared pasta sheets on a large sheet of plastic wrap. Spread the Marinara Sauce evenly over the top of the pasta, leaving a small border along the edge. Sprinkle the breadcrumbs and Parmesan cheese over the sauce. Roll the pasta tightly towards itself. Cut into individual servings.

Serving suggestions:

Garlic Knots - Brush garlic cloves with melted butter, roll into balls and serve alongside the chicken and pasta.

Enjoy your delicious Homemade Chicken Parmesan!

Text: A couple weeks ago I decided to get a new phone, after using mine for years. I had been waiting for a few months for an iPhone, since the last one I bought wasn't good enough. So, I finally picked up the latest model and installed iOS 9. It was pretty great until the first day I tried to update it.
The process started smoothly - I clicked "Update" and waited for it to finish downloading. Then, nothing happened. After several minutes, I noticed a notification pop-up saying "Download Failed". After a few more clicks, I found that my device had crashed. At first, I thought it was because of a software bug. But then I realized that my data had also been deleted. That's right, my entire music library and photos were wiped clean. And it turns out Apple doesn't even bother backing them up. You see, Apple has no backup system built into their phones. All your files are stored locally, and there's no way to recover them if something goes wrong.
I felt terrible. Not only had I lost my precious music collection, but I'd also lost access to all my personal information. For example, my contacts list, my calendar entries, my address book... Everything. And what made things worse was that none of these issues were due to human error. outputs: Text: I’ve always been fascinated by space exploration and technology. One of my favorite things ever happened recently though – I had the chance to go to Space Camp, a summer camp for high school students offered by NASA. It was amazing. I learned about astronaut training, space shuttles, and even met real-life astronauts. Afterward, I spent four days at the Cape Canaveral Air Force Station working alongside real astronauts. I loved every minute of it. But I also remember sitting in class during our science unit on planetary motion. My teacher asked us what would happen if we ran across a moving object. Without hesitation, many of us answered “It will hit us.” This question led to a debate between the students. Some believed that if someone fell through the Earth's surface, they wouldn't get hurt because gravity would slow them down before hitting the ground. Others thought that falling through the atmosphere could cause damage. As I listened to these debates, I realized that I wasn't sure whether to believe them or not. At first, I thought that I might have missed something crucial. However, after studying further, I found that both theories were true. Whenever we fall through the Earth's atmosphere, the air molecules surrounding us become supersonic, causing a frictionless descent. Even if the speed of sound doesn't exceed the velocity of sound at sea level, the density of air at those altitudes means that the air molecules collide with each other, creating sonic booms. These sonic booms can travel hundreds of miles per hour, depending on their direction and intensity. This is why people say "I heard the sonic boom" when planes fly overhead. And when they aren't flying overhead, they create sonic booms. Now, let me ask you a few questions. If you hear a sonic boom, are you scared? No? Then why are you reading this blog? Because sometimes I feel like I don't belong anywhere. Sometimes I wonder if I'll ever fit in. Sometimes I feel like I'm not good enough. Sometimes I want to give up. But then I think about the moments where I felt like I belonged, and how much joy I received from experiencing new things. Maybe that's why I love writing. Writing allows me to express my emotions and thoughts, no matter how big or small. Whether it's a story about my experiences or just my thoughts, writing helps me process and understand different perspectives. So, maybe next time you hear a sonic boom, take a deep breath and smile. Because that's how I'd like to see you react.

outputs: Text: I woke up to the sound of my alarm clock ringing. It was already five o'clock! My mind raced as I quickly dressed myself in my pajamas and headed towards the bathroom to make sure I wouldn't miss breakfast. When I opened the door to the kitchen, my heart skipped a beat. "Oh my god!" I exclaimed loudly. This was the first time I had ever seen someone else eat breakfast before me. They were sitting across from me at their desks. Their faces were hidden behind masks, and I could barely even see them. Suddenly, I realized why I hadn't seen anyone eat breakfast yet - because none of us had ever seen each other before. Weird, right? After what felt like forever, the bell rang to signal the beginning of our third period English lesson. As soon as we entered the room, I turned around to face my new friend. He looked very familiar, but I couldn't place where I had seen him before. He was tall, broad-shouldered, and wore glasses. His name tag read "Alex." "Hey," Alex said cheerfully. "Good morning," I replied nervously. Alex smiled warmly. "I heard your name is Sarah." I nodded, grateful for the distraction. "So, you guys haven't met?" Alex asked. "No," I admitted sheepishly. But then, something clicked inside me. "Uh...I've been watching you guys eat breakfast," I blurted out. "Really?" Alex asked surprised. "Yeah, I mean, come on. You're all eating food together, right?" "Well, yeah," I admitted. "But..." "Because," Alex continued, "you don't know any of us." "What do you mean?" I asked confused. "You're all sitting here and eating breakfast, but you don't know anything about us. How can you form relationships with us?" "It's okay," Alex said calmly. "We won't judge you. And besides, maybe you'd like to learn more about us." I hesitated for a moment, unsure whether or not to accept. Then, I decided to go for it. "Okay," I finally agreed reluctantly. Over the next few days, Alex became my constant companion during breaks and after school. We talked about everything under the sun - movies, books, TV shows, politics, and sports. He showed me different parts of the city, introduced me to local restaurants, and helped me navigate through the complexities of high school life. We laughed, cried, argued, and celebrated together. Throughout these experiences, I learned more about Alex than I thought possible. There wasn't a single thing about him that I didn't love. From his kindness to his intelligence, his sense of humor to his generosity, he truly touched my heart in ways I never imagined. One afternoon, after school, we sat in front of the TV, drinking coffee, and discussing our favorite movies. At one point, Alex leaned over and whispered in my ear, "Sarah, you need to watch this movie. It's amazing." Without thinking twice, I watched "The Social Network" with him. We both fell silent, lost in the story. By the end of the night, I couldn't stop thinking about it. The next day, Alex took me to lunch. On the way, we stopped by a small bookstore and bought a copy of the novel. As we walked through the store, I found myself drawn to the bright red cover. "This looks interesting," I said excitedly. "Yes, it does," Alex confirmed. That afternoon, we spent hours discussing the characters and their motivations. We discussed the plot twists and turns, analyzed the dialogue, and marveled at the writing style. Our conversation was intense, passionate, and full of laughter. I loved every minute of it. Finally, at dinner, Alex shared a personal experience with me. He told me about his father, who passed away recently. I listened silently, tears streaming down my cheeks. Later, we hugged tightly, holding onto each other's arms. We kissed softly, feeling the cool air against our lips. For a brief moment, everything seemed perfect. Until I remembered that this was high school and nothing lasted forever. I stood up to leave, ready to return to my own world. But Alex reached out and held my hand firmly. "Don't worry, Sarah. We'll always be friends." With those words, we parted ways, leaving the restaurant with smiles on our faces. Looking back, I realize that meeting Alex changed my life in ways I never could have anticipated. He taught me the value of open communication, friendship, and empathy. He showed me that sometimes the most meaningful connections are formed through unexpected encounters. I will cherish the memories we created together, knowing that we will continue to grow and evolve as individuals and as a group.

Text: I woke up early today to go see a movie with my boyfriend. We watched a comedy called "The Hangover Part III". It wasn't anything special, just a funny movie. However, during the end credits, I noticed a commercial for a new fast-food restaurant that opened yesterday near where we live. This made us both curious enough to stop by. So, after getting a free burger, we decided to get a drink and watch the trailer again.
As soon as we walked inside, the line started growing longer and longer. Apparently, the restaurant has been open only for four days, and already has hundreds of customers waiting outside.

My heart raced as I realized the magnitude of the crowd. But then, the manager appeared before us, introducing himself. He said that they had sold out within half an hour of opening!

We looked at each other in disbelief. Our hearts sank as we realized that we might never get to eat our burgers without paying $24 per person.

I could feel tears forming in my eyes. My boyfriend turned to me, "What can we do?"

"We don't know," I replied honestly.

Without thinking, I reached out to buy tickets online through their website. As soon as the transaction was completed, I ran over to the register to purchase our burgers.

A few moments passed, and the manager approached us once more. This time, he introduced himself as the owner. He explained that he had been struggling financially due to the high demand and low profits. He also revealed that the owners would need to sell shares to keep the business afloat.

At this moment, my boyfriend and I shared a look. We didn't want to lose our chance to enjoy our favorite burgers. We offered to pay whatever amount needed to make things right.

To our surprise, the man accepted our offer, even though he had initially declined. We exchanged numbers, hoping to continue our conversation regarding future investments.

Overall, this experience taught me a valuable lesson - sometimes the most unexpected opportunities can lead to unexpected solutions. And it doesn't always mean you win. Sometimes, it means giving up your dreams to support those who need it the most.

outputs: Text: So yesterday I found out that I had been living in denial for over a decade. For most of that time, I had been hiding my mental illness because I was afraid of what others would think of me. My anxiety has always been manageable (as long as I kept busy), but I finally reached a breaking point where I could no longer hide anymore. It started small; I began taking medication more regularly than usual, and I started therapy sessions once a week instead of twice. However, as soon as I stopped hiding everything, things became really difficult. I lost jobs, relationships, and basically everything I held dear due to the fact that I felt like I wasn't good enough. One thing led to another and suddenly I was homeless, jobless, and living in a hostel for four months straight. But then I met someone who listened to me without judgment and accepted me for who I truly am. They saw my struggles and helped me through them. Now I feel free again. I don't know what will happen tomorrow, but I'm ready for whatever comes. I'll face every challenge with courage and determination.

outputs: Text: So last weekend I decided to finally try and make homemade sushi. It wasn’t too bad, although it took quite a bit longer than expected (I was planning on making 24 rolls, instead I only made 8). Afterwards I decided to head over to a local brewery where they offered to provide us with food and drink specials. As soon as I walked inside, I felt like a kid in a candy store. There was a massive selection of craft beers available, including their signature “Golden Monkey” – a hoppy IPA that left me wanting more. And then came the food. First up was a sampler platter consisting of three different types of cheese, four kinds of meatballs, a pile of vegetables, pickles, and crackers. Then followed a variety of freshly grilled seafood dishes such as salmon skewers, tuna tartare, and shrimp tempura. All of these items were cooked perfectly and served piping hot. For dessert, we were treated to a decadent chocolate lava cake. But even though it was a great time, I didn’t feel satisfied. What really sticks out to me about our experience was the atmosphere. This place was packed full of people enjoying themselves, and despite the fact that it seemed like every table had been taken, the servers were never too busy to chat with each other and ask questions about what else was happening. Overall, it was a fantastic evening spent with good company and amazing food.

I went to buy some groceries, and decided to use the restroom at Walmart. As soon as I walked into the bathroom, I heard someone walking towards me. At first, I assumed it was my ex-girlfriend. But nope, turns out it was a guy. He had his hands down the front of his pants and he started fumbling around inside himself. His erection was visible, and I couldn't help but laugh. Then he stopped and turned around, revealing a pair of dickpads.

Suddenly, the whole side of my car was covered in red and blue lights. When I checked the rearview mirror again, everything was still fine.

And every time anyone asks me about it, I can tell them exactly what happened.

So, after walking back home, I went to buy groceries and ended up taking the subway downtown to grab lunch at a restaurant nearby. It wasn't very exciting, but it got me moving again and made me feel better mentally. Of course, once I arrived back home, I started working on this article, feeling pretty good about myself. When I finished, I walked into my living room, sat down, and decided to watch a few episodes of The Office before bed. His name was David. He was a tall, thin guy who wore glasses and a suit jacket. We talked for a bit, exchanging pleasantries and discussing our lives outside of work. Then, David asked me what my favorite part of being an editorial assistant was. At first, I felt nervous, thinking that maybe he was interested in my job, but his question gave me the confidence I needed to tell him the truth. My answer surprised him. Afterwards, we chatted some more, and I learned that David was originally from Canada, but had moved to New York City to pursue his career. the first thing that comes to mind whenever I hear jokes is laughter. Laughter has always brought me joy since childhood. I remember hearing stories from my grandfather about his family's experiences growing up. One particular story he told us about his uncle who would make funny jokes, even though he couldn't speak English fluently. He used simple words to express complex ideas. As soon as I heard these stories, I knew I wanted to do the same.

A company called Chocolate Chip Cookie Bark is coming out next month. It contains 16 oz of cookie dough, 8oz of dark chocolate chips, and enough sprinkles to cover a basketball court. All you need to do is place the baking sheet in the freezer until frozen solid. Then cut into squares and enjoy.

The only downside is that these cookies will probably taste better after being refrigerated, which means you may never get any more.

This sounds perfect for a cozy night in. Who doesn't love watching TV with a bowl of warm chocolate chip cookies? Plus, who needs to spend hours cooking dinner when you can eat it in minutes?

Sounds good, right? Well, not really. These cookies aren't healthy. They contain sugar, milk powder, and corn syrup solids. You know what else isn't healthy? Eating raw chocolate chip cookies straight from the bag. So why not just stick to traditional chocolate chip cookies?

And besides, what kind of person wants to watch TV while munching on cookies? That's like having a glass of wine while trying to clean the bathroom. No thanks.

So here's a suggestion: If you absolutely must indulge in something sweet, why not try making homemade brownies instead? Not only are they much healthier, but they also taste amazing. Just be careful not to burn yourself on the hot pan.

If you still think this is too complicated, you might consider making pumpkin spice bars instead. They're easy to make, even easier to eat, and most importantly, they won't mess up your hair.

Ultimately, it comes down to personal preference. For me, the benefits of these cookies far outweigh their drawbacks. However, if you've got kids, maybe you shouldn't buy them.

As I approached my driveway, I noticed them looking at something behind the fence where they were hiding. They then ran towards their truck and disappeared inside. After several attempts to get their attention, including a few verbal threats, I decided to try using my car's horn to get their attention. He told me he knew I had taken his property, but refused to give him any details. We exchanged numbers and parted ways without incident. This experience taught me never to trust strangers in public places, especially ones with masks. Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: I don’t know what happened to him, but he disappeared yesterday afternoon without leaving behind his phone, money, keys, passport, or even a single piece of paper. His family searched high and low for hours, but they were unsuccessful until we discovered him dead underneath our house. We called the police, who arrived shortly afterwards and pronounced him dead at the scene. No signs of struggle, no apparent cause of death. We couldn’t find a clue. It seemed like he had vanished forever.

I remember walking down the street with him, feeling safe in each other’s arms. He whispered something to me that made me feel loved and understood, and then suddenly, we both felt the ground give way beneath us. I heard a loud crack and the sound of metal hitting concrete. My heart stopped.

My body shook violently, my eyes widened, and tears streamed down my cheeks. What had happened? Where am I now? How can this be happening to me?

The officers questioned us, trying to figure out where he might have gone missing to. They told us that he may have been taken somewhere else, but we never found him again. We were told to leave town immediately.

We tried to cope with the loss of our beloved friend, but it was impossible. We mourned him deeply, and although we missed him terribly, we knew that he was happy in heaven, surrounded by friends and family.

As time passed, we slowly came back to ourselves. But the memories stayed with us, haunting us every night, making us wonder what might have happened.

It took years for us to come to terms with his disappearance. Every time we went outside, we noticed strange lights in the sky above us. We began to notice birds flying around in circles, and we soon learned that it was a sign of his presence, guiding us towards finding him once again.

Years later, we received a letter from someone claiming to be him. It read: “I’ve been searching for you guys for a while now. You’re the only ones who seem to understand me.” And we knew then that we had found our brother.

Now, whenever we hear the same bird circling overhead, we smile and think of him. Sometimes we see people staring at us strangely, wondering if we too are lost souls wandering aimlessly.

But we know that we’ll always have each other. Our love will continue to grow stronger because of him.

So, if you ever need someone to talk to, to vent your frustrations, to cry your sorrows, to laugh with, to love you, reach out to us. We’ll listen and offer support, no matter what kind of pain you’re going through.

Rest in peace, dear brother. Until we meet again.

Text: I've been trying to get into better shape since starting college last year. My friends joke that I have no endurance whatsoever - even walking around campus feels exhausting. But lately, I've been working harder than ever to improve my fitness routine. One weekend, while practicing yoga at home, I accidentally spilled water all over my sweaty mat. What followed next was a humiliation I never expected.

I was sitting cross-legged on my bed, legs crossed under me, feeling relaxed after a full night's sleep. Suddenly, my phone rang. It was my mom. She told me that she needed help with my laundry. At first, I tried to ignore the call; I wasn't feeling well enough to take care of such chores. However, my mother persisted until she convinced me to come downstairs immediately. When I arrived, she handed me a dirty white sheet and instructed me to fold it neatly. After completing the task, she thanked me profusely and left. As soon as I picked up the sheet, however, I realized that it was wet from my previous bathroom session. How could I possibly manage such tasks now?

Without thinking twice, I grabbed the wet sheet and began to dry it using only my hands. As I lifted the damp fabric, I noticed that my skin felt irritated and prickly. Before realizing what happened, I reached for a nearby towel, hoping to cover up the embarrassment. To my horror, however, the towel absorbed every drop of moisture on my body, leaving behind an unpleasant residue. This experience made me realize how difficult it would be to perform basic activities such as dressing and grooming without proper hygiene. I couldn't imagine living like this forever.

After several weeks of struggling, I decided to seek medical attention. A doctor examined me and informed me that I had athlete's foot. Despite my reluctance, I agreed to treatments, including creams and pills, to prevent further damage. The treatment plan required frequent changes of clothes, which became an inconvenience for me. Moreover, the constant cleaning and disinfecting of clothing resulted in a significant increase in expenses. These costs forced me to reduce my daily activities and limit my social life. It took months for me to regain my confidence, but eventually, I learned to live with my new reality.

In conclusion, I've learned valuable lessons throughout these experiences. Firstly, being self-conscious is natural, especially when someone else sees our flaws. Secondly, taking responsibility for one's actions has helped me grow as a person. Thirdly, learning to adapt and overcome challenges can lead to personal growth and development. Lastly, always seeking professional assistance may not solve problems entirely, but it will certainly provide relief and support.

Output: i found a quarter on a display of gum, cashier thought i was blatantly stealing gum right in front of her.

outputs: Text: "The Great Wall of China has been built by people who hate each other," wrote author David Maraniss in his recent book, "The Great Happiness Project." The phrase comes from the novelist's own experience researching the project. He writes that he spent months interviewing people living near the wall, then began working on the book, "Still Life With Bread Crumb Trail," after his wife left him. His journey eventually led him across China, where he met some of its most prominent citizens. He describes himself as a “poor man’s tour guide,” someone whose purpose is simply to show people around. But while the book is ostensibly about China, its title also reflects Maraniss’s interest in happiness. And, yes, the Great Wall itself plays a significant role in both books. It’s a symbolic landmark that looms large in Chinese culture, representing national unity, martial prowess, and endurance. As Maraniss explains in his book, many of the people he interviews describe their lives as happy ones—though not necessarily easy ones. Many live in poverty; many struggle against oppression. Still, despite these obstacles, they remain content. “It doesn’t matter whether I find a good job or not, whether I get rich or stay poor,” says one farmer in Shandong province. Another person who has never owned a house tells Maraniss that he would rather die than leave his family behind. The author notes that he learned something profound about life through talking to these people. They teach us about courage, patience, resilience, forgiveness, joy, hope, and love. The Great Wall, however, remains central to their stories. Its beauty can bring tears to their eyes, yet also inspire them to continue walking. Text: I can't believe what I just read...

I am a professional writer/editor living in NYC. My favorite thing to do is write articles, blog posts, essays, and books. But I recently stumbled upon something that has made me realize how much more important writing is than ever.

The reason why I feel so strongly about this topic is because I work with some amazingly talented people every single day - writers, editors, designers, and marketing professionals. And yet, despite their impressive skills, many of us spend our days feeling like failures. We hear stories of authors being rejected countless times, editors making silly mistakes, and designers failing miserably at their jobs. It seems that no matter where we look, everyone is struggling with the same problem – they simply don’t know how to make their ideas come alive on paper.

But wait, you might be thinking. Don’t these people just sit around in their cubicles, waiting for inspiration to strike? Wrong. These professionals are constantly working hard to improve themselves and stay ahead of the curve. They attend conferences, take classes, participate in online communities, and learn new techniques through reading and watching others. This isn’t easy, though. Most of us need help along the way. We want to create great content, but we often struggle with getting started, finding the right words, or creating a cohesive narrative. Sometimes, it feels like nothing will ever change. That’s why I wanted to share some tips that have helped me overcome similar obstacles. Here are three simple steps that have transformed my writing process:

1. Write regularly: Everyone knows that creativity comes from doing, not thinking. However, sometimes the best ideas come from taking action. Whenever possible, set aside time each week to write. Even if it’s only five minutes, the act of typing out thoughts on paper can provide immense benefits. For example, I used to procrastinate by trying to think too deeply about my project before starting. Now, whenever I find myself stuck, I start by jotting down a list of bullet points on the page. Text: I can't believe how much time I spend waiting in line for something that takes only five seconds to complete. It's like I just want to sit and wait instead of doing something productive.

This experience has taught me not to judge people too harshly based on their first impression. People often underestimate themselves and overestimate others, especially those with bad experiences. It's easy to see things through rose-colored glasses, and I'd never recommend blind faith, but sometimes we need to let our guard down and embrace change. Sometimes, all it takes is a little patience and persistence.

Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Text: I just got laid off from my job after 8 years. It feels like such a waste. I feel lost without a sense of purpose, especially since I spent most of my time working towards becoming a nurse. But instead of dwelling on it, I'm starting to see the silver lining - I can finally pursue my dream of becoming a writer.

I took a break from my career to focus on writing, and now I have a beautiful piece of paper to prove it. It means everything to me that I made the right decision by stepping away from a paycheck to follow my passion.

This is the first step in making a living through my craft. Now I'm ready to write stories, poems, essays, and anything else that comes to mind. And I hope you enjoy reading them as much as I enjoyed creating them.

Writing has always been a part of who I am, even before I became a nurse. Writing allowed me to express myself in ways no one could understand. My heart aches every time I think about how many talented writers are stuck behind locked doors, never able to reach their potential due to lack of resources. This is why I decided to make a change.

It's time for us to take our voices seriously. Time for us to fight for equal opportunities. We owe it to ourselves and those who come after us. We owe it to our fellow creatives. We owe it to our community.

So here I sit, surrounded by books, pens, and piles of papers. I have nothing left to lose, except my fear of failure. I will continue to pour my heart and soul into my art, knowing that I'm doing what makes me happy. And someday, maybe, I'll discover that happiness is worth fighting for.

Until then, I'll keep striving for success. Even when it seems impossible. Because I refuse to let anyone dictate whether or not I can achieve my goals. No matter what happens, I'll keep moving forward, determined to become the best version of myself.

Thank you for taking the time to read this letter. I hope you'll join me on this journey. Together, we can create a world where artists thrive and talent isn't limited by financial constraints.

outputs: Text: I recently discovered that I can no longer watch Netflix without crying every time someone dies. It started with the finale of Stranger Things, and now I'm watching season 4 of Lovecraft Country. And I just realized that I love those shows too. So far, season 4 has dealt with issues like race relations, mental health, and the legacy of colonialism. But what really struck me was the way in which these themes were intertwined with the supernatural elements. There's this scene near the end of the episode where Atticus (Matthew McConaughey) goes hunting with Jesse (Jaboukie Young-White), who has lost his wife to cancer. As he stalks through the woods, he comes across a group of Native Americans, who seem to be using a type of energy that seems to correspond with the sound of a drum. This leads Atticus to believe that the spirits of the dead are communicating with the living, and perhaps even seeking revenge against white settlers who killed their ancestors. Meanwhile, Atticus' own daughter is dealing with her own trauma - she witnessed her father kill a black man in self defense when she was very young. These different threads come together in the final moments of the show, when Jesse confronts Atticus over his beliefs. He asks him why he thinks the world is so evil, and why he feels like he needs to protect himself by killing anyone who crosses him. Atticus responds by saying that sometimes it takes losing everything to truly understand what's important. That's such a beautifully simple statement, and yet it's profoundly true. The more I think about it, the more it resonates with me personally. In the context of our current political climate, I feel like it speaks directly to the ways in which people are often left to grapple with grief alone, rather than finding community in shared experiences.
