outputs: Text: I recently took a trip to see my grandparents who live in Florida. My mom picked me up in New York City and drove us through Long Island and into South Carolina until we reached their house. When we arrived, I went straight inside to grab my stuff and headed outside to take pictures of the scenery. That's when I realized that my camera had run out of battery power. Now what do you think I was supposed to do?? Well, I could either just walk back to the car and hope someone else noticed that my camera ran out of juice, or I could risk walking across a swampy field to reach our destination. So, I walked across the swampy field. It wasn't too bad - I made it halfway across without falling over or tripping on a sturdy root, but then I heard a loud growl coming from behind me. I turned around to see a huge python slithering towards me. At first, I thought it was some kind of exotic pet, but nope, it was real. As soon as I saw its eyes, I started running like hell. But I didn't make it very far before I came upon a road that led right past the swamp. I hesitated for only a moment before taking a chance and driving onto the road. I hit the brakes, thinking that maybe the car wouldn't hurt anything. To my surprise, it did, and I quickly realized that I needed to get out of there ASAP. After managing to free myself from the snakes and crawling under a nearby tree, I finally got out of there safely. What I learned from this experience is that sometimes the safest option isn't always the most obvious choice.

The buildings loomed closer together than they usually do, and there was a strange sense of unease that settled into my stomach like a heavy weight. I kept walking, ignoring the feeling, until I reached the top of the hill. There, standing above me, was a giant, black object that glinted in the moonlight. At first, I thought it was some kind of spacecraft, but after a moment's pause, I realized what it was - a massive, shadowy figure. My heart pounded against my chest, and my breath caught in my throat as I stood frozen in terror. But then, without warning, something shifted inside me. A primal urge surged within me, like a fire burning deep within my soul. And suddenly, I knew exactly what to do. I ran. As fast as my legs could carry me, I raced towards the nearest building. I slammed open the door, threw myself inside, and closed it behind me. But even as I ran, I couldn't shake the feeling that someone was watching me. Everywhere I turned, I felt eyes on me, searching for any sign of danger. Finally, I heard footsteps approaching. They came closer, until I was almost face to face with a group of men dressed in dark suits and masks. They spoke in low voices, their faces hidden beneath hoods, and I knew immediately that they weren't human. I tried to run again, but they followed me, shouting and gesturing wildly. Suddenly, one of them lunged forward, grabbing me by the arm. I struggled free, kicking and screaming, only to see him disappear into thin air. Panic took hold of me once again, and I broke down completely. I collapsed onto the ground, crying and trembling uncontrollably. After what felt like hours, I slowly regained consciousness. When I opened my eyes, I saw that I was lying on a bed, surrounded by people who appeared to be medical professionals. I sat up quickly, dazed, and looked around. It was clear that I had no idea how I got here, but I hoped that the others would tell me what had happened. As I began to speak, however, I noticed that everyone was staring at me, their expressions blank. I tried to explain what had happened, but no one seemed interested. Eventually, they asked me to sit quietly while they conducted tests on me. During the process, I learned that I had survived a catastrophic event, one that nobody else had ever experienced. It was then that I understood why the men had attacked me. They had come to collect a payment, and they were willing to kill anyone who refused to hand over their wealth. For weeks, I lived in fear, never knowing whether I would make it out alive. But eventually, I discovered a way to escape. With help from some unlikely allies, I managed to evade the men and flee back to civilization. As I walked away from the hospital, I knew that I wouldn't be returning there anytime soon. The memory of that night will always stay with me, a reminder that sometimes, life can throw us curveballs that seem impossible to overcome.

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.

I woke up early this morning, feeling tired and disorientated. My alarm clock went off at 6am sharp, but I couldn't seem to make any sense of the time. I looked at the clock again, hoping to find some clue, but nothing seemed familiar. A few seconds passed, and I realized that I had left my keys behind somewhere in my room. Panic set in. What could I do without them?

Suddenly, I heard a faint noise coming from outside. Curiosity got the best of me, and I pushed open the door. To my amazement, I saw my friends standing there - Jake, Sarah, Mike, and Emily. They all looked worried and excited.

"We can't leave yet," Sarah said. "There's something important we need to do first."

Jake nodded. "Yeah, we need to figure out how to cross the country without using public transportation. There aren't many places to stop along the way."

Mike raised his eyebrows. "And how exactly do you plan to do that?" he asked.

Emily grinned. "Well, we're planning to drive our cars!" she exclaimed.

The rest of us exchanged looks. We knew each other too well. But then, we started laughing. And soon, everyone else joined in. Our laughter echoed through the house, filling the empty rooms with sound.

As the sun began to rise higher over the horizon, we packed our bags and headed towards the nearest gas station. As we pulled onto the highway, we realized that we weren't alone anymore. We had company. A truck stopped beside us, its driver, a middle-aged man named Derek, eagerly offering to help us carry our luggage. He introduced himself and gave us directions to a nearby campground.

During the next couple of days, we drove further west, stopping every once in a while to stretch our legs and explore small towns along the way. Each town was different; some were quaint, others bustling with activity. Some were beautiful, with rolling hills covered in greenery. Others were depressingly rundown, with dilapidated buildings and boarded-up windows.

At night, we settled down at campsites, pitching our tents and sharing stories under the stars. Sometimes, we slept in, sometimes we stayed up late talking until dawn. No matter where we ended up, we always felt grateful to be together.

On our final day, we planned to visit a national park called Yellowstone. We were excited and nervous about it all. When we arrived, the weather was unpredictable - raining heavily most of the afternoon, then clearing up in the evening. Despite the rain, we still managed to enjoy ourselves. We hiked along the river, watching geysers erupt from the ground. We watched the sunset over the waterfalls, casting shadows on the rocks below.

When we finally reached the entrance to the park, we were greeted by hundreds of other tourists. We quickly took refuge in a nearby restaurant, where we spent the entire evening catching up on news and sharing stories. By the end of the night, we knew we wouldn't forget this experience forever.

As we prepared to leave, we promised to come back sometime and retrace our steps. We smiled at each other, knowing that even though we had crossed state lines, we had formed lifelong friendships.

It wasn't easy, crossing the country by car. But in the end, it was worth it. We laughed, we cried, we shared memories that will last a lifetime. Most importantly, we came together as a team, learning valuable lessons about friendship, resilience, and adventure.

Text: the most important lesson I learned after college was how not to use email. It took me years to realize this fact.

I got fired for using email inappropriately when I was working at XYZ company. I tried explaining myself to my boss, but she wasn't buying it. She told me to either stop sending emails or resign immediately. This is why I never use email again.

The moral of the story is simple: Never send an email unless absolutely necessary. You can save yourself a lot of trouble and embarrassment by avoiding the temptation altogether.

Cut to the end of the conversation with my former coworker.

She looks at me skeptically. "What kind of advice is that? Why would you even bother telling someone else what to do?"

I shrug, knowing that I'd rather listen to her opinion than anyone else's.

After some hesitation, she agrees to give me a piece of paper and pen. We sit across from each other, staring at our screens, waiting for something interesting to happen.

Suddenly, a message pops up on my screen. "Hey man, thanks for being here. Do you remember those times when you used email instead of talking to people directly?"

My heart starts racing. My mind races too. What does she mean? Was I really caught doing that?

I take a deep breath and start writing back.

"No, I didn't," I say, feeling my hands tremble. "But yeah, sometimes you can skip right over direct communication and still accomplish things."

Her expression softens slightly. "Okay, fine. But you better make sure you only use email when it's absolutely necessary."

It's hard to hear her words, but I nod my head silently, understanding completely. Afterwards, we exchange numbers and promise to stay in touch.

For a few weeks, I stick strictly to the letter of the law. I delete all my old emails, and only use messaging apps whenever possible. Whenever I feel the urge to communicate, I think back to that conversation and remind myself of the importance of proper etiquette.

In the end, it's worth it. I saved myself countless hours of frustration and stress, and I gained valuable experience learning to appreciate the power of personal connections.

outputs: Text: I was walking home from the store with my wallet, phone, keys, etc., and I suddenly felt something hit me on the head. When I turned around, I saw someone running towards me with a knife. They jumped over the fence and ran away. As soon as they disappeared behind the trees, I realized that I was holding onto my wallet. It wasn't too heavy, but I didn't feel very safe carrying it. After realizing how lucky I was to not have been hurt, I started to walk faster than normal. Suddenly, I heard footsteps approaching fast. At that moment, I knew who it was. I tried to run, but I couldn't move properly without falling. My heart was racing, and sweat was pouring down my forehead. Finally, after what seemed like forever, the person stopped right beside me. He looked like he belonged to a gang. His name was Jake. We talked for a while until he told me his story. He said that he lived near here and had been involved in a drug deal gone wrong. He explained that everyone in his group died except him. That was the only reason why he came across me. Now, I was really scared, but I decided to help him. First, I helped him unlock the gate to let us through. Then, I took him to a nearby park where he could sit down and relax for a bit. From there, I followed him to his house, hoping that he wouldn't tell anyone about our conversation. But, as soon as I entered the front yard, I noticed that there was no sign of life inside. Just a few trash cans scattered throughout the yard. There was nothing else. I waited outside for several hours, hoping that maybe he would come back. Eventually, he did. He apologized profusely for everything that had happened. I listened carefully to what he had to say. He revealed that he was homeless and that he needed money to pay for medical expenses. I offered him whatever little I had, including food and clothes. He thanked me profusely and left. Later that evening, I met up with some friends at a nearby bar. While drinking, we discussed the incident that occurred earlier. Someone suggested that I contact the police since I witnessed something suspicious happening. However, I hesitated for a moment. What if they think I'm involved in the murder? And what if I end up being blamed for the crime? I decided to stay quiet, knowing that it may put people's lives in danger. Afterward, I went back to my own house, feeling much lighter. For the first time in weeks, I slept soundly, without any worries.

Text: I went camping last summer with some friends. We had no electricity or plumbing, just tents and cooking utensils. There wasn’t much food around either, but we managed to make a nice stew using wild berries and mushrooms.

We set up our tent by the river and spent most of the night chatting and telling stories. It felt like such a simple life - nothing too fancy or luxurious, just enjoying each other and nature.

The next morning, we woke up early and packed everything into our car, heading out to explore the nearby trails. As we drove, I realized how lucky I was to have made these memories with these amazing people.

It hit us both hard that we wouldn’t see them again soon. That feeling of being alone and disconnected from everyone else, even after only a few days together, was overwhelming. But I knew that this experience would forever change us.

By the end of the trip, we were all a little sad to leave, but grateful for what we had shared.

As we headed home, I couldn’t help but think about how blessed we were to have experienced this moment. How many opportunities we would miss out on if we never took risks and tried new things.

I decided to take a leap of faith and quit my job to pursue writing. And while the first year has been challenging, I am learning so much and loving every minute of it.

Because sometimes, the best experiences happen outside of your comfort zone.

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: I am very excited to announce that I will be performing live at the world famous Odd Mom Out festival on June 3rd!! This show will feature some of your favorite comics including myself and several others who you may recognize. If you love standup comedy, you won’t want to miss this event!!!

The excitement has set in, I can feel my palms sweating. My heart races like I’m running a marathon, yet again. As soon as I finish speaking, I start preparing my material. But what happens next leaves me stunned. A woman walks up to me and asks “Can I ask you something?” I freeze for a moment, unsure whether she wants to talk to me. She speaks in a soft voice, “I heard you perform at our last event and loved your act.” Her eyes meet mine, and her smile spreads wide. “Wow,” she says, “you really impressed me!” My heart swells with pride as I thank her for her kind words. We exchange numbers and plans to catch up later.

After the show, the audience starts clapping and cheering. I turn around to take a bow, and suddenly I hear someone shout “Hey man, you did a good job!” To which I reply “Thank you” with a grin. Another person approaches me, holding a poster in their hand. They introduce themselves and tell me they attended the show and enjoyed my performance. Their name tag reads “Mark”. After exchanging numbers, Mark invites me to his table at the festival, where he tells me he’d like to meet up afterwards. I agree and head backstage to freshen up. When I walk by him, he smiles and waves. He’s wearing a button-down shirt, jeans, and loafers. He looks exactly like the photos on his website.

As we sit together, we talk about everything under the sun – politics, movies, books, etc. His name tag says “Bradley”, and I immediately notice his piercing blue eyes and dark curly hair. Bradley introduces himself as a producer and talent manager for the festival. He offers me a ride to my hotel, and as we drive, he shares stories about his experiences working with many successful comics, such as David Cross and Dave Attell. Bradley also tells me about his own journey in the industry, starting out doing standup and moving onto producing shows. It turns out that Bradley used to manage a few of my old friends, and I’ve known them for years. Together, we plan our night at the festival, which includes a meet and greet with Bradley.

On the way to the festival, Bradley mentions that he recently finished recording a podcast called “Stand Up and Stories” with a few of his friends. It sounds interesting, so I download the first episode and listen while driving. At one point, I glance at my phone to check the time and realize I’m late for my meeting. Panic sets in, but then I remember Bradley’s offer. He hands me a business card with a contact number and message to stay in touch.

Finally arriving at the festival, Bradley greets us both and leads us to a spot in front of the stage. The festival staff organizes the crowd and welcomes everyone with open arms. Bradley takes charge and directs the proceedings. We watch as various comics take the stage and engage with the audience. One particular comic, named Emily, stands out to me. She has a unique style that combines physical comedy and storytelling. I’m struck by her ability to connect with people and make them laugh.

When it’s my turn, Bradley takes the mic and introduces me. I share my background, my comedy, and explain how much I appreciate having met him. I receive a standing ovation, and as I exit the stage, I’m surrounded by hugs and high-fives. Bradley even offers to take pictures with me and give me his autograph. Before I leave, he gives me his business card once again, saying he’ll reach out to me soon.

Overall, the experience was nothing short of magical. Seeing so many talented comics sharing their passion and craft with each other was inspiring. However, the most significant part of the evening came afterward. Bradley reached out to me shortly after the show, offering to produce my first standup special. I couldn’t believe it; it felt like fate. And now, thanks to his connections and generosity, I have a chance to bring my unique perspective to audiences everywhere. Thank you, Bradley, for making my dream come true.

Text: You know how I love to travel, right? Well, after seeing pictures of these amazing islands, I knew I had to visit them. And I did! These photos will always hold a special place in my heart.
This trip has taken me through several countries and cultures, but I think this island has stolen my heart the most. It’s called the Galapagos Islands, and they are located east of Ecuador. They’re home to many unique species of animals and plants, including giant tortoises, marine iguanas, and Darwin finches. There are even some sea lions and penguins around!

I spent five days exploring the different islands, hiking through trails, swimming in crystal clear waters, snorkeling, and even doing some kite surfing. Here are some of my favorite photos from each island.
The first island we visited was Isabella Island. We took a boat ride to the mainland, where we could explore the island. This photo shows us standing near a beautiful waterfall. It was incredibly refreshing and serene. We also walked along a trail that led to a viewpoint overlooking the ocean.

On the second island, Santa Cruz Island, we visited a colony of marine turtles. These guys were very curious and came out to check us out. We watched them lay eggs and nursed their young. It was such a peaceful experience. We also enjoyed walking along the beach, watching seals play in the waves.

We ended our journey on Fernandina Island, where we met some adorable baby sea lions. They were super friendly and let us pet them. We also climbed to the top of a volcano, where we were able to see breathtaking views.

One of the highlights of my trip was meeting Charles Darwin himself while we were researching his life and work. He lived here for years and wrote many important books about evolution. His former home, the Mansion House, still stands and offers guided tours. We learned so much about him and his ideas while learning about the history of the islands.

In conclusion, the Galapagos Islands have left a lasting impression on me. Each island has its own beauty and charm, and I am grateful for having experienced them. What made your visit to the Galapagos Islands unforgettable?

The driver seemed to be okay, but his vehicle looked like it was totaled. After a few moments of shock, I began to realize that this was something far worse than just a minor accident. There was blood everywhere, and it seemed like someone had died inside. We ran outside to check for any survivors. Thankfully, none were found. A woman lay sprawled across the hood of her car, clutching her chest in pain. Her husband sat next to her, holding her hand. They both looked pale and distraught. One of the paramedics approached us, and we exchanged a nervous glance. She spoke softly, asking if we knew each other. I shook my head, feeling dizzy and disoriented. She asked if we needed medical assistance, and I nodded frantically. We were taken to the hospital, where we waited anxiously for news. By the time we received word that the man had passed away, we were already in tears. His wife and children were devastated. I couldn't believe how traumatic it was for them. When I returned home, I collapsed on the couch, unable to move. My mind raced as I tried to process everything that had happened. What kind of person drives like that? Why did nobody stop him? So I lay there thinking about how much I love sleeping in until 7, how I wish I could go back in time and tell myself to stop being such a lazy ass, how I wish I could give up sleep altogether. Suddenly, I felt a surge of energy. It wasn't an adrenaline high, exactly, since I already feel pretty good most days. But somehow, someway, I felt like I could accomplish anything I set my mind to. This idea came out of nowhere, but it stayed with me. What did I need to change about myself? How could I make a difference in the world? After a few moments of thought, I decided to start small. I knew I needed to actively seek out ways to improve my life. One day, I will become an advocate for animal rights. Another day, I will volunteer at a homeless shelter. I never lost sight of my goal, nor did I let external factors interfere with my progress. It was an amazingly empowering experience, and I learned so much from it.

Text: this morning I woke up feeling sick and disoriented. My stomach was growling, and my throat hurt. As soon as I got out of bed, I headed straight towards the kitchen. After taking some water and digging into a jar of ketchup, I noticed something odd - there was no meat in the fridge. It was empty except for canned vegetables. So I started making soup. But when I brought it over to my room, I realized that the only way to make the soup taste good was by adding spaghetti. Which meant I needed pasta. And since I didn't own any, I made myself buy some.
The next few days were rough. Every time I looked at my plate, I saw pasta. Pasta for breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks. I couldn't stop thinking about it. And then I remembered something else: the last time I bought groceries, I forgot to put everything back in the cart. By the end of the week, I was almost too embarrassed to walk through the store again. Eventually, I gave up and just ordered online. I spent the rest of the week trying to convince myself that this was okay. That maybe, just maybe, I could survive without food.
I was wrong. At least until this afternoon.
My mom called me. She said she'd seen the news report and was worried about me. She offered to pick me up at school, even though I knew I wasn't supposed to eat anymore. When I finally did eat, I felt a wave of relief wash over me. It wasn't much, but it was enough.
As I sat down to write this story, I wondered why it had taken me so long to realize that I needed food. Maybe it was because I thought I was invincible, that nothing could harm me. Or maybe it was because I was afraid of being judged. Whatever the reason, I'm glad I learned my lesson sooner rather than later. Because now I know that I am capable of surviving without food.

Text: I recently discovered the wonders of homemade chicken noodle soup. It’s incredibly easy to make, only takes 30 minutes to prepare, and it tastes SO GOOD! Plus, it’s loaded with veggies and protein. So far, I’ve made it twice already – once with leftover rotisserie chicken and again with freshly cooked chicken breasts. Both times, it turned out perfectly every time. If you want to give it a shot, here’s how to make your own chicken noodle soup from scratch:
1. Start with a pot large enough to hold all the ingredients comfortably. Cook some water in a separate pan until boiling. Add a tablespoon of olive oil to the water, then add diced carrots, celery, garlic, and onion. Sauté for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. 2. Pour the vegetable mixture into the big pot and add salt and pepper. Stir well. Now, bring the broth to a simmer over medium heat. This will help ensure the flavors meld nicely when added later. 3. Once the broth has come to a gentle simmer, add the canned chicken pieces. Stir everything around until they are coated with liquid. Cover and let sit for about 45 minutes to 1 hour, depending on how much meat you’re using. 4. While waiting, prep the rest of your ingredients. Rinse pasta under cold running water and drain thoroughly. Dice the bell peppers and zucchini. Toss them with olive oil and seasonings. Chop kale leaves finely and set aside. 5. When the chicken is done, remove it from the broth and transfer it to a plate. Let it cool slightly while you clean the pot. Using tongs, carefully remove the chicken from the broth. Shred the meat into bite-size pieces. Return the shredded chicken to the pot along with the chopped bell peppers and zucchini. 6. Pour in the remaining broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to loosen any bits stuck to the sides. Bring the broth to a rolling boil over high heat. Then reduce the heat to low and cover tightly with a lid. Simmer gently for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Check the seasoning. Adjust as necessary with additional salt, pepper, and herbs (such as thyme). You may need to add extra liquid if the broth seems too dry. Serve hot, ladling over individual bowls. Text: I love being a student at a small liberal arts school, but sometimes I feel like I'm living in a time warp. Everyone has their phones with them constantly, and even when they aren't checking their messages or social media, they seem to always be on their phones. It's hard to stay focused on studying and doing homework when every second seems to count.

Last semester, I decided to challenge myself and try something different. Instead of using my phone to study, I started carrying a notebook and pen everywhere I went. At first, it seemed impossible, but eventually, I realized that it wasn't nearly as bad as I thought it would be. Whenever I needed to focus, I simply reached into my pocket and pulled out my notebook.

This change in habits took a little adjustment at first. I still checked my email several times each day, but I stopped answering texts right away. I learned to set aside specific times for studying instead of just letting myself get distracted whenever I felt like it. And, surprisingly, it didn't affect my grades too badly. Maybe it's because I was able to avoid procrastination, but my grade point average increased by almost half.

But despite these improvements, I couldn't help feeling like I was missing out on something important. There were times when I felt like I was running on empty, and I wondered whether spending all that extra time studying was worth it. But over time, I began to see the benefits. My grades improved, and I became less stressed overall.

In fact, I found that I enjoyed studying more than ever before. I could spend whole afternoons poring over notes and diagrams, and I never missed a deadline. It gave me a sense of accomplishment that I hadn't experienced before, and it helped me develop a deeper understanding of what I was learning.

So maybe I'm not the only person who thinks that students can learn better without their phones. Maybe it's possible to balance productivity and self-discipline, even in a world that encourages constant connectivity.

Later that evening, I received a letter informing me that I owed $800 in unpaid tips. Needless to say, I was extremely upset. Overall, the experience taught me that sometimes, taking responsibility for your actions can make all the difference between being a victim and becoming a hero.

Text: I've always loved playing guitar. I remember buying my first one when I was sixteen years old and spending countless afternoons practicing scales and chords. One day, however, things took a turn for the worse.

One afternoon, I was sitting in class, humming along to "Sweet Child O Mine" when suddenly, I felt a sharp pain shoot through my neck. It wasn't anything major - nothing like a concussion or even a broken collarbone - but it definitely hurt. And then came the next wave of agony; every movement sent shooting pains through my body. My head throbbed, my arms ached, and my hands shook uncontrollably. By the end of the day, I could barely pick up a guitar again.

I was devastated. Guitar-playing had always been my passion, and now it seemed like it might forever remain just that – a passion. I spent the rest of the weekend watching videos online and practicing exercises on YouTube. But despite my efforts, my fingers continued to slip over each other, my coordination remained rusty, and my mind became foggy. Every night, I would lie awake, staring blankly at the ceiling until dawn.

It wasn't until a couple of days later, during dinner with friends, that I realized what was really bothering me. My friend had heard about my guitar troubles and suggested we play music together. At first, I hesitated, knowing full well that playing guitar required skill beyond my current level. But he persisted, reminding me that playing guitar could teach me new skills and improve my mental state. So, with a renewed sense of determination, I agreed.

And thus began my journey towards recovery. With the guidance of my friends and the encouragement of my therapist, I started taking steps towards rebuilding my guitar playing skills. Over time, I slowly built up my strength and coordination, and even found myself enjoying the practice sessions more than ever before. Before long, I was able to perform simple songs without causing pain or discomfort.

Now, whenever I hear a song that makes me feel good, whether it's a classic rock anthem or a pop ballad, I think of those early days of frustration and doubt. Even though my guitar has suffered a bit since that fateful day, it remains a constant source of joy and fulfillment in my life.

Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Input:
outputs: Text: I went camping last weekend with my friends, we hiked through beautiful scenery and even saw a bear! We also cooked over an open fire pit, and made s'mores! It was amazing! Afterward, we all took turns playing "hide-and-seek" underneath our tents. When we were done searching, I felt incredibly guilty because I left behind my trusty flashlight and headlamp. My friends laughed at me, but I thought maybe they wouldn't mind finding them for me? So, I started walking towards the tent where my stuff was, and suddenly realized that I could hear someone following me. As soon as I turned around, I saw a giant black bear coming straight toward me. At first, I panicked, thinking he would attack me. But luckily, he stopped just shy of me. And that's when I realized that he was really friendly, and he wasn't going to hurt anyone. He just needed a place to rest for the night. Since I had no flashlight or headlamp, I thankfully found a small cave nearby, and we spent the next hour sitting inside, snuggling together, and enjoying each other's company. Even though it was terrifying, I learned that sometimes the biggest threats come from nature itself. This experience taught me that sometimes the things that scare us most can lead to unexpected blessings.

Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Input: Text: tifu. i was in line at the gas station, waiting to pay for my soda and gas, when i saw a quarter on the packs of gum directly in front of the counter. when it was my turn to pay i bent over and scooped up the quarter, and put it in my pocket, forgetting about it instantly. putting my soda on the counter and reaching for my wallet, i looked up and saw the cashier eyeing me with an angry glare. i was confused by this. was she mad at my choice of soda? (she could be one of those freaks that prefer pepsi) did i have an offensive t shirt on? (not unless she's offended by my obscure podcast shirt) 

i say "......$40 on 2 please." and she responds with "what's in your pocket?" 

"huh?" i stammer before finally understanding. "oh! i didn't steal anything!" and proceed to fervently pull everything out of my pockets, dropping change, and other things. i pick up the 25 cent culprit and thrust it to the cashier, as if it proved my story somehow, and explained that i had just seen the quarter on the gum and nabbed it.

 her face hadn't changed at all during the entire exchange. she finally just completed my transaction and said have a nice day. i'm not sure if she believed me or not, but i gathered all my stuff and hightailed it out of there.
Output: i found a quarter on a display of gum, cashier thought i was blatantly stealing gum right in front of her.

Input:
outputs: Text: I walked into the grocery store yesterday morning to grab some eggs, milk, and bread. As soon as I opened the door, I noticed a $2 bill lying on the ground near the entrance. At first, I assumed it was left behind by someone who forgot to take it home with them, so I picked it up and started walking away. However, as I approached the register, I realized something wasn't quite right. There were no customers lined up in front of me. It was empty except for me and a couple of people ahead of me. My mind raced with questions - What had I done wrong to deserve such a fate? Was I even in the correct store? Had I accidentally stepped onto public property? Suddenly, a man burst through the doors behind me, holding a sign that read "Egg Scandal!" He pointed to where the egg lay on the floor and shouted, "Look what we got here! An egg scandal!" I tried to explain to him that I didn't know what he meant by "egg scandal," but he seemed too focused on his mission to listen. As I turned back towards the register, I heard the sound of footsteps coming from down the aisle. A group of people appeared from nowhere, including several men in suits carrying briefcases. They began searching the registers and checking each item carefully. I knew I needed to act fast. Without thinking twice, I grabbed the remaining three items and quickly fled the store, hoping that I wouldn't be caught red-handed. Input: Text: You enter a grocery store and spot a $2 bill on the ground. You assume it's left by someone who forgot to bring it home. But when you approach the register, you realize that nobody else seems to be in line yet. Panic sets in as you start to wonder whether you've stumbled upon an actual egg scandal.

outputs: Text: so I have always loved music, especially rock n roll and jazz. My favorite band is Led Zeppelin. I am obsessed with them. However, I recently discovered another amazing band called Guns N Roses. Their music reminds me of what I love most about Led Zeppelin - raw energy, passion, and great songwriting. This discovery has made me want to listen to every single album they ever released. But where do I start? Well, I don't know if I can afford all those albums. So, I've started collecting some of their singles on YouTube. I find these songs inspiring, even though they aren't as powerful as the full-length LPs. Recently, I found a playlist titled "The Definitive Collection" on YouTube. It includes every single album plus many bonus tracks. Each track is accompanied by a brief description, including lyrics and instrumentation. After listening to each track, I try to determine whether or not I would recommend it based on factors such as lyrical content, musical quality, and overall impact. One of the songs that really struck a chord with me is "November Rain." The opening guitar riff immediately sets the tone for the rest of the song, and the drumming keeps up a steady rhythm throughout. Additionally, the vocal harmonies between Axl Rose and Slash make it stand out amongst other GN'R songs. Another song that stands out is "Welcome To The Jungle," which starts slow but builds quickly towards a catchy chorus. The solo section features both guitarists playing simultaneously, adding depth and complexity to the song. Aside from the first couple of songs, however, I'd suggest starting with "Sweet Child O' Mine" and working your way backward. "Patience" is a great example of how GNR uses simple yet effective arrangements to tell a story. And who could forget "Paradise City"?! What a rocker! Overall, I highly recommend checking out "The Definitive Collection" on YouTube. It's a fantastic resource for anyone interested in learning more about Guns N Roses.

Text: the day I found out that my boyfriend had cheated on me.

i woke up to an empty bed, tears streaming down my face. My heart was pounding so hard that I thought I might die. It felt like forever since I had kissed him goodbye at the doorstep. I looked over at his picture hanging on our wall and tried to remember what had happened between us. He had always seemed too perfect for words. And yet here I was, feeling completely broken.

The next morning, I woke up early and went straight to the coffee shop near our house. There, I sat in silence, staring blankly at the screen of my laptop, trying to make sense of what had happened. As soon as I got home, I collapsed onto my couch and cried until my eyes burned red. When I finally came back online, I typed out the most hurtful things anyone has ever written about me. I posted it on Facebook, hoping it would somehow find its way to him.

It took hours before I received any response. Then, something strange happened. His name popped up on my newsfeed, along with a message from someone who claimed to know him. They told me that he was upset because he couldn't figure out why I had suddenly become so cruel towards him. They even gave me advice on how to apologize properly. But I refused to listen to anything they had to say. All I needed was closure.

I waited patiently for days, waiting for some kind gesture from him. But nothing came. Finally, one evening, I received an unexpected message. It read, "Hey girl, I hope this finds you okay."

At first, I was shocked. How could he still care? But then, I realized that maybe, just maybe, he wasn't done with me yet. Maybe he had changed his mind.

So I wrote back, thanking him for taking the time to reach out. We exchanged numbers, and I started calling him every day. At first, it was awkward. We talked about everything under the sun, but mostly about how sorry we were for what had happened. I explained how much I loved him and how much I wished things could be different. He listened without interrupting, and we shared stories about our past together.

As time passed, we grew more comfortable with each other. We began spending more quality time together, talking, laughing, and exploring our interests. Our conversations became deeper, more meaningful, and ultimately led to something beautiful.

We broke up eventually, but not before I learned a valuable lesson. Sometimes, it takes a painful experience to realize that love isn't something that can be taken away easily. It requires work and effort, but it also requires trust and vulnerability. Most importantly, it requires honesty.

From that day forward, I will cherish every moment spent with him. I won't take him for granted anymore. I am grateful for the chance to learn from his mistake, grow as a person, and start fresh with someone else.

Text: 1984 was a terrible year. There wasn’t any good music released in 1984. I still remember “Money” by Michael Jackson and “I Want You Back” by Jackson 5.

In fact, if I recall correctly, 1984 was a terrible year because of George Orwell’s novel 1984. This novel is an allegory for what can happen under totalitarianism, such as a government controlling every aspect of citizens lives.

The novel revolves around four main characters: Oceania, Eurasia, Eastasia, and Newspeak. These countries are divided into three different areas based on geography and political structure. They live in fear of Big Brother who controls everything including speech, thoughts, and even dreams.

The story follows the journey of Winston Smith, a citizen of Oceania, who discovers that his past has been erased from his memory. He becomes obsessed with the idea of overthrowing Big Brother and begins to write down stories of the past to preserve evidence against him.

As the novel progresses, Winston starts to realize that he is not alone in his quest for freedom. Julia, another character, joins forces with him and together they begin to fight back against Big Brother.

At the end of the book, Winston realizes that the cost of fighting for freedom will be too great. But he also knows that the price of living in a world without free thinking and expression cannot be worth losing his own soul.

Social commentary is present throughout the novel. It shows the importance of individual rights, freedom of thought, and the dangers of censorship.

Overall, 1984 is a powerful critique of modern society. Its message resonates with many readers and continues to influence culture today.

outputs: Text: I am writing this essay for an online journalism class. It has been over a month since I first submitted this piece, and I am nervous to revise it. This piece is about the experience of living through a natural disaster. When Hurricane Katrina hit New Orleans in August 2005, many people lost their homes, jobs, and lives. I lived through this tragedy as a child, and I have grown up hearing stories about it ever since. But there were times when I felt helpless and scared. As someone who loves animals, I witnessed several wildlife deaths during the hurricane. Many dogs died trying to escape the flooded streets. Dogs were thrown off rooftops and drowned underneath cars. Some cats died of dehydration and heat exhaustion. Even though we knew that the storm would eventually pass, we couldn't help feeling helpless. We watched in horror as buildings crumbled and water flowed in. At night, our family slept outside because our house was destroyed. One particular night, I heard my mother crying softly. She told me she was scared and worried about her husband, who worked at the hospital nearby. He hadn't come back yet. Later, I saw her cry tears of joy when she learned that he was alive and safe. I also remember seeing people searching for loved ones. My cousin, who works in a supermarket, went door to door asking for information about his brother, who had been missing. His sister, however, was too frightened to answer questions. After days of waiting, I finally received news that he was found alive and injured. It was a relief, but it was hard to know if he would survive. During the hurricane, we stayed indoors most of the time. Our neighborhood was cut off from the rest of the city. No food, no water, no electricity. Everyone seemed to be doing okay until the power started flickering on and off every hour. Then we began to hear strange sounds coming from inside our house. It sounded like footsteps and whispers. People tried to ignore them, but soon everyone became paranoid. I don't know what those creatures could be. Was it another person? Or maybe something worse? We spent hours locked in our bedrooms, listening to each other's breathing and praying that we wouldn't be attacked. Eventually, the lights came back on. We resumed our normal routine. For days afterwards, we remained quiet and afraid. Sometimes, I wondered whether we will ever feel safe again. But even now, years later, I realize that we emerged stronger than before. We grew more aware of the world around us, and we learned to rely on ourselves. Looking back, I realized that Katrina taught me important things. It showed me the importance of community and the strength of human spirit. And perhaps most importantly, it reminded me of the fragility of life.

Text: I have no idea what I did wrong!

the first thing I noticed was that I felt exhausted after a weekend away. It wasn’t until I got back home that I realized something else - I haven’t eaten anything since Friday afternoon. I thought maybe I could survive without food for another three days, but I quickly learned otherwise. My stomach growls whenever I sit down to eat, and my mouth feels dry even though I’ve consumed plenty of water.

I don’t know if it’s because of the travel, or if I just lack an appetite lately, but whatever the reason, there isn’t any sense of hunger anymore.

I feel like I am drowning in a sea of stress. I want to run away, but every step I take brings me further into my own abyss.

My mind starts to play tricks on me, and my thoughts start spiraling out of control. Sometimes I think about suicide, other times I’m convinced I will die alone in my room. But most of the time, I just sit here, feeling powerless and helpless.

I know deep down that I shouldn’t give up on trying to recover. There’s nothing more important than my mental health, and I need to keep pushing forward. But I also realize that this journey won’t be easy, and I may never fully overcome my anxiety.

She started playing a game called "Trivia Night," and I quickly realized I knew nothing about most of the questions. As the night progressed, I found myself laughing more and more. Finally, we finished the round and I won! Afterwards, I walked over to her bedroom and took a shower. When I returned, she was sitting on the couch, reading a magazine. "Hey," I said, "Would you mind sharing your drink?" She smiled and handed me a glass filled with lemonade. We both sipped on them together, and chatted about whatever we wanted. It felt like we were just having fun talking, and not even really paying attention to each other. Later that evening, we went outside again. This time, she invited me to join her on her porch swing. She told me stories about growing up, and showed me pictures of herself and her family. We talked until late, and I couldn't stop smiling. At first, I thought maybe I would fall asleep next to her, but she stayed awake and kept talking. Eventually, she fell asleep too, and I snuggled up beside her. For hours, we talked and laughed. Then, we heard the sound of a helicopter flying overhead. My heart raced as I looked up at the sky. Was that a plane? Or was it just a storm coming through? But then, we saw the lightning flashes, and the thunder booms. Suddenly, the sky turned dark and heavy. We both froze in terror. And then, suddenly, the wind picked up. The leaves on the trees began to rustle, and the branches swayed violently. A strong gust hit us, knocking us off balance. We scrambled for cover, holding onto each other tightly. For what seemed like forever, we held onto each other, shaking with fear. When the wind finally died down, we breathed a collective sigh of relief. But we were still shaken, and we knew that the danger hadn't passed yet. That's when I noticed a small bird perched on a nearby branch. Its wings flapping furiously, it flew towards us, its eyes fixed on mine. It landed on my shoulder, and I felt a sudden surge of warmth spread throughout my body. The bird seemed to know something important was about to happen, and its voice was full of confidence and anticipation. It spoke to me, saying, "You will survive." But every challenge has also brought moments of joy and wonder. Sometimes those moments feel like tiny miracles, and I want to hold onto them tightly. Other times, they seem insignificant compared to the bigger picture. Either way, though, they always remind me of how lucky I am to have such amazing companions.

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: last night I went out to eat with some friends. We were trying to decide what restaurant we wanted to go to because everyone has different preferences. One friend suggested we try "The Bitter End," which is known for its seafood.

My other friend who loves veggies and salads immediately pointed out that it was a vegetarian restaurant. Another friend who likes steak and cheese burgers also mentioned that it was a steakhouses. However, my friend who loves pizza seemed hesitant, saying he doesn't care for anything that comes from the oven. He explained that they have a few options, including pizza, wings, and pasta dishes. My friend agreed, but he did mention that the food was good quality and the prices were reasonable.

We arrived at The Bitter End and walked inside. It was quite busy; people were waiting outside for tables. There was an enormous menu, and we tried to choose something simple yet satisfying. As soon as our drink orders came, we noticed that the waitress recommended several appetizers to start us off.

I ordered the crab dip, and my friend chose the chicken parmesan. They both loved their choices! The crab dip was delicious - it had a tangy flavor that perfectly complemented the creamy texture of the dip. My friend enjoyed his chicken parmesan even though he isn't too fond of meat.

Both of them also shared a side order of garlic bread. The bread was crispy and slightly sweet. My friend liked it a lot and added it to his plate, while my friend enjoyed the fresh garlic flavour without having to add it to his meal.

As we waited for our entrees, I noticed another table nearby. A group of four guys were eating spaghetti and meatballs. Their conversation was loud and animated, causing the sound level in the restaurant to increase significantly.

One of the men spoke excitedly, asking the server if they could get the spaghetti sauce spicy. The server politely declined, explaining that the restaurant was not designed to serve spicy food. But the man insisted anyway, adding that he couldn't bear to miss out on such a unique experience.

Another customer entered the restaurant, ordering a large margarita. The server apologised again, stating that the restaurant does not allow alcoholic beverages during dinner hours. The man, disappointed, thanked him for letting him know and continued to talk loudly.

Finally, my turn came to order dessert. Since I don't love ice cream, I opted for a small fruit platter. My friend selected a large dessert, which turned out to be tiramisu.

When the bill finally arrived, we saw that the total cost was $67.89. This amount surprised us because we hadn't seen that price tag before. Our server explained that the restaurant charges an extra $5 per person above the standard rate. The reason behind this additional fee is that they provide multiple courses, meaning each course requires a separate payment. Additionally, they offer special deals where customers can save money by paying separately for certain items.

Overall, our meal at The Bitter End was enjoyable. Although the restaurant may seem expensive initially, the overall value of the meal far exceeded the initial costs. The atmosphere was cozy and friendly, with a mix of young couples, families, and businesspeople enjoying their meals together. Despite the noise from the other tables, the service was prompt and efficient. Overall, we highly recommend this restaurant to anyone seeking a relaxing evening out with good food and excellent service.

Text: I recently started working full-time and have noticed a trend among employees who work remotely. They often don’t communicate effectively because they feel overwhelmed by the amount of information they receive daily through various channels.
I think many companies could benefit from implementing a communication plan that includes regular status updates and clear expectations for performance metrics.

It’s essential to ensure everyone knows what is expected of them in terms of deliverables, timelines, and goals. By following these tips, we believe remote teams would find greater clarity regarding expectations and better collaboration leading to increased productivity and employee satisfaction.

Text: I love coffee! It makes me feel alive.

     A few years back, I tried to quit drinking coffee altogether because I thought it might lead to an early death. But over the past decade, I've learned that caffeine isn't exactly what kills you - it's the stress that causes your heart to race. When you finally realize that your mind doesn't need coffee to function properly, you start drinking it anyway. And once you know this, you don't even notice that you're missing out on all these benefits.

I've always loved coffee, especially the smell of freshly brewed coffee wafting through my living room. So why did I stop drinking it? Well, for starters, I realized that I could probably survive without it if I needed to. That's not something I want to say about my health, though; I used to worry that my blood sugar levels were low, and I stopped taking insulin because I couldn't tolerate the side effects. Luckily, my doctor told me that there are natural alternatives to insulin that are more effective and easier to digest.

In addition to feeling lighter overall, my energy level has improved since quitting coffee. There's nothing quite like the feeling of having extra energy during the day, and it's nice to not feel tired throughout the night. This leads to better sleep quality too, which is important for mental clarity. Plus, I find that I have more energy to explore my hobbies, which is great for me because I really enjoy playing guitar.

So, I guess I won't miss the jitteriness anymore. While I haven't completely stopped drinking coffee, I definitely limit my consumption to a few cups per week. For some reason, coffee has become a habit, and I struggle to resist the urge to indulge. However, I also understand that everyone has different preferences and dietary restrictions, so I encourage anyone else struggling with coffee addiction to consider trying herbal tea, which often contains fewer calories and less caffeine than regular coffee.

It's hard to explain to someone who hasn't experienced it firsthand, but sometimes people ask me if I ever miss coffee. My answer is usually yes, but I try to remind them that my brain works differently nowadays. Coffee may not seem like such a big deal, but it does provide many physical and psychological benefits that I wouldn't trade for anything. If you're curious about other substances that can help boost your brainpower, I recommend checking out books like "The Power of Now" by Eckhart Tolle or "The Alchemist" by Paulo Coelho. They offer fascinating perspectives on how certain practices can enhance cognitive abilities.

Text: 
one day I walked through the park where I used to play every morning. As usual, the birds chirped happily and leaves rustled softly. But something strange caught my eye - the sky looked darker, the sun lower, the trees swayed more violently, and I couldn't shake off an uneasy feeling. My heart pounded faster than ever, my palms grew clammy. I started walking towards the river, hoping to find some solace in nature.
As I reached the banks, I noticed a group of people playing a game called "The Last Man Standing." They seemed calm, content, unaware of anything outside. It was eerie; no noise could be heard except for the occasional bird song. Then, suddenly, I saw him - the last man standing. He was alone, without his family or any other human contact. His face showed deep concentration, and his eyes fixed on the ground. I watched silently, mesmerized.
He remained still for a minute, and then slowly lifted his head. A smile appeared on his lips. "Hello," he uttered softly. "I am David." I stared blankly at him. No words could come out of my mouth. All I could think of was that he might have lost someone close to him. We stayed silent for sometime, neither speaking nor moving. After a while, David got up and approached me. "David?" I spoke, surprised. "Yes, John?" He nodded. "You know, I don't want to hurt anyone here. Can we please leave now? Please?" "No," he replied firmly. "We can stay if you wish. Just let us say goodbye." "Okay," I agreed, feeling relieved. I knew it would be difficult for him to talk to strangers, especially those who look different from him. However, he managed to make small talk, thanking me profusely for stopping by. "It was nice meeting you," he said, extending his hand. "Thank you, sir." We shook hands awkwardly, and I left. On my way home, I thought of the conversation we had shared. Was it true? Did he love someone else besides himself? Would he regret leaving her behind? These thoughts haunted me until I finally fell asleep that night. The next morning, I woke up early. It was still pitch-black outside. Suddenly, I heard footsteps approaching the door. I opened it cautiously. To my surprise, there was David waiting for me. He looked exhausted, but somehow, I could sense that he wasn't lying. "Good morning, Mr. Johnson," he greeted me. "Good morning, David," I replied, smiling weakly. "Do you mind if I tell you why I stopped by?" "Sure, David. Go ahead." "Well, I was thinking about starting a new chapter in my life. Maybe finding someone special will help me feel complete again." "That sounds interesting, David," I responded. "But I have a daughter at home. She needs me too." "Oh, yes. You understand, don't you?" David nodded. "And your father doesn't seem to care about me either." "That's true. But I don't want to ruin things between us. If I leave, she won't know about it." "Fine, fine. I understand completely. So, maybe you could visit me once in a while. And if you meet someone, let me know. We can plan a date soon." David smiled. "Thanks, sir. That means a lot to me." I smiled back. "Me too, David. Me too."

Text: "this is what happens when your girlfriend gives birth to twins."

The following sentence appears underneath the title: "This is why we can't have nice things"



I know I haven't posted anything recently because of the fact that I am still recovering from giving birth to twin boys. This story is more personal so here goes:

My husband and I were blessed with twin boys on June 9th. It has been quite an experience so far. Our first son, John Alexander was born at 6:57 pm PST on Friday, June 18th. He arrived healthy and strong. Our second son, Thomas Andrew was born at 7:22 pm PST on Saturday, June 19th. He also arrived healthy and strong. We will celebrate both boys together next month on July 2nd.

As soon as our doctor gave us the okay to leave the hospital, we immediately started planning the party. I spent countless hours researching different ideas online and found several great ones. One idea that caught my eye was to make cupcakes with names on them. Since I couldn't find any cupcake decorating supplies at Walmart, I decided to try making some using cookie cutters. My husband came up with the name idea, and we got creative with colors, designs, and flavors.

We used Wilton® Sugar Cookie Cutters to create unique shapes. For example, there were baby boy cookies with the words "Newborn" written inside, baby girl cookies with "First Birthday" written inside, and even some with heart-shaped cookies with the words "Mommy & Daddy Love You" written inside. There were also "Twin Boys" cookies, and "Big Sister/Brother" cookies.

Our friend Megan helped us bake the cupcakes and decorated them. She suggested using edible glitter, sprinkles, and royal icing. We chose white cake mix and chocolate frosting, along with vanilla and strawberry ice cream. We used royal icing for the decorations, and I think it turned out really nicely.

To make sure everyone knew the date, we hung up signs outside our house saying "June 2nd - Twins Birthdays!" On top of the sign, we wrote down each child's name and age, along with "Born Today!" And we hung a large balloon over the front lawn with a message reading "Happy Birthday Twin Boys!"

We celebrated both boys separately on their special days. They loved playing with their siblings, eating ice cream, watching movies, and doing other fun activities. Their big brother, Thomas, took charge of the party and played games, sang songs, and read books to his younger brothers.

It wasn't until the end of the night that I realized something strange. While trying to clean up after the party, I noticed that the floor looked dirty. As I walked back into the living room, I saw a tiny footprint on the rug near where the table had been set up. At first, I thought maybe someone had stepped on it accidentally, but then I noticed another small print on the wall behind the couch. I ran over to investigate and discovered a matching pair of prints on either side of the couch.

These prints weren't just random prints; they were the same size and shape. I quickly realized that someone had taken a photo of us during the party and uploaded it onto social media.

After realizing the mistake, I called the police department and reported the incident. They sent officers to our home to investigate, and luckily no arrests were made. However, the culprit(s) did confess to taking pictures of the party without permission, although they claimed they didn't realize they were stealing from us.

In conclusion, I would like to thank my family, friends, and community for supporting us throughout this crazy journey. Being a parent has taught me the importance of having trusted people in my life, especially those closest to me. It's hard sometimes, but knowing that I have support makes everything worthwhile. Thank you.

Text: I don’t know why we have to live in such close quarters with all these bags of stinky pee, but it seems like it’ll always be so.



this is an essay about living together in dormitories and what makes it bearable or unbearable depending on your perspective.



the first few years were great because there weren’t any other people sharing our space. We could come home every night without feeling guilty about having fun. However, things changed once I moved into my own room. Now, even though I can hear everyone else showering downstairs, I still feel trapped. It feels like no matter where I go, someone will always find me. And sometimes I wish they wouldn’t.



The reason I mention the smell specifically is that I don’t want to sound too negative. There are definitely moments when I love living here. When we have parties, everyone gets along, and nobody is moaning about sleeping arrangements. But then, the party ends, and everyone heads back to their rooms, and I realize I’m alone again. Sometimes, I think about moving out, but I’ve gotten used to sharing a space with others. So, I try to keep it light and enjoy each moment.



I guess part of the problem is that I am introverted. Being surrounded by other people means that I tend to become more reserved. My roommates are kinda nice, but I don’t really talk to them outside of class or during breaks. Even then, I mostly listen and nod. They seem to understand that I need some distance between us.



One thing I’ve learned is to respect boundaries. If my roommate wants to watch TV late at night, she needs to let me know ahead of time. I also don’t mind staying up late if she does. She’s allowed to have her own thoughts, so I don’t feel like I’m constantly interrupting her.



Another issue is that we both have different schedules. For example, my roommate has classes during lunchtime, whereas I usually have classes during dinner. This means that I often spend hours waiting for her to finish eating, and then I have to walk around campus to avoid crowds. On top of that, she doesn’t always eat breakfast before class, meaning that I have to leave early and miss class. This has led to arguments over whether or not we should move out altogether.



So, yeah, it’s hard to balance living together with keeping ourselves separate. One thing that helps is knowing that we’re both adults and responsible for taking care of ourselves. Plus, we’ve tried to make sure that we communicate effectively.



In conclusion, living in a dormitory is difficult. No matter how many positive experiences we may have, we’re stuck with each other for fourteen months. Still, it would be amazing if we could figure out ways to make it easier on each other. Maybe we could schedule times for meals or movies, or maybe we could start a tradition of leaving notes on each other’s doorsteps to remind us of each other’s presence. Whatever works best, I hope we can learn to coexist peacefully.

outputs: Text: I have been thinking lately how much better life would be without social media. It has become such a distraction that I can barely concentrate on anything else. There's just too many notifications pounding away at my phone all day. But when I finally find myself alone, I am amazed by how much more present I feel. The silence of the world around me feels refreshing. As I walk outside, I can hear birds chirping, leaves rustling, and even distant cars honking their horns. I've never felt so alive before. Sometimes I wish people could just leave me alone forever. They can go back to their lives where they know everything will happen according to plan. Or maybe they'll change their minds once they see the impact of their actions. Either way, I'd rather be able to choose when and where I want to spend my days. Output: I used to love going out to dinner because the atmosphere was perfect for conversations and catching up with old friends. Whenever I'm walking through a park, listening to the sounds of crickets and leaves, I forget about everything else for a few minutes.

Input:
outputs:
Text: I have been trying to use a productivity app called "to-do" for a while now but every time I open it I feel like I'll never finish everything. So I started looking into other options. One thing led to another and before I knew it, I found this little gem: Trello. It has helped me immensely with my tasks and reminders. Here's how I set it up:

Step 1: Sign Up For A Free Account On Their Website
Click the signup button located at the top right corner of their website. Fill out your name, email address, password, and choose a username if desired. Click Create Account. Step 2: Add Boards And Collections To Your Board
Create boards for different projects, teams, or categories of tasks. You can also create collections within each board. For example, you might create a board for "Marketing," and inside that board, you could create subboards for specific campaigns or ads. Click the plus (+) symbol to add a new board or collection. Step 3: Set Up Lists And Labels
Lists allow you to group related items together. They make it easy to organize tasks based on priority or deadline. To create a new list, click the + symbol next to the "Boards" section. Select "New List." Give your list a name, such as "Product Development" or "Budget Tracker." Next, click the "+Labels" icon and select labels to apply to your list. You can add multiple labels per item. Finally, click the checkmark beside each label you want to assign to each item. This will give you a complete view of what items belong to each category. Step 4: Start Adding Items To Your Boards And Collections
Now that you have created lists and assigned labels, start adding items to your boards and collections. Drag and drop items onto your boards and lists as needed. When you're ready to move an item between boards or collections, drag it across to the appropriate destination. Step 5: Use The App To Track Progress
To track progress, simply mark completed items. If an item doesn't require completion, mark it as "In Progress." Whenever you add an item to a board or collection, Trello automatically updates your progress bar. The green bar shows you how far along you are in completing tasks. The blue bar shows you how many items remain to be completed. Step 6: Customize Your Workflow Based On Your Needs
Trello offers several customization options to help you streamline your workflow. You can change the color scheme, fonts, and layouts of your dashboard. Additionally, you can add cards to your boards based on criteria such as due date, status, or type of project. By customizing your workflow, you can ensure that you always stay focused on the most important items first. That's it! With these steps, you should now have successfully set up Trello and organized your workflow effectively. Remember to regularly review your lists and checklists to ensure they are still relevant and effective.

Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Input:
outputs: Text: I woke up early this morning feeling like I could barely walk. It wasn't until after my morning run that I realized what happened...I slipped on a patch of ice in our front yard. My foot was stuck underneath me for quite some time before finally coming free! Not only were my shoes wet (which I didn't realize), but also my pants and jacket were submerged in ice water! Needless to say, I felt extremely embarrassed by my predicament. After running around outside for several minutes trying to figure out where I fell, I realized that I needed to warm myself up first. So I started shivering uncontrollably, hoping that would make me feel more comfortable. After several minutes, I realized that I had frostbite. Frostbite occurs when your body's blood vessels constrict, causing tissue damage due to low temperatures. Unfortunately, this meant that my skin would turn red and blotchy, along with numbing sensations throughout my entire arm. As soon as possible, I sought medical attention and began treatment. Thankfully, it wasn't too severe; however, the experience left me feeling humbled and reminded me why I love winter sports such as skiing and snowboarding.

Input:
outputs: Text: I’ve been running for years, but never before has it felt like such a struggle. It’s not that I don’t enjoy the exercise – I love running! But sometimes, after only a few minutes, my knees feel like they’re made of lead. My legs burn, and sweat drips down my face. Sometimes I can barely walk, let alone run. This morning, I woke up with soreness everywhere. Not even a full day of running could alleviate it. When I stepped outside last night, the wind hit me square in the chest, making breathing difficult. The sun beat down mercilessly, causing my skin to turn red. And then, just when I thought things couldn’t get worse, I noticed blood coming out of my ear. A sudden headache took hold, accompanied by nausea and dizziness. Oh, joy. “I think I’ll skip my workout,” I told myself. That’s exactly what I did. As soon as I walked into the house, the pain began to spread across my entire body. My heart raced, and I quickly realized that my first mistake had been skipping my regular check-up. My doctor didn’t see me until late that afternoon. By then, the swelling had already begun to subside, but my ears were still ringing, and my sinuses were congested. My muscles ached. For days afterwards, I struggled to sit upright without feeling like I might collapse. I felt disoriented and anxious, constantly worrying about what I would eat next. At times, I found myself lying awake, staring at the ceiling, wondering whether this was all worth it. How many times does a person have to break their leg before learning? One day, I realized that I needed to stop playing catch-up. Too often, I was putting pressure on myself, pushing too hard, trying to prove something to others. Now I know why I started running – because it helped me deal with stress. Running taught me that taking care of yourself wasn’t selfish; it was necessary. Over the course of several weeks, I learned to listen to my body. Instead of pushing through pain, I listened carefully to what my muscles wanted. If my knees hurt, I sat down. If my ears hurt, I closed them. If my shoulders tensed, I relaxed them. With each passing week, I became more comfortable with my limitations. Finally, I felt ready to tackle another challenge. Last Saturday, I ran the New York City Marathon. The race itself was grueling, physically demanding and emotionally exhausting. Every step felt like a battle, every mile felt like an accomplishment. There were moments where I felt completely drained, and other moments where I pushed beyond what I thought was possible. Yet, no matter how tired I was, I kept moving forward. Through sheer willpower and determination, I crossed the finish line. Afterward, I spent the rest of the day surrounded by loved ones, celebrating with tears streaming down our faces. We talked about the memories we shared during the marathon and laughed together. We celebrated our victory, knowing that we had accomplished something truly incredible. Even though I may have broken my leg once again, I’ve learned that strength comes from within. Strength doesn’t depend solely on physical abilities. It’s about finding your inner resilience, staying strong, and continuously pushing towards growth. So, the next time someone asks you how you’re doing, try to smile and answer honestly. You never know who else might benefit from hearing your story.

 her face hadn't changed at all during the entire exchange. she finally just completed my transaction and said have a nice day. i'm not sure if she believed me or not, but i gathered all my stuff and hightailed it out of there.

Input: Text: obligatory comment about this not actually happening today, and this being a throwaway account.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.
