Text: This TIFU has nothing to do with your company's recent hiring decisions.

The job market seems bleak these days. With companies slashing headcount and layoffs becoming commonplace, I thought it might make sense to offer some advice based on what I have learned since joining the industry.

As someone who joined shortly after the recession began, I can tell you that hiring trends have changed significantly over the past five years. Employees were once seen as assets - something you could invest in if things turned around - rather than liabilities. Nowadays, however, employers are more focused on cost-cutting measures, including cutting payroll expenses. As such, recruitment tactics have become leaner, with fewer candidates being approached for interviews. Instead, businesses are focusing heavily on testing the waters with smaller, informal job opportunities.

In fact, many companies now require prospective employees to fill out applications online. It’s not uncommon for applicants to receive upwards of 50 responses within hours. If you don’t hear back, chances are you won’t move on to the next stage of the process. To avoid falling victim to this trap, consider taking advantage of networking events, attending open houses, or reaching out directly to potential employers. Don’t rely solely on online application methods; it may take longer to find suitable positions.

When applying for jobs, be sure to highlight specific skills and experiences relevant to the position. For example, if you work in finance, focus on financial analysis and quantitative modeling. Make sure to tailor your cover letter and resume accordingly. When submitting your application materials, send them via email rather than postal mail. This will help speed up the review process.

If you are interested in a particular role, research the company thoroughly before applying. Look for information regarding the culture, mission statement, values, and any notable accomplishments or awards. Additionally, read reviews from current employees and seek feedback from supervisors. Finally, ask questions during the interview process to ensure you understand the company's goals and objectives.

I hope these tips provide some insight and guidance for navigating the job market. Remember, finding a great fit takes time and effort, but it doesn't necessarily mean sacrificing personal growth and development. Good luck!

cut to the second lunch break.

this is where the fuck-up happens.

it was at this moment that i knew i could weave my way out of the situation by just ratting on x and z.

luckily it worked. unluckily they don't want to talk to me ever again.
Output: acted like a suicide bomber in school, lost two friends in the process.

Text: when I was 5 years old, I found a piece of metal in my backyard. It wasn't until later that night that I realized what it was. It was a piece of junk mail from the local paper with a small, bright red X drawn across the front cover. That single letter has haunted me all these years.

I remember thinking how ridiculous it was to think someone would send me something that was meant for the trash bin. But looking back on it now, it's clear why they sent it. They wanted me to know that if I continued to ignore their adverts, they wouldn't stop sending them. And guess what? They never stopped. Over the next few months, every week or so, another one arrived in my mailbox. At first, I didn't even notice. Then, I started feeling guilty about ignoring them. Soon enough, I couldn't keep up with the number of letters coming to my house each month. One year, I only received three letters. Another year, I received none. My parents finally took action. They put together a list of things I needed to buy instead of buying advertised items. This helped a lot, but it still felt wrong noticing those little yellow envelopes. Eventually, after many more failed attempts, I gave up. I accepted that I would always receive these annoying flyers. Yet somehow, despite everything, I couldn't help but feel angry. Why bother trying to fight against such petty advertising? Who cares about those big businesses who sell us products? I wondered. Wasn't it better to just accept whatever came our way? Eventually, I stopped complaining. I learned to see the world differently. Instead of seeing advertisements as intrusive and unnecessary, I began to appreciate them as opportunities to learn. Whenever I got a bill in the mail, I used to read the circular carefully. I learned that some companies offer discounts to customers who subscribe to their newsletters. Others offered loyalty programs for frequent purchasers. I discovered that certain retailers had coupons available online. These were great because they allowed me to save money without having to go to physical stores. I also noticed that some stores would give away free samples with purchase. Sometimes, I'd try out different brands to find my favorite ones. I started to view advertisements as a learning opportunity rather than simply as wasteful ways to spend money. As a result, I became less judgmental towards others who might have seen the same thing happening. Some may argue that advertising isn't necessarily bad. After all, most consumers rely on it to make informed decisions. However, I believe that advertising can become obnoxious and invasive when it becomes too commonplace. Advertisements aren't inherently evil, but they certainly shouldn't be celebrated. Ultimately, it comes down to personal choice. If you decide that advertising doesn't fit within your values, then you should consider whether or not you really need to consume any products or services that depend on it.

Input: Text: so i live in new york and it's getting a bit colder here so my fiancé kept asking me to take out the air conditioner.  we live in an apartment on the second floor.  i had just come off a 10 hour shift and i was pretty beat but i decided lets just get it done.  we slowly take apart the window and gently push it forward.  now here's the issue.  we had forgotten that it had rained yesterday so the air conditioner had  collected a bit of water.  it came pouring out and in the surprise we lost the grip on the air conditioner.  it plummeted out the window and went through a class covering over the stairwell.  it shattered.  needless to say its gonna be expensive to fix it and the owners weren't happy.  luckily there was nobody on the stairwell at the time.
Output: i'm and idiot and air conditioners are heavy

Input: Text: filmed a few things for a friend's english class, based off of a book they had read. he needed people to run from something, so i put on a blanket and acted as an old beggar with a walking stick.


when the time came to panic and run away, instead of staying true to my elderly character, i threw the stick to the side and ran.


we were doing this in another friend's backyard, and the portion we were running on was quite uneven. i ended up stumbling, and landed wrong on my leg when trying to catch myself.


ended up bending my knee a direction hinge joints should not bend, which led to me falling on the ground in absolute agony. 


luckily the damage was minimal and i still have a functioning knee.
Output: the fast lane is not for me

this reminded me of a conversation I had recently where someone mentioned feeling disconnected from the world around them. I realized that sometimes our ability to immerse ourselves in a topic can lead us to miss out on the bigger picture.

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: I am currently living in New York City, where summer temperatures can reach well above 90 degrees Fahrenheit during the daytime. However, due to the humidity level in the city, many people choose to invest in AC units. My current apartment building has no AC installed; however, my roommate recently bought a small portable unit for our bedroom, and I have been trying to convince him to install one for us too. After several attempts, he finally agreed to purchase one for himself. However, his decision resulted in a catastrophic failure within hours of installation.

The reason behind this incident lies in the fact that the portable AC unit he purchased is not designed to operate in high humidity environments like NYC. As soon as it rains, the moisture collects inside the device, leading to condensation and eventually breaking down. This happened while we were both working late at night, and the rain poured onto the AC unit, causing it to malfunction completely. It fell backwards and landed on top of our shared bathroom sink, causing the entire kitchen sink to overflow. Needless to say, the damage was significant, and we had to replace all of the components before they could function again.

My experience highlights the importance of considering factors such as climate conditions and potential hazards when making decisions regarding indoor comfort.

Input: Text: well, a little context. i´m the kind of boy who needs to make experiments, to push a little the limits and i can´t stay without making something too much time.
a friend came with the idea of rockets : dude, i got this really cool project, we need household items and it´s going to be awesome!
we gather the materials, make the mix, cook it and burned it. it was awesome as he said and we make it like 3 times that day.
by this point he tells me that the mix can be used as fuel for rockets.
sooooo, this morning i just wanted to make some fuel. mix the ingredients, ready to cook in my kitchen.
maybe some glasses to look more professional? ok, lets do it.
so, there´s me, heating an inflamable mix.
then, it happens. a huge flame in front of my eyes. i move back and protect me, but it was instantly gone. the smoke covered everything, so i went outside to cough a little when my sister saw me. burned hair, the glasses were black, as my nose and forehead. my hand suffered the most and the house was filled with smoke (wich i didn´t know if it was toxic or not). 
never cooking again by myself.
Output: got burned cooking rocket fuel, filled the house with smoke

Text: "I have never felt so alive!" exclaimed a young girl from the suburbs as she ran towards her mother who had been waiting patiently at their car. Her mother raised an eyebrow. "Animals? That sounds like a good plan," she remarked.
The girl smiled, pleased with the way things turned out. It wasn't always easy to figure out what she wanted to do, but this year, she knew what she needed to do.

outputs: Text: I have been having some health issues lately, but I’ve never felt so alive than when I was running around New York City. It wasn’t always easy, though; sometimes the city would feel oppressive, and I found myself struggling to find joy in even the simplest things. But then, I remember why I started running in the first place – to clear my head and feel free from all the worries. So I took a deep breath, stepped into Central Park, and let loose. This park has been such a blessing for me – the fresh air, the open space, and the endorphins released after each run. I’ll admit, the first few runs weren’t easy. My knee wouldn’t hold up, my legs were sore, and I couldn’t seem to keep up with the others. But gradually, I learned how to listen to my body, focus on what I could do rather than what I couldn’t, and trust that the pain was temporary. And now, every weekend, I wake up early enough to hit the streets before the sun rises. It may only be a mile-long jog, but every step feels like a victory. Sometimes, I’ll pass a stranger, and their smile will lift my spirits. Other times, they’ll stop and ask where I’m heading. They’re curious about my journey, and I love hearing their stories. It reminds me that I’m not alone, and that there are people out there who care about my progress. Some days, I’ll run until my heart starts pounding, feeling the adrenaline surge through my veins. Then, I’ll stop and rest, taking deep breaths and savoring the moment. I don’t know what the future holds, but I know that whatever comes next, I’ll face it with grace and determination. That’s the power of running – the strength it takes to overcome obstacles and persevere. Output: ran every single day since the beginning of summer, passing strangers and enjoying the warmth of sunrise. Running helped ease stress, boost confidence, and connect with others.

Input: Text: background: i went to summer camp about two weeks ago and met a guy. it's long distance and we text every second we possibly can. 

      now fast forward to this week. i'm in my school's marching band, and our band camp started this week, which means i get the pleasure of spending six hours a day on my feet doing things that the human body was not naturally made to do. our rehearsals are in the mornings and late afternoons/evenings which means i get a couple of hours a day in which i can do whatever. well, i was supposed to do the work for my online class and practice my music for band, and i hoped to fit eating, napping and texting the bf in somewhere int those precious band-free hours.

Text: Background: I recently got engaged to my girlfriend of almost three years. It's been a whirlwind romance from start to finish. We were high school sweethearts and since then we've gone through several ups and downs before finally deciding to give love another chance. Here's how we got together...

     My first year of college, I took a job working at a local bar downtown. One night, after closing the bar, I walked home feeling tired and alone. As I turned onto the street leading back towards campus, I saw her walking toward me - a tall blonde woman with piercing blue eyes and a smile that lit up the entire block. She stopped abruptly when she saw me approaching and looked away embarrassedly. "Hi," I said tentatively. "I'm sorry if I'm interrupting anything." Her eyes darted nervously between mine and the empty road ahead. After a few moments, she nodded slightly, seemingly relieved to have found someone to talk to. Over the next month, we hung out more often than not. I remember one particularly hot afternoon when we sat outside on the patio of a small diner on Main Street. She wore a flowered dress that seemed tailored specifically for me, and her hair fell loose and cascaded over her shoulders like silk. She smiled softly and offered me a drink. When I declined, she reached across the table and tapped the glass against hers. "Want something?" she asked, looking up at me with bright green eyes. "No thanks," I replied. "Just trying to make conversation." Our conversations became increasingly intimate as we spent more time together. By the end of the semester, we knew each other so well that we could both tell what was coming out of each others' mouths without having to ask questions. We exchanged numbers and began making plans to see each other again soon. Soon enough, though, reality set in. We moved in together, graduated, and started a life together. It wasn't always easy, but it has been incredibly rewarding. I know that sometimes relationships don't last forever, but I also know that they're worth fighting for because they bring joy, laughter, and happiness into your life. And for us, it's definitely worth it.

Text: today I went to my friend's house to hangout with her and her family but when I arrived she told me she had already invited some other guys over so I decided to go home instead

After dinner I came home to an invitation for a party. After getting ready I found out that the host was also planning on bringing over a group of girls.

I wasn’t really feeling the idea of having three groups of girls all together so I politely declined their offer and headed straight back to bed.

The next night I received an email saying “Dear Sir/Madam, Please join our exclusive event tonight”. This prompted me to quickly check if there were any other events happening in town. To my surprise, there was a big bash planned for tomorrow evening at a local hotel. I couldn’t believe my luck. What better opportunity to meet new people?

However, upon arriving at the hotel I noticed something strange. All of the guests seemed to be dressed up and looked extremely happy. I felt embarrassed and left the venue immediately. That’s when things started to get weird. Everyone kept staring at me and whispering. It turned out that the entire event was organized by a couple who wanted to ‘introduce themselves’ to each guest. They asked me what my name was and how many years older I was. Needless to say, I didn’t know how to answer these questions. As much as I tried to avoid eye contact, I couldn’t help but notice the smiles on every face. Eventually, someone suggested I take part in a game called'speed dating'. This sounded intriguing enough to give it a shot. I agreed, and soon found myself standing in front of a table full of strangers. We were introduced, exchanged numbers, and spent a few minutes chatting before moving on to the next person. But something was different. These conversations weren’t about flirting or finding common ground – everything was awkwardly forced. There was an underlying tension between us that felt almost electric. At one point, I mentioned that I was nervous about the event. My date replied, “It’ll be fine. You’re not alone.” She was right. Looking back, I realized that the only thing holding me back from leaving was my own insecurities. Maybe I was too old for this kind of thing, maybe I wasn’t attractive enough. Who knows? Whatever the reason may be, I was stuck in a never-ending cycle of self-doubt. On the third night, I met a guy named John. He was friendly and easygoing, but he seemed to sense that something was wrong. His eyes narrowed as he listened to my story, and I could tell he was trying his best to make me feel comfortable. Despite our initial exchange, however, I couldn’t shake the feeling that I was walking into a trap. And yet, despite my misgivings, I stayed until the end of the night. By then, I had formed a connection with John, and I realized that sometimes, meeting someone new can lead to unexpected discoveries.

Text: i hate getting emails from companies asking me if I want to sign up for their services but every email has a different subject line like "get started with our free trial" or "sign up today and receive $500 off" etc.. i'd always read those without thinking too much about it until yesterday. It turns out that some of these companies send promotional emails via an autoresponder service called autohosting.com and their spam filter automatically adds an extra space between the subject line and the body content, causing them to show up as spam.

To solve this problem, you need to check your company's email marketing automation platform settings. You can usually access this information by clicking on the'marketing' tab in your company's admin dashboard. From there, you should see a section called 'email marketing'. Under this section, look for an option called 'autoresponders'. Make sure this setting is set to 'off', otherwise any emails sent from autohosting will still appear as spam.

Text: I had this crazy idea for a business venture, I wanted to open a burger joint with a twist. My friend suggested we get together with some of our college buddies who were also interested in opening their own place. So after months of planning and research, we finally decided to give it a shot.

We found a location, hired some employees (including myself), and started preparations for the grand opening. We set aside $20,000 towards advertising, packaged burgers, bought cookware, utensils, and other kitchen equipment. Everything seemed great until the night of the big event.

The weather turned nasty during the early evening, and rain poured down heavily throughout the entire dinner service. Our customers were drenched, hungry, and grumbling, but we didn’t care! It was our chance to prove ourselves. As soon as the first customer entered the restaurant, she exclaimed “Wow, these burgers taste amazing!” To her surprise, every single patty tasted like cheese, and each bun was covered in tomato sauce. She even asked us why they weren’t real cheeseburgers?

This prompted us to make some changes. Firstly, we switched to using fresh ground meat instead of pre-made patties. Secondly, we added more vegetables such as lettuce, tomatoes, and onions. Thirdly, we changed the seasonings to add spiciness without overpowering the flavors. Finally, we introduced a new menu item called the “Cheesy Chicken” which featured crispy chicken tenders dipped in melted cheese sauce. Customers loved it, and it became a huge hit.

After a few weeks, word spread quickly about our unique concept, and soon enough, we received orders pouring in. But things took a turn for the worse when we realized that our signature Cheesy Chicken item wasn’t selling well. We tried different variations, including different types of bread, cheeses, and seasonings, but nothing seemed to work.

Frustrated, we consulted with our suppliers and manufacturers, asking for feedback on what went wrong. After days of analyzing data and discussing ideas, we came across a major problem – the quality control measures in our supply chain. Supplies were arriving damaged, and food safety protocols weren’t followed. This led to contamination issues, which resulted in the loss of revenue and brand reputation.

Our team worked tirelessly to fix the issue, but it proved too challenging. With limited resources, we struggled to address the underlying problems and maintain our operations. Eventually, we reached out to our investors for financial assistance. They agreed, but only if we agreed to sell the company to them. Reluctant to hand over control, we accepted their offer. However, we regrettably had to close our doors forever.

In conclusion, starting a successful business can be incredibly rewarding, but it requires a significant amount of effort and sacrifice. Our journey taught us valuable lessons about managing risk, prioritizing tasks, dealing with obstacles, and staying resilient under pressure. Despite the setbacks, we learned that sometimes, the most unexpected events lead to the greatest opportunities.

As I stepped outside, I heard my wife's voice shouting at me from inside our house. I hesitated for a moment before walking towards her door. Text: My friend and I went to see a horror movie called 'The Conjuring'. We had been anticipating it since its release. It lived up to our expectations. At least until the climax scene when the demon possessed a child who tried to kill his mother.

I remember being horrified when the screen showed the demonic possession of a young girl. However, after watching the rest of the film, I realized that the child wasn't actually possessed by any demon. Instead, it was just a manifestation of a very strong desire inside him. The demon's presence only manifested itself because the little boy felt a need to possess something.

It took some explaining to convince my friend that what happened was more complicated than simply the demon possessing someone. But we eventually got past that argument. We realized that sometimes the real danger lies within ourselves rather than external forces.

That's why we always try to watch movies with captions. They can help us get a better understanding of how characters feel and think. And maybe even give us some insight into their motivations.
Output: This movie gave me nightmares and taught me that sometimes the true dangers lie within oneself.

Text: today I got hit by a bus. Not really hitting hard though. It only knocked me back slightly so I wasn't even able to see who hit me.

I think I may have been walking down the sidewalk when suddenly a bus came barreling towards me from the opposite direction. There was no warning, no chance to duck, nothing. Just a loud crash and bang followed immediately by silence.

My heart stopped. My brain registered what happened. Then I realized something horrible... I was standing on the curb, and there was no car parked nearby.

This realization sent shockwaves throughout my body. I tried to move away from the debris, but instead, I ended up getting pinned against the brick wall. That's how close I was to being run over.

It took some time for the paramedics to arrive, but eventually, I was taken to the hospital. When I woke up, I couldn't remember much about the incident. All I know is that I was lucky to make it out alive.

The aftermath of this event left me feeling vulnerable and helpless. For weeks afterwards, I struggled to come to terms with what had actually happened. But slowly, over time, I began to realize that life goes on regardless of whether or not we can control events. We just need to learn to accept them and find joy in whatever comes our way.

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email.

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: I recently discovered an interesting fact. Everyone knows what it means to say "I love you," yet nobody does.

This sentence has become popularly known as the Love Paragraph. However, it seems that nobody else can write it properly. Therefore, here's mine:

Love is the sound of birds chirping in the morning,
The rustling leaves underfoot, and the gentle breeze.
It's the warmth of sunshine on our faces,
And the taste of honey on our tongues.

We hold hands tight, as if we belong together forevermore,
With hearts full of love, so deep within us shines.
For those who know how to spell and punctuation,
This is surely a poem worthy of appreciation.

But alas, many fail miserably, unable to put these words down onto paper in any coherent manner. They start with "Love is..." and end up writing something more like "Awesome, awesome." But still, some find beauty in their work, and others simply scream obscenities at the world.

Those of you who can't quite grasp the concept of proper grammar may feel discouraged, but fear not! You too can make poetry. Here's another example:

There once lived a girl named Sarah,
Who loved nothing more than reading books.
She spent hours every day curled up on her bed,
Gazing at the ceiling and dreaming of adventure.

One night, she stumbled upon a bookstore,
Wherein she found a treasure trove beyond compare.
As she picked up each title, she felt her heart beat faster,
And imagined herself living out her wildest dreams.

Days turned into weeks, and soon Sarah realized,
That reading books wasn't just fun, but also a necessity.
Her eyes glittered with excitement as she read each page,
Hoping to meet someone special someday soon.

Inspired by this passion, she began to pen letters,
To anyone who might hear her voice, calling forth joyous tales.
Through her words, she hoped to reach far and wide,
And touch lives with her message of hope and love.

So begins Sarah's journey towards finding true love,
While always remembering to stay true to herself.
For in the midst of darkness, there lies light so bright,
Surrounded by the stars above, waiting to guide.

Input: Text: last thursday i was given the ultimate dare by my friends - let's call them x and z. both of them instructed me to walk into the middle of the middle of the hall and yell out "allahu akbar" at the top of my lungs. i did it twice that day.

the first time i did it i made sure there were no staff around. then i walked into the middle of the hall and yelled it out. everyone laughed while x and z instructed me to do it again; i promised them i would do it on the second lunch break.

cut to the second lunch break.

halfway through the break, they reminded me to do it. again, i made sure there were no staff around before i yelled it out, this time louder than last time.

this is where the fuck-up happens.

after i said it i saw a teacher. he was just out of my line of sight.

"fuck!" i thought. there's no way i'm gonna escape this.

"what have you succeeded in by doing that?" he says.

"um, offending several people?" i reply.

"yes. yes, you did. now i'm going to have to inform the your guidance counsellor about this. you do understand that, correct?"

it was at this moment that i knew i could weave my way out of the situation by just ratting on x and z.

luckily it worked. unluckily they don't want to talk to me ever again.
Output: acted like a suicide bomber in school, lost two friends in the process.

Input: Text: this happened either in the first or second week of school last semester. i had just gotten back from summer vacation and was excited to see all my college friends again, so naturally i went on about a week-long bender of getting piss drunk every night. following a long night at the bars i somehow made it back to my dorm and promptly passed out on the futon. now i should mention that i have an old george foreman grill that i use from time to time. it's a small dorm room so i have to keep it on the floor against the wall. so there i am sleeping soundly for a couple of hours before i woke up (still heavily under the influence) and had to use the restroom. i thought that i got up, walked out the door, down the hall, and into the bathroom to hose down the porcelain. however, as you might have guessed, that is not what happened. apparently, i got up, opened the electric grill, and relieved myself all over poor george as well as my wall. i don't have a roommate to confirm that is exactly what happened, but i quickly figured it out the next morning when i wanted to grill some breakfast sausage. 

in my defense the grill looks a lot like a toilet seat when it is closed.
Output: got drunk, urinated in a george foreman that i thought was a toilet

When we tried to pay for the bill, the clerk told us to go home and never come back. From there, we decided to head back to California, hoping that the memory of our failed attempt at pickpocketing wouldn't haunt us forever. outputs: Text: today I discovered something very interesting. It turns out that the most annoying person in the world is someone who always makes their own coffee. That sounds harmless enough until you realize that you can never get it right. This has been true since high school. My mom always insists on using instant, but I refuse because I know she will never measure correctly. Then, when I finally got my own kitchen I started making her coffee. At first I was really happy with how good it turned out. But after a few weeks I realized that I wasn't satisfied anymore. So I decided to try making it myself. After much trial and error I found that if I added milk and sugar I didn't need any extra coffee powder. Since then I make coffee almost every day. It's amazing how simple things like that can change our lives. Output: discovered that making your own coffee takes less effort than asking someone else to do it

outputs: Text: I can never remember who said this quote, but I think it was Mark Twain. It goes something like this: "The only true wisdom is in knowing you know nothing." This has been running through my head since yesterday afternoon. Whenever I find myself thinking about anything other than work, it feels like I am missing a piece of information. I try to make sense of things based solely on the fact that I cannot possibly know everything there is to know. But today I decided to challenge this belief with a newfound respect for ignorance. As I sat down to write this blog entry, I realized that I knew absolutely nothing about what I was writing about. That is why I love learning. It allows me to expand my knowledge base and gain perspective on topics I previously found boring. So instead of focusing on the topic at hand, I decided to focus on how much I learned today. What I discovered today was that life is too short to waste anytime feeling stupid. Output: finally felt free to pursue knowledge without fear

Text: I was driving down the highway when I heard an eerie silence from behind me. I looked back to see a man hanging himself from a tree. It took me a minute to realize what had happened. When I pulled over to check if anyone else was hurt, I found myself face to face with a cop who told me to pull over immediately. He asked why I didn't stop to help him. My heart raced as I realized how much my actions might have contributed to his death. That night, I went to bed feeling guilty for not stopping to help him.

I got up early the next morning, determined to find justice for the man whose life had been taken away. As I drove, I kept thinking about the incident. Everywhere I turned, someone seemed to know something about it. A friend even offered to give me advice on how to proceed. But as I approached the town where the man lived, I began to feel paranoid. Who knew? Maybe I wasn't meant to find peace in helping someone die. And maybe, too, the police officer wasn't wrong after all.

But then, something strange happened. I came across a small church. Inside, I saw a sign saying "Come forward and ask for forgiveness." I hesitated for a moment, wondering whether to try. Then, without warning, I felt a wave of guilt wash over me. For the first time since the incident, I stopped and listened to the words spoken by the priest. The man who had died hadn't done anything wrong. Instead, he had fallen victim to circumstance. The priest spoke of God's mercy, and of forgiveness. As I left the church, I felt a sense of relief wash over me. I knew that justice wouldn't come easily, but that didn't mean I couldn't offer forgiveness. Maybe, just maybe, my own mistake wasn't as terrible as I once thought.
Output: I learned the hard way that sometimes, things aren't always black and white.

Text: yesterday I met a guy who told me how much he loves me. It wasn't until today when I realized that he was only saying those words because he had already broken up with his girlfriend.

I felt like crying, but I didn't want to give him the satisfaction of seeing tears fall from my eyes. So instead, I asked him if he wanted to come over to mine tonight. He agreed.

We spent the night talking about our dreams, what we hoped to achieve, etc. But as soon as we got inside, something strange started happening. His hands were moving themselves! They weren't touching anything! I tried to stop him, but he kept on playing around.

Finally, after an hour of this weirdness, he turned to me and said, "Listen, Emily. I know this sounds crazy, but I love you." And he kissed me.

It was the most beautiful thing I've ever experienced.

Text: A man has been charged after police say he assaulted his wife during a domestic dispute in Adelaide's north.
Police allege Mark Andrew Johnson, 48, hit his wife Sarah Elizabeth Johnson, 39, multiple times in their home near Currie Street and Mawson Lakes roads on Saturday night.
He allegedly struck her in the head three times and once in the arm. She was taken to hospital in a serious condition.
The woman told police she had left the house because Mr Johnson was drinking heavily and becoming abusive.
She claims he punched her repeatedly when she went to intervene, knocking over furniture and causing injuries to herself.
Cops searched the property after receiving reports of a disturbance. They found a red Toyota Camry parked outside the house.
A woman who lived nearby claimed she heard screaming coming from inside the home earlier.
The woman, who cannot be named under state privacy laws, told news.com.au: "I heard shouting and banging. I think someone was fighting."
Mr Johnson appeared in court today via video link from Port Pirie Police Station, dressed in a blue prison jumpsuit. He pleaded not guilty to charges including grievous bodily harm, common assault and family violence occasioning actual bodily harm.
Defence barrister Michael McMahon said his client suffered from depression and anxiety and had sought help for alcohol addiction since December 2016.
He said Mr Johnson had received medication to treat his mental health issues, but stopped taking it recently due to financial difficulties.
McMahon argued Mr Johnson believed his wife was cheating on him and needed protection.
Justice Paul Flynn granted a non-parole period of six months for the 54-year-old, saying he showed signs of rehabilitation.
Judge Flynn warned Mr Johnson against reoffending and urged the community to support his recovery.

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

outputs: Text: I used to work at an office that used to send their employees to conferences all the time. This meant I would spend hours every weekend attending meetings and presentations. It also means that whenever someone wanted to hang out with me during the conference season, I would always end up being busy. One such person who tried to take advantage of my schedule was my coworker. He would often show up at our coffee breaks with drinks and snacks (I was never allowed anything other than water) and try to start conversations with me. At first, I would politely decline his offer, telling him that I had things to attend to. But eventually, I couldn't keep denying myself these moments of human interaction. We struck up a conversation and soon became close friends. Our friendship continued even though I stopped attending most of the company's events because of my workload. Output: it's good to know that some companies recognize the value of human connection despite the demands of the job.

Text: i recently read an article about a guy who died because his wife was diagnosed with breast cancer. I cried my eyes out reading it. I know what happened next will sound ridiculous, but I couldn't help myself. I went online and searched "how to die from breast cancer." This brought back memories of all the times I wanted to quit smoking (which led to a lung cancer diagnosis) and also some bad experiences with heart disease. It makes me wonder if maybe death isn't such a bad thing.

I spent most of yesterday afternoon browsing sites about dying and death, hoping someone might have something helpful to share. But nobody seemed to think I was crazy. One site even suggested I check out "deathbed confessions," which sounds like an awful lot of material for a blog post. So instead, I wrote down everything I felt I needed to say. And then I posted it here.

It's not a comprehensive guide, but hopefully it helps someone else feel less alone in their struggles. If you're interested, please feel free to leave comments below. I can only imagine how many other people feel the same way I do.

Text: I am a scientist from the future, here to tell you how to survive in our world.
You might think this sounds funny, but hear me out. Our planet has been ravaged by a massive asteroid, leaving us all vulnerable to radiation poisoning. It’s not only dangerous for humans, but animals and plants alike. We need to find ways to adapt quickly to save ourselves. This means getting creative and inventing new technologies. Here’s how you can help:
1) Create a self-contained shelter. This is crucial since many areas will be affected by the radiation. Build a large structure using materials such as metal sheets, plastic bags, cardboard boxes, and anything else you can get your hands on. Make sure it has good insulation and ventilation.
2) Grow food indoors. Many crops can tolerate low levels of radiation. Try growing herbs, vegetables, and fruit. You can also use LED lights to grow plants indoors.
3) Develop medical equipment. We won’t have access to hospitals or clinics until after the crisis. Start collecting supplies and developing medical devices to keep yourself alive. Some ideas include making homemade bandages, sterilizing water and disinfectants, and creating portable oxygen tanks.
4) Find alternative sources of energy. As mentioned earlier, solar power may not work due to the amount of radiation present. Consider building wind turbines, geothermal heat pumps, or even small hydroelectric generators.
5) Communication tools. Keep communication channels open between different regions. Use satellite phones, radio broadcasts, or other forms of technology to connect people.
6) Defense mechanisms. Protect yourself against radiation exposure by building shields, wearing radiation-blocking clothing, and keeping yourself hydrated. If possible, wear sunscreen to avoid excessive UV damage.
7) Don’t forget basic hygiene. A clean environment is essential for maintaining healthy living conditions. Wash your hands regularly, brush your teeth, and take regular showers.
8) Stay informed. Listen to news reports and research updates from reputable organizations. Be prepared to act fast when necessary.
9) Prepare your loved ones. Let them know what you plan to do and ask them to prepare accordingly. Share resources and information.

Text: This year, I decided to go all out on the Halloween costume theme. My favorite movie is Scream, so I had to dress up as Ghostface.
I started off with a white tuxedo jacket from Old Navy, black skinny jeans from H&M, and a red bandana necklace from Target.
The shoes were a pair of classic slip-on black boots that I found at Walmart.
Finally, I added my signature hairstyle – pigtails. They weren’t perfect, but they looked good enough to eat.

As soon as I arrived at the party, my dad noticed my new attire and asked what happened.
“Oh, it’s nothing,” I told him. “Just getting dressed.”
But when I walked towards the dance floor, things took a turn for the worse. A group of teens suddenly lunged toward me, brandishing scissors.
Suddenly, I realized that my mask wasn’t covering my face properly. Blood spilled everywhere. It was clear that someone else had been playing pranks on me.
My heart raced as I ran away from the scene. Panic set in, and I began to panic. But, I couldn’t leave without telling anyone what had happened.
Without thinking, I pulled out my phone and called my best friend, Lila.
She answered right away, her voice calm and composed.
“Hey, Emily. What’s wrong?” she asked.

“It looks like I got attacked by some trick-or-treaters,” I replied, trying to keep my composure.
Lila listened intently, nodding slowly.
“That sounds serious,” she said finally.

“What do you mean? Did any of those kids hurt you?” I asked, hoping to get some clarity.

“No, Emily. None of them even tried to touch you. But, they definitely left their mark on you. You look…disorientated,” she said softly.

I felt tears streaming down my face. How could these guys think that would be funny?

We talked for a few minutes longer, sharing our fears and worries. We both knew that we needed to report the incident to authorities.

After that night, I stopped practicing my trick-or-treat routine. Every year, I kept waiting for someone to try and harm me. And every year, I was relieved to find out that nobody had actually done anything to me.

Output: Got attacked by trick-or-treater(s), disoriented after being hit, reported to police

However, after arriving in town, we realized that we couldn’t find any archery targets. After asking around town, we finally found an archery range near us. We arrived early enough to shoot before the competition starts, but unfortunately, they ran out of arrows. Luckily, we had brought extra sets of arrows from home!

We decided to go to the store nearby to pick up more arrows since we wouldn’t need them for the actual competition. As we were walking back to the archery range, Sarah noticed something strange. A group of teenagers were standing outside the entrance, watching us enter. When we turned around, we saw them pointing guns at us. They seemed angry because we weren’t wearing our helmets, even though we had asked for them earlier during registration.

To our surprise, they let us pass without causing trouble. Once inside, we immediately set up our equipment and began practicing. Our first event was discus throw, and we performed extremely well. outputs: Text: I had an accidental encounter with a clown yesterday afternoon when I was trying to get home after work. It wasn't exactly what I expected, but I guess it's better than getting mugged? Anyway, I remember looking up and seeing this little clown standing outside the building. He seemed pretty friendly enough, and since I couldn't really say anything back to him (I was already late), I just smiled and kept walking. Then...he started dancing around in front of me. At first, I thought maybe he wanted to dance with me, but nope, he was more interested in making faces at his reflection in the window. After some awkward silence, I turned around to see if anyone else was around, and lo and behold, there was another clown sitting in the shadows. Weirdly enough, all three of us were dressed similarly, so I figured it might be a prank. Well, turns out it wasn't. One of the clowns grabbed me by the arm and led me down the alley behind the building. Apparently, this was our way of escaping the cops who were probably waiting for us somewhere nearby. We ran for about five minutes until we reached a park across the street. There, we split up and went our separate ways. My heart was pounding so hard I could barely breathe, but somehow I managed to keep running towards the exit. As soon as I emerged onto the sidewalk, I collapsed to the ground, feeling like a complete idiot. That whole experience left a mark on me, though. I realized how much I take things for granted, especially ones like this. Maybe someday someone will make a real life clown prank movie, and I won't feel so bad anymore.

Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Input:
outputs: Text: This story takes place during a raging thunderstorm, with lightning flashes crackling overhead. A group of five friends were camping out in a tent near the edge of a dense forest. Suddenly, a loud boom shook the ground, followed by several minutes of deafening silence. As the storm subsided, the rain started falling harder than ever before. The five friends decided to venture outside and explore their surroundings. But then, something strange began happening. The trees started swaying violently, as though they were alive and reacting to the wind. The air grew thick with moisture, and suddenly, a swarm of mosquitoes descended upon them. They shrieked and ran inside, clutching each other tightly. "What the hell?" muttered the leader, looking at his friends. They looked equally perplexed. "I think we need to leave," he said finally. "But where? We can barely even walk." "We can try the nearest trailhead," suggested the smallest friend, a young girl who wore bright yellow sunscreen. The others agreed, but as they walked deeper into the woods, the mosquitos became more numerous, more aggressive. They stopped, frantically searching for a way out. "This isn't working," said the leader. He took out his phone and dialed 911. Within moments, the emergency services arrived, led by a uniformed officer who introduced himself as Lieutenant Johnson. "Are you okay?" asked Johnson, inspecting the group carefully. "Yes," replied the leader, nodding firmly. "Thank you for calling us, sir." "You know what I mean," snapped the lieutenant, glaring at the three teenagers. "Come on!" yelled the leader, grabbing his arm. "We're doing alright, thanks." "Alright" repeated the lieutenant, scowling at the group. "Let's go," he ordered, leading the way through the trees. By the time they reached the clearing, the mosquitoes had retreated into hiding places. The sun beat down mercilessly, making everything look gray and ominous. There was no water nearby, and the air felt heavy and humid. "It seems like we've been walking forever," remarked the leader, tugging at his collar. "Maybe we should turn back," suggested the smallest friend. "No," said the leader, taking a deep breath. "Not yet. Let's push forward." And they pushed, slowly but surely. After what seemed like hours, they stumbled across a small stream. "Drink!" cried the oldest friend, reaching for a bottle lying beside the water. It was filled with muddy brown water, but they drank anyway. "That'll do us right," exclaimed the leader, holding out his hand. "And thank you kindly," added the smallest friend, smiling broadly. Soon enough, they came upon another clearing, this one larger and brighter. "Is this it?" whispered the leader, pointing towards a tall tree. "Looks like it." They climbed the tree, which gave them excellent views of the surrounding countryside. From above, they could see the entire valley spread out below them, with mountains towering in the distance. "Wow," breathed the leader, gazing down at the scene. "The view from here is truly magnificent." "Yeah," chimed in the smallest friend, admiring the scenery too. "Just wish we could stay here for longer." But soon enough, they heard the sounds of cars approaching. "Quick, let's get moving," shouted the leader, pushing his companions towards the entrance. They stumbled onto the main road, dodged traffic, and continued onwards until they found themselves lost in a sprawling metropolis. They searched high and low, but could find nothing to guide them. "We may never make it back to our campsite," groaned the leader, pulling out his map. "Fine," replied the smallest friend, shrugging. "Then let's just head straight to the police station." And so they did, heading towards the only visible building on the horizon. When they finally entered the city gates, they realized they had traveled far beyond their comfort zone. Everywhere they turned, they saw signs warning them of dangerous wildlife and poisonous plants. "Why didn't anyone warn us?" gasped the leader, peering at a sign advertising a local zoo. "Well, we assumed it would be safe since it wasn't open yet," explained the smallest friend, grimacing. "Stupid assumption." The group pressed on, determined to reach their destination. Eventually, after what felt like an eternity, they spotted the familiar outline of their campsite. They gathered their things and set out once more, hoping to avoid further disasters along the way. Along the way, they encountered a number of obstacles, including steep hills, treacherous bridges, and unfriendly locals. One particularly grueling stretch involved navigating a maze of narrow streets lined with decrepit buildings. At times, they almost fell victim to gang violence, but they held together and fought bravely. Finally, after what felt like an eternity, they burst through the doors of their campsite, relieved and exhausted. They settled into their makeshift shelter, grateful to be safe and dry. That evening, they sat around the fire pit, sharing stories and drinking warm tea. They talked about their hopes and dreams for the future, and promised to support each other no matter what challenges arose. For the first time in weeks, they felt hopeful. Maybe, just maybe, they weren't completely alone.

Input: Text: this happened either in the first or second week of school last semester. i had just gotten back from summer vacation and was excited to see all my college friends again, so naturally i went on about a week-long bender of getting piss drunk every night. following a long night at the bars i somehow made it back to my dorm and promptly passed out on the futon. now i should mention that i have an old george foreman grill that i use from time to time. it's a small dorm room so i have to keep it on the floor against the wall. so there i am sleeping soundly for a couple of hours before i woke up (still heavily under the influence) and had to use the restroom. i thought that i got up, walked out the door, down the hall, and into the bathroom to hose down the porcelain. however, as you might have guessed, that is not what happened. apparently, i got up, opened the electric grill, and relieved myself all over poor george as well as my wall. i don't have a roommate to confirm that is exactly what happened, but i quickly figured it out the next morning when i wanted to grill some breakfast sausage. 

in my defense the grill looks a lot like a toilet seat when it is closed.
Output: got drunk, urinated in a george foreman that i thought was a toilet

Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Text: I have always been fascinated by aliens since childhood. It started when I saw the movie "E.T." My mom would take me to watch movies whenever she could. She even let me stay up late to watch "Close Encounters of the Third Kind" and "The Andromeda Strain". So after watching those films, I became obsessed with anything related to extraterrestrial life.

I remember vividly sitting on my bed reading books such as "Contact," "Ascension," and "Flying Saucers Over the Bottomless Pit." This led me to think that perhaps we were not alone in the universe. As I grew older, I found myself more interested in the subject matter than just wanting to believe in alien abductions. I began studying astronomy, astrophysics, and cosmology in high school.

In college, I took classes in theoretical physics and astronomy. However, these subjects didn’t interest me nearly as much as space exploration. During my junior year, I decided to attend a science fiction convention in San Francisco called "Worldcon." At this event, I met many people who shared similar interests as mine. These individuals helped me become more involved in space exploration through their enthusiasm and knowledge. They introduced me to the International Astronautical Congress (IAC), which brought together scientists and engineers working towards space exploration projects. After attending several conferences and workshops, I realized that becoming an astronaut wasn’t enough for me; I needed to learn more about the technical aspects of space travel.

As I continued pursuing my passion for space exploration, I discovered that the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) offered internships and scholarship opportunities. After completing my application process, I received acceptance letters from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the Ames Research Center. Both institutions provide valuable research experience in fields such as engineering, robotics, computer programming, and data analysis.

After receiving acceptance into both organizations, I spent six months conducting fieldwork and experimentation at JPL. Throughout my time at JPL, I learned everything from basic mechanical engineering to complex software development. While conducting experiments, I encountered numerous challenges, including unforeseen failures and unexpected setbacks. Nevertheless, I persevered, learning new skills along the way.

One of the most significant experiences during my internship was designing and building a Mars rover simulator using Unity. With support from JPL, I created a replica of a Mars Rover with sensors and cameras designed to simulate driving on Mars. Using the simulator, I tested different features of the rover, analyzed data collected during simulations, and improved upon the rover’s functionality.

During my final project, I developed a program that allowed users to input information about potential landing sites on Mars and then analyze the probability of successfully reaching them based on factors such as wind speed, atmospheric pressure, and distance from the surface. This program also included a visualization tool that showed the user where the Mars Rover would land based on its trajectory.

This summer, I will begin training for my first mission to Mars. Despite the daunting challenge ahead, I feel confident in my ability to succeed because of the knowledge and expertise gained throughout my internship and previous experience.

Input: Text: tifu. i was in line at the gas station, waiting to pay for my soda and gas, when i saw a quarter on the packs of gum directly in front of the counter. when it was my turn to pay i bent over and scooped up the quarter, and put it in my pocket, forgetting about it instantly. putting my soda on the counter and reaching for my wallet, i looked up and saw the cashier eyeing me with an angry glare. i was confused by this. was she mad at my choice of soda? (she could be one of those freaks that prefer pepsi) did i have an offensive t shirt on? (not unless she's offended by my obscure podcast shirt) 

i say "......$40 on 2 please." and she responds with "what's in your pocket?" 

"huh?" i stammer before finally understanding. "oh! i didn't steal anything!" and proceed to fervently pull everything out of my pockets, dropping change, and other things. i pick up the 25 cent culprit and thrust it to the cashier, as if it proved my story somehow, and explained that i had just seen the quarter on the gum and nabbed it.

 her face hadn't changed at all during the entire exchange. she finally just completed my transaction and said have a nice day. i'm not sure if she believed me or not, but i gathered all my stuff and hightailed it out of there.
Output: i found a quarter on a display of gum, cashier thought i was blatantly stealing gum right in front of her.

outputs: Text: today I discovered that my phone has a feature called "do not disturb". This means that whenever I want to talk to someone, I have to manually unlock the screen and then press the button on the side of the phone. So far, this has been a big problem because I can only get messages while I'm walking around campus. For example, I was trying to call a friend who lives close by, but I accidentally dialed his number instead of hers. When I realized this, I tried calling him several times without success. Finally, after standing there for what felt like forever, I gave up and started running towards home. That was until I heard the familiar ring tone of my mom's phone. It turns out that my phone had automatically turned itself off when I locked the screen. And since I couldn't reach her anyway, I decided to wait outside for her to come home. After about half an hour, I finally caught sight of her car parked across the street. I ran inside and asked her where she was going. She told me that she was at work, and that her supervisor would probably be happy to hear about my exciting adventures. But I wasn't really interested in hearing about any such thing. Instead, I took advantage of the fact that she was gone to go check out a new coffee shop nearby. I waited for a few minutes before deciding to try the place out, even though I knew that it wouldn't do much good considering how crowded it was. However, as soon as I sat down, I noticed something strange happening. My headphones were plugged into the earbud jack on the left side of the table. At first, I thought that they had fallen out somewhere along the way. Then, as I reached for them, I realized that they weren't actually connected to anything. They seemed to be stuck on their own endless loop. Eventually, I managed to break free from the cycle and set them aside. While I was still trying to figure out why they weren't working, a young woman approached our table. Her name tag read "Maria", and she introduced herself as the owner of the coffee shop. Maria listened patiently as I described my situation, asking questions and offering advice. As we talked, I learned that the coffee machine in the back of the store was broken, and that I needed to take the headphones to the service desk. Maria helped me find the service desk, and once I showed her my plastic card, she handed me a keycard to access the machines. With Maria's help, I was able to fix the coffee maker and get back to talking to my friend. Even better than that, I also received a complimentary cup of coffee from Maria, which made my trip even more enjoyable. Output: I was sitting alone at a coffee shop, trying to fix a faulty coffee machine, when a friendly barista came up to me and offered me a free cup of coffee.

Text: I used to love watching the news. It was something that kept me company while doing homework, or reading books. Nowadays though, I find it very difficult to watch. There seems to be no end to these stories of violence and terrorism. All the talk shows seem to focus more on how bad our government is than how much worse we are. Everyone talks about the economy, but never mentions how bad things were before they even started. And who wants to hear about another school shooting when there are already enough horror stories happening in our own country? 

I decided to write my own version of a news report. Here it goes...

[INTRODUCTION]

(The camera zooms in on a young man sitting alone in his living room, staring blankly ahead.)

Narrator: Welcome to the world of the news. A place where tragedy reigns supreme, where people are driven to madness by events beyond their control. Today, let us take a closer look at some recent headlines. [SCENE OPENS WITH INTIMATE FAMILY VIDEO OF MOTHER AND SON IN THEIR HOME.]

Mother: Hey son, do you want to come along with me for dinner tonight?

Son: Yes mom, thanks.

Mom: Great, we're going to the grocery store.

They walk outside together. They stop at a convenience store. Mother buys food and Son decides to buy himself a new pair of shoes. He returns inside. His mother asks him why he needs shoes. Son: Just because I can afford them. Mother: Shoes aren't worth the money. You need clothes, and then maybe you can get a job sometime.

[INTRODUCING NEWS ANCHOR ON SCREEN]

News Anchor: Hello everyone. Welcome back to our live broadcast. We have been covering the aftermath of the massacre in Newtown, Connecticut. As you know, six children lost their lives today. The families of the victims are still struggling to cope with such a terrible loss. We spoke to one family earlier today. Their name is Rachel, and she lost her little boy Alex yesterday. She told us, "It's like someone took away our child. We will always miss him." [SCENE CLOSES WITH LIVE REPORT FROM NEW YORK CITY].

New York City News Reporter: Last night, a gunman entered a busy subway train, killing eight innocent passengers and injuring thirty others. This horrific incident has left many wondering whether America is ready for a war on terror. Police Chief Bill Bratton addressed the media saying, "We are seeing the worst kind of terrorist attack possible. These shootings are designed to cause maximum destruction and death." [SCENE OPENS WITH POLICE CHIEF BRATTON WALKING INTO OFFICES AT HQ.]

Police Chief Bratton: Good afternoon, everyone. We have received several reports of suspicious activity around the city. We believe that these incidents may be related to terrorists seeking to carry out attacks here. We encourage anyone with information regarding these matters to contact us immediately. [POLICE OFFICER TAKES NOTES AS HE CONVERTS NUMBER TO DIRECTED ENQUIRY CODE.]

Directed Enquiry Code: What is the number for the police department?

Police Officer: [Replies:] That would be (phone number). Thank you for calling the NYPD Emergency Services Unit.

[FADE OUT]

Conclusion: As we approach the final moments of this series, it becomes clear that these tragic events have only brought greater awareness to the issues facing our society. But it also underscores the fact that, despite the best efforts of law enforcement agencies, it remains a dangerous world filled with unpredictable danger.

Text: This is probably the worst part of being a writer. I always feel like I could write something better than the stuff I already have written. Sometimes it's frustrating, sometimes it's exhilarating. But mostly it's just exhausting. So when someone asks me how much longer until they publish a novel, I say "it depends" and take a deep breath.

This sentence comes from a recent conversation with my agent, who told me she'd love to read my latest manuscript. I can't wait to hear her thoughts. And yet here I sit, staring at my laptop screen, typing away. It feels good to put pen to paper - especially since I wrote the last few pages in half an hour yesterday afternoon - but I'm sure I'll end up deleting them soon. Maybe tomorrow. Or maybe never. I think this story idea has legs, but only time will tell whether anyone else does too.

As I mentioned earlier, writing takes a certain amount of discipline. You have to set aside time each day to put your ideas onto paper. That means finding moments throughout the day when you won't be interrupted by family members, colleagues, or anything else. Even when you're tired or feeling unmotivated, it's important to push through those feelings and finish the damn thing. There's no substitute for hard work.

But I'm also learning that perseverance isn't just about sticking with a project. It's also about recognizing that writing isn't always easy. Sometimes it's tough. Sometimes it's slow. Sometimes it feels like nothing is happening. But even when things aren't working out perfectly, I still believe in this story. And that keeps me going.

I hope you enjoyed reading this draft. If you'd like to help support me further, consider purchasing a copy of my novel. My publisher is offering discounts right now for early bird readers. Just click here and enter code EARLYBIRD18. Thank you so much for your continued support!

Text: I've been struggling with my mental health lately, and sometimes I feel like I can't take any more. It feels like no matter how much I try, nothing seems to change. Sometimes I even question whether I'm worth living.

My therapist suggested talking through these feelings with someone else who understands them. So I reached out to a friend, and she listened patiently while I poured my heart out. We talked about our struggles and how they affect us both emotionally and physically. It felt good to finally share something so personal with someone.

Afterwards, I realized how much better I felt after sharing those thoughts with her. And I knew I needed to reach out to others too. So I asked my coworkers if they minded if I shared some things I was dealing with personally. They said yes, and that's how this group started. We talk about everything - love, loss, successes, failures, and everything in between. There's always someone willing to listen and offer support.

It's taken some time to build relationships within this community, but it has become incredibly important to me. Having people who care about me and who can relate to my experiences has helped me heal and grow as a person. My therapy sessions have taught me that everyone goes through tough times, and that having a support system can make all the difference.

I hope this helps illustrate the power of connecting with others who understand your struggles. Let's continue building connections and finding ways to help each other thrive.

Input: Text: this happened either in the first or second week of school last semester. i had just gotten back from summer vacation and was excited to see all my college friends again, so naturally i went on about a week-long bender of getting piss drunk every night. following a long night at the bars i somehow made it back to my dorm and promptly passed out on the futon. now i should mention that i have an old george foreman grill that i use from time to time. it's a small dorm room so i have to keep it on the floor against the wall. so there i am sleeping soundly for a couple of hours before i woke up (still heavily under the influence) and had to use the restroom. i thought that i got up, walked out the door, down the hall, and into the bathroom to hose down the porcelain. however, as you might have guessed, that is not what happened. apparently, i got up, opened the electric grill, and relieved myself all over poor george as well as my wall. i don't have a roommate to confirm that is exactly what happened, but i quickly figured it out the next morning when i wanted to grill some breakfast sausage. 

in my defense the grill looks a lot like a toilet seat when it is closed.
Output: got drunk, urinated in a george foreman that i thought was a toilet

Input: Text: this actually happened about 20 minutes ago? so yes, today. (do i get bonus points?)

my hair is currently down to my waist and obviously quite long. i keep putting off getting it cut though, because i haven't found a stylist in my area that i trust enough, so now it's at the point where i'll likely donate a chunk of it and get it styled, because it's so long.

i, also, currently hate my job and have a job interview on monday, go me! so of course to look more professional, i wanted to get my hair cut before then. (do you know where this is going? of course you do.)

so i'm in the office, sitting at my desk/open cubicle thing, and find a local place to call and try to find an appointment:

***
_m: "hi, i was wondering if you had an appointments available for saturday."_


_salon: "unfortunately we're all booked up, is there another day that would work for you?_


_m: "no, i work during the day [their hours are 9-5 on weekdays], and **i have a job interview on monday**, so i need to get it cut before then._
***
said in full earshot 

of multiple other employees. 

all the color drained from my face as the words were leaving my mouth. 

i've been looking for a job for months, but that doesn't mean i want to lose my current job before getting a new one...
Output: trying to get my hair cut. might actually be getting my job cut.**

Input: Text: obligatory comment about this not actually happening today, and this being a throwaway account.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: "the worst day ever."

I remember clearly the way I felt when I received this note - heartbroken, confused, and completely lost. It wasn't until I started digging through my memories and trying to make sense of things did I realize just how horrible that day really was. At the time, I couldn't quite put my finger on why I was feeling so terrible; maybe it was because I had just broken up with someone close to me, or maybe it was because I had just found out that my father had died unexpectedly. But whatever the reason, something inside of me snapped, and suddenly, I knew that I needed to do something to help others who were suffering similarly.

Over the coming days and weeks, I spent countless hours pouring over medical journals and conducting research on mental health issues. I learned about trauma, depression, anxiety, and other conditions that could lead to such a devastating reaction. I also discovered that many people who suffered these kinds of emotional injuries often struggled with feelings of shame, guilt, and self-blame. These negative thoughts were almost always fueled by the fear that they would suffer another breakup, loss, or tragedy in the future.

It wasn't easy, but I eventually came across a therapist who specializes in helping individuals struggling with traumatic events. Together we worked hard to identify the root causes of my own pain and build coping strategies to manage them. Over time, those techniques became part of my daily routine, and I began to feel more confident and empowered than I had in years.

As for the specific event itself, it took place during a particularly difficult period in my personal life. I had recently turned thirty and was starting to experience some significant changes in my relationships and career goals. However, despite my best efforts, I still found myself constantly comparing myself to others around me. This led to a spiral of negativity and hopelessness that ultimately resulted in a full-blown panic attack.

Throughout the healing process, I found solace in the knowledge that I was far from alone. Many people face similar challenges, and there is no shame in seeking support when you need it most. Even though the road ahead may seem daunting, know that you are not alone, and that there is hope for a brighter tomorrow.
