Input: Text: last thursday i was given the ultimate dare by my friends - let's call them x and z. both of them instructed me to walk into the middle of the middle of the hall and yell out "allahu akbar" at the top of my lungs. i did it twice that day.

the first time i did it i made sure there were no staff around. then i walked into the middle of the hall and yelled it out. everyone laughed while x and z instructed me to do it again; i promised them i would do it on the second lunch break.

cut to the second lunch break.

halfway through the break, they reminded me to do it. again, i made sure there were no staff around before i yelled it out, this time louder than last time.

this is where the fuck-up happens.

after i said it i saw a teacher. he was just out of my line of sight.

"fuck!" i thought. there's no way i'm gonna escape this.

"what have you succeeded in by doing that?" he says.

"um, offending several people?" i reply.

"yes. yes, you did. now i'm going to have to inform the your guidance counsellor about this. you do understand that, correct?"

it was at this moment that i knew i could weave my way out of the situation by just ratting on x and z.

luckily it worked. unluckily they don't want to talk to me ever again.
Output: acted like a suicide bomber in school, lost two friends in the process.

Text: I recently moved into a new house with three other roommates. We live together pretty much all year round, except during winter break. It’s always funny when our cat gets stuck inside because she can’t get outside without using the bathroom.

One evening after dinner, we decided to take turns playing “cat-and-mouse” with her. This involves pretend-playing like cats play – chasing each other, clawing each other, etc. And then finally catching each other.

The game started fine until our cat decided to climb onto the bed. She has never done this before, so we were a bit taken aback. But then she suddenly jumped off the bed and began crawling towards the closet.

We didn’t know if she meant to go to the bathroom or not. So we all followed suit, thinking maybe she’d accidentally step on something. After about five minutes of watching her try to find a spot to pee, we realized she wasn’t coming back anytime soon.

So we turned around and headed to the kitchen to make dinner. As we sat at the table, our cat came bounding up to us, looking around frantically.

“Oh! Oh!” she exclaimed, running up to us and trying to sit on the chair. “I found something interesting!”

She reached into her mouth and pulled out…a whole bag of flour.

“What?” we asked, confused.

Our cat explained that she had been hiding behind the cupboard in search of something edible.

And then she proceeded to eat the entire bag of flour.

It took about ten seconds for us to realize what had just occurred.

“Well, that was unexpected,” I joked.

But really, it was just another example of how our cat seems to be able to solve problems whenever she wants.

Input: Text: this happened either in the first or second week of school last semester. i had just gotten back from summer vacation and was excited to see all my college friends again, so naturally i went on about a week-long bender of getting piss drunk every night. following a long night at the bars i somehow made it back to my dorm and promptly passed out on the futon. now i should mention that i have an old george foreman grill that i use from time to time. it's a small dorm room so i have to keep it on the floor against the wall. so there i am sleeping soundly for a couple of hours before i woke up (still heavily under the influence) and had to use the restroom. i thought that i got up, walked out the door, down the hall, and into the bathroom to hose down the porcelain. however, as you might have guessed, that is not what happened. apparently, i got up, opened the electric grill, and relieved myself all over poor george as well as my wall. i don't have a roommate to confirm that is exactly what happened, but i quickly figured it out the next morning when i wanted to grill some breakfast sausage. 

in my defense the grill looks a lot like a toilet seat when it is closed.
Output: got drunk, urinated in a george foreman that i thought was a toilet

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: I canceled my cable service because I decided to try watching Netflix instead.

It took me a while to figure out how to set it up, but once I did, I couldn't believe how easy it was. It's also been amazingly affordable compared to paying for cable!

I used to watch TV religiously, but the commercials were driving me crazy, and I always felt like I missed out on something by having them. Now, I just go through episodes whenever I feel like it without even bothering to check the channel guide anymore.

I also love being able to skip ads whenever they come on. It makes the whole viewing experience much faster and more enjoyable. Plus, I never miss a single episode!

The only thing I miss is sports programming, but that's okay too. There are plenty of other shows out there that are equally entertaining. And who needs sports anyway? They suck for most people.

In conclusion, switching to streaming has been a game changer for me. I've saved hundreds of dollars each month and I no longer feel guilty about watching TV. Plus, I've discovered new shows and movies that I wouldn't have otherwise seen. It's a win-win!

outputs: Text: I recently took a trip to canada with my family where we visited several museums including the canadian national museum of immigration history. During our visit to the museum, I stumbled upon a painting depicting a man holding a sign reading "I hate being Canadian." As someone who has lived in Canada his entire life, I couldn't help but feel embarrassed by this statement. However, instead of trying to defend my identity, I decided to take a deep breath and simply enjoy the exhibits while keeping the conversation positive. After much reflection, I realized that I shouldn't be ashamed of where I come from. Being Canadian isn't something to hide or pretend is all right. It is who we are, whether we admit it or not. So I decided to share this experience with my mom during dinner that evening. She laughed and told me that she always knew Canadians were proud of their country. I nodded in agreement and said that I couldn't agree more. It's moments like these that remind us that even though our background may differ, our shared experiences bring us together.

Input: Text: well, a little context. i´m the kind of boy who needs to make experiments, to push a little the limits and i can´t stay without making something too much time.
a friend came with the idea of rockets : dude, i got this really cool project, we need household items and it´s going to be awesome!
we gather the materials, make the mix, cook it and burned it. it was awesome as he said and we make it like 3 times that day.
by this point he tells me that the mix can be used as fuel for rockets.
sooooo, this morning i just wanted to make some fuel. mix the ingredients, ready to cook in my kitchen.
maybe some glasses to look more professional? ok, lets do it.
so, there´s me, heating an inflamable mix.
then, it happens. a huge flame in front of my eyes. i move back and protect me, but it was instantly gone. the smoke covered everything, so i went outside to cough a little when my sister saw me. burned hair, the glasses were black, as my nose and forehead. my hand suffered the most and the house was filled with smoke (wich i didn´t know if it was toxic or not).

outputs:
Text: I recently started working part-time while going to college full-time. One day, I decided to go out with some coworkers after work. As soon as we arrived at a bar, everyone ordered drinks and began chatting. I noticed one of my coworkers sitting alone at a corner booth. After a few moments, she approached us, looking lost. "Excuse me," she said, "do you know where the bathrooms are?" Everyone looked around, trying to find the nearest bathroom. Finally, someone spotted a nearby convenience store and suggested we head inside. We followed her directions, only to realize too late that we had entered a different building entirely. There was no signage indicating the entrance to the bathroom. All of us ended up walking aimlessly through the parking lot until we finally stumbled upon a gas station across the street. Once inside, we found ourselves facing a locked door with a sign reading "no smoking." This was obviously a problem since we were all dressed professionally. Our coworker tried to open the door using a key card, but it wouldn't budge. She then reached behind herself and pulled out a pair of scissors. With a deft motion, she cut the lock off the door. At this point, we all burst out laughing, feeling silly for being caught in such a ridiculous predicament.

In my defense, I think the fact that we were dressed professionally helped make the situation seem less absurd.

Text: I recently discovered the joy of making my own soap. It has been quite the learning experience. Here is a simple recipe for homemade lavender and tea tree soap using olive oil, coconut oil, aloe vera gel, and essential oils. Ingredients:
- 8 oz Olive oil
- 5 oz Coconut oil
- 10 drops Lavender Essential Oil
- 6 drops Tea Tree Essential Oil
- Alcohol (optional)

Instructions:
1. Melt the coconut oil in a double boiler until fully melted. Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
2. Add the olive oil and stir to combine. This will help create a lighter consistency.
3. Stir in the lavender and tea tree essentials oils.
4. Pour the mixture onto a sheet pan lined with parchment paper. Spread the soap out in thin layers.
5. Allow the soap to solidify completely. Once hardened, remove the sheets from the pan.
6. Clean your work surface thoroughly after handling the soap.
7. Lather the soap by pouring warm water into a bowl and placing the soap in the water. Let sit for a few minutes while the soap melts and forms bubbles.
8. Gently massage the soap into your skin. Be careful not to scrub too vigorously or burn yourself.
9. Rinse the soap off with warm water and pat dry with a clean towel. Store any leftover soap in a sealed container.

This soap smells divine! And it’s super easy to make. Happy DIYing!

outputs: Text: I was driving home from work tonight and realized that I had forgotten my wallet. I had no other way to pay for gas because I didn’t have enough money. So I decided to stop by Walmart to buy a new wallet. When I arrived, I noticed that their parking lot was completely empty! There were no cars, no people walking towards the store. It looked like nobody would ever come inside Walmart again. So I started looking for something else to do until I remembered that I forgot my wallet. I took out my phone and searched for directions to Walmart using Google Maps. I turned onto Main Street and saw the Walmart sign. As soon as I entered the parking lot, I immediately saw that the whole place was full of people. Everyone was waiting patiently for their turn to shop. It was crazy. So I walked around and tried to find something interesting to do, anything that wouldn’t involve buying stuff. Finally, I found an old lady sitting alone in a booth eating her lunch. She wasn’t really interested in talking to anyone, but I could tell that she was lonely. I sat down across from her and asked if she needed help finding something. To my surprise, she agreed and told me where to go. After a few minutes, I finally found the grocery section. They had everything you need for your household. But I couldn’t resist trying something. I bought a box of chocolate covered strawberries. I then proceeded to eat them right there in the middle of the store. I even managed to walk out without being caught by the security guard. This experience taught me that sometimes you can make things better than they already are.

outputs: Text: This morning I found myself lying in bed staring blankly at the ceiling, trying to figure out why I feel so angry today. It started out innocently enough - a disagreement between my best friend and her boyfriend. We both felt hurt and upset because we couldn't agree on something important. But then, things took a turn for the worse. My best friend told me she didn't love me anymore. She said she loved him more than me. At first, I tried to rationalize everything away; I explained to myself that maybe he wasn't feeling quite right lately, maybe he was just going through a rough patch. And maybe our friendship could survive without us being together. But no matter how hard I tried, the anger kept creeping up inside me. By afternoon, I was ready to scream. So I did. I called her a name that I never used to call anyone else. Then I stormed out of their house, slamming the door behind me. When I finally calmed down, I realized that I hadn't done anything wrong. Maybe she really meant what she said, and maybe we can still be friends even if we aren't together anymore. As I sat there alone, I knew deep down that I needed help. So I reached out to my therapist, hoping that he would understand where I was coming from. And he did. He listened patiently as I shared my thoughts and feelings, and he gave me the tools I needed to cope with this difficult moment. Over the weeks that followed, I began to realize that sometimes, the only way to move forward is to confront your pain head-on. And that's okay too. Sometimes, the worst thing that can happen is realizing that you need help. Output: got angry, confided in therapist, learned coping mechanisms

Text: I have been waiting anxiously for this moment since yesterday. It has finally arrived! I am going to be married to someone who will love me more than anything else ever could! And yes, I know how ridiculous that sounds, but please understand why I feel this way. Firstly, we were both raised by single mothers. Our mother passed away when we were just children, leaving our father to raise us. He was never able to fully bond with either of us due to his job. We grew up hearing stories about him working late hours and coming back exhausted. As such, we learned early on that true happiness comes from having a partner who loves us completely regardless of where their priorities lie. Secondly, there is no denying that our relationship began after our marriage proposal. There had been moments where she felt unsure about marrying me because of my past infidelity (she found out through a friend), but I knew deep down inside that I wanted to give her everything I had. Lastly, we met during college. She came to visit me in New York City for the first time, and we ended up spending three months together before moving to Boston. We fell in love quickly and decided to move here together. All these factors combined have made me realize how lucky I am to have her. But most importantly, I want to spend eternally happy and fulfilled with her.

the ceremony itself went without a hitch. My father officiated, and I wore my best wedding dress. Everything seemed perfect until I saw my husband-to-be walk down the aisle holding hands with another woman. To say I was taken aback is an understatement. At first, I thought maybe he had forgotten or misread my signal, but then I realized it wasn't possible. This person was supposed to be my future wife? Nope, no way. My heart sank as tears streamed down my face. How could this happen? Wasn't I getting what I deserved? But then I remembered the words of wisdom my father imparted upon me earlier. They told me that sometimes things aren't meant to be, and sometimes we need to learn to let them go. That night, I sat crying outside in the cold. What had I done wrong? Had I been too trusting? Or had I overlooked signs? Either way, it didn't matter anymore. Now I needed to focus on myself. Who was I without this person beside me? What did I truly desire in life? These questions consumed me, and I couldn't shake them off. However, despite the turmoil within me, I remained confident that we could overcome any obstacle that lay ahead. Because ultimately, I believed that true love was worth fighting for.

Input:
outputs: Text: I went into my office building last night for an important meeting and decided to take advantage of their free coffee machine to get a few more hours of sleep before heading home. After sipping my latte, I noticed something odd - there were no other customers present. This was not unusual, however, since most people tend to head home after their meetings. As I was finishing up my drink, I glanced over at the front desk and saw the janitorial staff cleaning the floor outside. My heart started racing as I realized that someone had been lurking around the building during my nap. But what could have possibly gone wrong? And worse, how could they know I wasn't there? As I stepped outside to grab my coat, I heard a strange noise coming from inside the lobby. It sounded like footsteps, pacing back and forth, maybe getting ready to come out? With my mind racing, I quickly grabbed my keys and ran down the hallway. Once I arrived outside, I peered through the window and saw a figure walking slowly toward the elevators. They looked like a tall man, dressed in black, with shiny boots and a hoodie covering his face. Suddenly, he stopped right in front of me, staring directly at me. He seemed to recognize me, judging by the expression on his face. "Excuse me," he said softly, "I didn't mean to startle you." I tried to calm myself down, thinking he might just be lost or confused. But as I continued to speak, I suddenly remembered everything else going on that evening. The missing files, the weird coffee incident, the stranger at the front door, and finally, the person waiting for me in the elevator. All these events added up to create a perfect storm that led to my discovery. Without hesitation, I opened the door, revealing a pair of eyes watching me from within. It was dark and shadowy, but somehow, it was familiar too. I felt my skin crawl, wondering if this person knew me or if I was imagining things. Before I could think any further, the doors slid open and I found myself standing in front of the elevator. A moment later, the doors closed, and I was left standing alone once again. What followed was a series of twists and turns, leading me deeper into mystery than ever before. The stranger turned out to be none other than my coworker, Jake, who had been keeping tabs on me throughout the entire evening. We had both been hiding our true intentions from each other, trying to avoid causing trouble. But when I saw him in the elevator, my heart skipped a beat. We exchanged small talk until the doors opened, and we embraced each other tightly. Our embrace was brief, but it gave me hope. Maybe this time, we wouldn't end up getting caught.

I continue pursuing my passions and goals, living life to the fullest. Even though I miss the thrill of risking everything for success, I'm grateful for the experience.

Looking back, I realize that sometimes, the best thing you can do for yourself is to step away from the noise and follow your heart.

Text: I hate these commercials where people sing their own songs like they were original compositions... I mean, come on now! And here we are, stuck listening to "Love Me Like You Do" by Ellie Goulding. I don't know what it is about this song, but it seems to be everywhere lately. It sounds like a terrible pop ballad from the '80s. So why am I forced to listen to it every time someone uses the word "love"?! 

The first thing I noticed was how many times it was used in ads. "You love me like you do..." Repeating it multiple times felt like I was hearing the same phrase more than once. I think this may also be because it feels trite and cliché. Maybe I'll never find true love and instead end up with "I love me like a dog loves his vomit," or something equally disgusting.

But then I heard a commercial featuring the guy who played Jake Sulser in Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country. He sang a cover version of "Ain't No Mountain High Enough". It wasn't quite as bad as "Love Me Like You Do", but it definitely wasn't good either. This made me wonder if maybe the people who write these ads don't even care about quality music anymore. They seem to only want people singing songs they already know well. Why can't they find new talent or try to create unique arrangements?!

So anyway, after I stopped thinking about how much I hate these commercials, I started watching the show that aired earlier tonight. It's called "American Idol". Apparently they're trying to revive the show, but apparently they haven't learned anything since its early days. There were plenty of talented contestants, but unfortunately none of them seemed particularly memorable. At least the judges were entertaining enough to keep me interested throughout the episode.

It seems like most people aren't too fond of American Idol. Someone mentioned recently that they couldn't wait until next year's season ends, so they wouldn't have to hear another round of horrible performances. But honestly, isn't that just cruel? Isn't it better to enjoy great music and art than to constantly be subjected to mediocre performances?!

Input: Text: obligatory comment about this not actually happening today, and this being a throwaway account.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: when I was 15 years old, I decided to start a blog about my life. It wasn’t easy. My family didn’t know how much I was writing about until later on, when they found out. They asked me why I was putting myself through such an emotional rollercoaster, and told me that if I wanted someone to read what I had written, I needed to learn to control my emotions better. This experience taught me something important – that sometimes, things aren’t always black and white.

The following weekend, my sister came over and watched my blog posts. She wrote down her thoughts and feelings after reading each entry. She shared them with me and encouraged me to keep writing. Her words gave me strength during those dark times.

As she sat across from me, looking up at me with big brown eyes, I felt a pang of guilt. I had been holding back because I didn’t think anyone would care enough to comment. But she listened patiently as I explained why my blog hadn’t taken off. She even took the time to respond to every single message I sent her, letting me know that she appreciated everything I had done.

That night, I went online and posted my newest blog entry. When I hit “submit,” tears streamed down my face. For the first time since starting my blog, I realized that my audience cared.

This experience has changed me in ways I never imagined possible. It taught me that not everyone will appreciate what I write, but that doesn’t mean I shouldn’t try. And more importantly, it showed me that I am capable of growing and learning from difficult experiences.

I hope that sharing my story helps others who may feel like giving up. Writing isn’t just about expressing yourself, it’s also about learning to accept feedback and grow as a person.

Text: I used to love going to the beach when I was younger. It was always sunny, warm, and the sand felt good underneath my feet. Nowadays, I only visit the beach if I need to relax from my daily routine. My recent trip to the beach involved sitting on a bench reading a book, watching other people play volleyball, and enjoying the scenery. As the hours passed, I began to feel an overwhelming sense of contentment. However, I couldn't help but think how much better life would be without having to worry about anything else.

The sky started turning pink, and the sound of waves crashing against each other grew louder. A few minutes later, I heard footsteps approaching. When I turned around, a man approached me holding a sign that read "FREE ENERGY". He explained that his company had created a device that allowed people to harness their energy, allowing them to live more sustainably. I was skeptical at first, but after hearing what he had to say, I decided to give it a try.

I put the device onto my head, and immediately felt a surge of electricity coursing through my body. I was amazed! This newfound power seemed almost magical. After using the device, I felt invigorated, energized, and happy. I realized that small changes in our lives could have a big impact on the environment. Instead of constantly consuming resources, we could start living in harmony with nature.

As I sat there feeling grateful for this experience, I noticed something strange happening outside. People were starting to gather around the park, laughing and joking together. They didn't seem bothered by the noise or disruption, instead they were embracing the beauty of their surroundings. I couldn't shake the feeling that maybe I wasn't crazy after all. Maybe this was the beginning of a revolution.

In conclusion, my experience on the beach taught me many things. Firstly, the importance of simplicity and mindfulness. Secondly, the benefits of taking action towards creating positive change. Lastly, the idea that sometimes even the smallest actions can have a significant impact.

Text: A friend recently told me about an interesting game they were playing called 'The Game.' It's described as a psychological horror story where players try to win by manipulating their opponents to think that someone else has betrayed them. I immediately dismissed it because I don't like games that involve deceiving people. But then I saw a trailer for a new Netflix show based on it and decided to give it a shot. Turns out, it's quite good!

So far, we have played three rounds. We each start with $2000, and our first move involves choosing whether to play against each other (which is very easy), or against the house (where everyone wins). If we choose to play against each other, we reveal who we are before the round begins. My partner chose to play against the house, and she won!

Afterwards, we discuss what went wrong during our turn. She says something like, "I made a big mistake," and we both laugh and agree that we shouldn't say anything until we know everything about our opponent.

In addition to the gameplay itself, I appreciate how the characters interact with each other. They seem genuinely concerned about each other's wellbeing, even though most of the time, it feels like they're just trying to manipulate each other. And maybe that's part of the point - it's funny to watch these strangers slowly figure out how to trick each other.

As for the plot, I love how it twists and turns around unexpected events. There are several moments where things feel completely random, yet somehow add up to create a satisfying conclusion. For example, one night, we find ourselves locked in a closet together. At first, we think it might be a prank, but then we hear footsteps outside. Suddenly, we're surrounded by other players who also happen to be trapped inside. As the tension builds, we realize that the whole thing is a setup designed to take advantage of us.

Overall, I highly recommend watching this show. It's hilarious, creepy, and suspenseful. Plus, it has some amazingly beautiful cinematography.

Sentence: One night, after hours of hard work, I had finally finished my report for my manager. He seemed satisfied and handed it over to me. As soon as I walked into his office, I could feel the weight of my mistakes on my shoulders. I knew that if I failed here, it would set me back years. My heart raced, and sweat dripped down my face. My mind raced through every possible scenario; did I mess up enough to lose my job? Was this another chance to prove myself wrong? Did I regret even coming into this meeting? As I sat down across from him, I tried to remain calm and composed. I told him that I was nervous because I wasn’t sure how good my report was, but I also let him know that I was willing to take feedback and improve. outputs: Text: I'm sitting at my desk typing away when my phone rings. It's my boss calling to tell me he needs me today. He asks if I have any backup plans, saying he doesn't know what might happen. My heart races as I consider the possibility of not showing up to work tomorrow. But I also feel guilty for neglecting him. We had a rough patch last month, and I need to show some loyalty. Today is Wednesday, so I'll have to work Friday instead. My mind starts racing again. What if I miss work? How will my coworkers react? What if my boss sees how much I missed yesterday and thinks less of me? I decide to go over my options before I make a decision. First, I check my emergency fund. I only have $35 left. Second, I think about taking a sick day. I usually take Fridays off, but my doctor told me I could use it for my birthday instead. That way, I won't have to worry about missing work, and I still get to spend time with my family. Third, I remember that my boss has been asking me to help out with other projects. Maybe I could volunteer to cover his schedule while he's busy. As I sit down to write my email, I realize that my boss may not be willing to give me more responsibility. And I definitely wouldn't want to burden him unnecessarily. I decide against volunteering, figuring that maybe someone else deserves my attention right now. Instead, I send him an apology letter explaining that I couldn't keep my promise to work on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I hope he understands. Later that night, I receive a message from my boss thanking me for helping out and letting me know that he appreciates our teamwork. I smile warmly at my phone, knowing that I didn't disappoint anyone. I head home feeling relieved and proud of myself.

outputs: Text: I had a really bad weekend, let's just start there. But then I found out I won a big jackpot at my local casino last Friday night. I could not believe it. It felt amazing, especially since it wasn't mine to keep. And I couldn't wait to share it with my friends. So, I decided to go to my friend's place first thing Monday morning, excitedly telling her everything that happened during our weekend adventure. She was shocked and surprised, but she loved hearing how much fun we had together. We were laughing so hard we almost fell over, and she couldn't stop giggling. Afterwards, we went to lunch at a fancy restaurant. My friend ordered the biggest burger ever, and while I ate my salad, I watched her eat hers and thought, 'This is what I need.' As we left the restaurant, my friend looked at me and said, 'I think I might have been lucky tonight.' I nodded gratefully and said, 'Yeah, well, you definitely weren't.' To make matters worse, I ended up losing $350 on the slot machine later that evening. I tried to blame my loss on my poor luck, but I know deep down that I was too busy having fun to pay attention to my cards. The next day, my friend came over again and asked me how things went. I told her the truth - that I had lost money playing the slots, and I wanted to take some time to regroup before making any more decisions. She listened patiently and didn't judge me. Instead, she encouraged me to take a break from gambling altogether and focus on other things that brought me joy. When I finally broke down and admitted to her that I was still upset about the money I lost, she hugged me tightly and told me that I needed to remember that sometimes life doesn't always give you what you want, but it gives you experiences that change your perspective. That experience changed my perspective, and I learned that sometimes, the most important thing isn't winning or losing, but finding happiness in every moment.

Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

outputs: Text: I had been struggling with low self-esteem for years, ever since I first saw myself reflected in a mirror without makeup. It wasn’t until recently that I began to understand why these negative thoughts were happening to me. A few months before I met my current partner, he asked me out to dinner. I was nervous because I had never gone on a date before. He took charge, made the plans, and set aside everything else in life except for us. We went to a fancy restaurant and ordered cocktails, each of them unique and delicious. Afterwards, he led me to a private room where we could enjoy our drinks and dessert together. As soon as he turned to leave, I started imagining what would happen after leaving him alone again. What would happen if someone came over and found us? Would he ask me out again? Would I let him? Would I regret choosing him over others who seemed more interesting? These questions consumed me for several minutes. When I finally left, I felt relief wash over me. My fears dissipated, and I was ready to take another chance on love. I went to see him again, and he told me that he wanted to spend the rest of his life with me. That night, I cried myself to sleep. And every day since then has been filled with joy, happiness, and new experiences. I no longer feel ashamed of myself; instead, I embrace who I am and celebrate my flaws.

I came home late last night after having dinner with some friends. When I got into bed, I noticed my phone charging on the side table beside me. As soon as I touched the charger, I heard a loud clicking sound. That's when I woke up. My alarm clock wasn't ringing, and I checked my phone again - nothing. Panic set in. I quickly turned off the alarm, but it still wouldn't go off. This continued until around 1 am. Then I started hearing strange noises coming from my room. They were coming from inside the wall. I tried opening the door, but couldn't find any way through it. Soon, I realized that my walls weren't solid anymore. There was a crack between them. At first, I assumed it was just a small hole, but then it grew bigger. Suddenly, the whole wall was starting to crumble apart. It took me almost 30 minutes to get the strength to open the door and check what was happening. What I saw made my blood run cold. A group of people were standing outside my room, looking inside. One of them spoke to me in a language I didn't understand. He told me that he was their leader and that they needed me to do something. But before I could make sense of his words, they attacked me. They grabbed me and dragged me away. Now, I'm trapped in another world. How will I survive here without help?

Text: I tried to buy a pair of shoes online last night and they didn't come through. It wasn't even shipped yet. I feel really stupid right now. What should I do?

I bought them online, not thinking too much about how many people got their orders wrong and ended up missing deadlines. Now, I am stuck with a bunch of unsold shoes.

My first thought was to return them, but they'd charge me $13 per item, and I already paid for delivery. So what could I do?

The second option seemed pretty obvious - sell them on eBay. But why bother when Amazon has a vast selection of used shoes for cheap prices? I checked their website and saw some pairs that were still in boxes. That was tempting.

But then I remembered how embarrassing it would be to advertise that I was buying shoes from someone else who hadn't delivered yet. And worst of all, I couldn't remember exactly what sizes I needed. I'd never done anything like this before.

In the end, I decided against selling them and instead went to the mall. There, I picked up a few pairs and headed home, feeling guilty about losing money. As I walked past the display cases, I noticed that most of the brands I usually shop at were empty. Maybe they weren't expecting anyone to stop by?

Later that evening, I received an email from the company apologizing for any inconvenience. They offered to send replacement shoes immediately. While I appreciated the gesture, I felt bad about causing such a hassle for them.

So, now I sit here, feeling both relieved and sad. Relieved that I didn't ruin my credit score or cause damage to my reputation. Sad because I spent so much money on shoes I wouldn't wear anyway.

As I lay in bed, scrolling through Facebook, I wonder if anyone will notice the empty displays. I hope not, but I also worry about what might happen if someone does spot them. Will I ever get my money back? Or worse, will I be banned from ever using their site again?

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: I have a confession to make - I accidentally deleted my entire family photo album last weekend! I think it may have even been because I thought I could erase them permanently. And no, there wasn’t any catastrophic loss of data or anything. It was just that I got really tired of seeing photos of my kids growing up and thought deleting would help. But alas, I didn’t realize until now that I couldn’t restore the files from the hard drive since I moved it somewhere else. What do you mean you haven’t heard? I told you last weekend! Anyway, let me explain why this matters – I will be moving house soon and need to take all these pictures downstairs and store them elsewhere. If anyone knows where to find some cheap storage space near me, please let me know.

The reason I accidentally deleted the whole thing is because I went through and edited each picture on the camera roll. There were too many of us together, and it seemed like a good idea at the time to delete some, but it turned out that there were a lot more people than I thought, and I ended up deleting most of the rest. I tried to recover the images using Photo Recovery software, but it kept failing. So now I am left with nothing but memories of my kids growing up.

I guess I should have known that deleting photos wouldn’t solve the problem. Maybe someday someone who has a backup system will come across this message and rescue my precious family photos. Or maybe not. Either way, it seems like I might end up having to relive the whole experience again once I move away from here.

Text: A few months ago I went to see a friend who had a showcase for her new collection. She was super excited about the lineup she showed off, and I was equally enthusiastic (though I didn’t know what she meant by “excited”). So when she introduced me to the designer, I knew right away that this was a special moment because she had never done anything quite like this before. It wasn’t until afterward that I started to think about how unique her presentation was – especially since most designers present their collections during fashion week in New York City.

It turns out, however, that this particular designer was actually based in Los Angeles! And not only did she have a showcase there, but she also presented a collection exclusively for our local market.

I was stunned – I mean, seriously? How cool is that?! As soon as the designer walked down the runway, everyone erupted into applause. But even more exciting than the fact that she was presenting locally was the fact that every single piece in her collection was made specifically for the LA Market. That’s right, no prints were used. All of the fabrics were locally sourced. This was truly groundbreaking, innovative, and incredibly inspiring.

The clothes themselves were beautifully crafted, yet simple enough to wear in any season. They were stylish without being overwhelming, and the colors were vibrant and fresh.

And the best part? My friend, who was sitting across from me in the front row, wore a dress from the same collection! It was absolutely breathtaking – I couldn’t take my eyes off it.

Of course, it wasn’t all rainbows and sunshine. There were moments where the models looked awkward and unpolished, which took away from the overall experience. However, overall, I felt extremely lucky to have been able to witness such an amazing display of creativity and style.

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: I recently bought a new laptop because my old one broke down completely. However, during the process of replacing the hard drive, I accidentally erased all my data! Oh noes!!!! What am I supposed to do now??

The first thing I did was start rebuilding my computer, but before doing anything else, I decided to take some pictures of everything on my hard drive. This included all my files, documents, photos, videos, music, etc. When I finished taking these pics, I noticed something strange. All of the folders were empty except for one folder titled "Recycle Bin."

I tried deleting every single file inside this Recycle Bin folder and then trying again, but nothing happened. So, I knew right away what I needed to do. First, I deleted the Recycle Bin folder altogether. Then, I went back into My Computer and selected all of the files and double clicked each one to go into Properties. Underneath the General tab, I changed the "Show hidden files and folders" option to "Always show hidden items," and then clicked OK. Afterwards, I went back into Windows Explorer and searched for all of the files I wanted to keep (the ones without the.jpg extension). I deleted them all, one by one, until I had finally filled up the Recycle Bin. Once I had emptied it, I restarted my computer.

As soon as the computer turned back on, I checked the Recycle Bin once again and sure enough, ALL OF THE FILES ARE IN THERE NOW!!! YAY!!!

This whole experience taught me a valuable lesson - never delete your entire computer folder by mistake. It's always better to save a few things and keep a backup copy instead.

Text: I bought myself a new pair of sneakers yesterday, which means that now I have no excuse not to wear them all day today. They feel fantastic! My feet are so much happier since getting these.

However, I also discovered that my old running shoes are still in good shape, so I decided to go ahead and replace them too.

I've been using them every single day since then, except for this morning. I went to run outside, but instead of feeling fresh and energized, I felt like crap. I tried to ignore it at first, but by lunchtime, I knew something wasn't right.

After some googling (which led me here), I came to the conclusion that my body may have developed an allergy to the new shoes. It doesn't matter whether I ran barefoot or wore sandals - both options hurt my feet worse than the original ones did.

It turns out that these shoes contain a type of chemical compound known as DOT (Dermatological Oxygen Transfer) which causes redness, inflammation, and pain. Apparently, I am immune to this chemical compound, making it difficult for me to tell when I'm being affected by it.

My only option now is to switch back to the old shoes, which will hopefully bring my feet back to normalcy soon.

So far, my experience has been that whenever I try to run without these shoes, I feel fine until around mile 4, when my feet start hurting again. From there on out, I know I'll need to rest or find another way to exercise.

Until then, I guess I'll stick to my favorite yoga stretches and maybe even try doing a few jumping jacks before bed.

In other news, I've decided to give up on trying to write anything interesting. All I ever seem to come up with is either terrible puns or ridiculous stories. This isn't helping me get better at writing. Maybe I should take up acting instead?

Input: Text: background: i went to summer camp about two weeks ago and met a guy. it's long distance and we text every second we possibly can. 

      now fast forward to this week. i'm in my school's marching band, and our band camp started this week, which means i get the pleasure of spending six hours a day on my feet doing things that the human body was not naturally made to do. our rehearsals are in the mornings and late afternoons/evenings which means i get a couple of hours a day in which i can do whatever. well, i was supposed to do the work for my online class and practice my music for band, and i hoped to fit eating, napping and texting the bf in somewhere int those precious band-free hours.
      let's just say i managed to get plenty of time in texting the bf. i had done about half of the work that was due today, but had procrastinated in the rest. well, here comes 6 in the evening, and i realise oh shit i still have all this work to do. so i rush to try and complete all the work, and 11 rolls around, the cut off time for due dates.
      i think no problem i'll just stay up until who-knows-time of the morning, finish the work, and sneak it into the the system so that the teacher would see it in the morning. but just my luck, the system goes down for maintenance, and here i'm stuck with uncompleted work and no way to complete it. so i end up finishing the assignment that i have to do offline and submit to the system, and now i'm stuck with work that's going to be late and the only option i can think of is emailing the teacher in the morning and hoping he'll take my late work.
Output: texted bf, didn't do work, am now possibly screwed

outputs: Text: I woke up at 3am last night because I couldn't sleep! It was hot outside, and I was feeling really tired. But then, I decided to go to bed early, and when I finally fell asleep, I got a phonecall from my best friend telling me she'd arrived home safely from her trip to Europe. And I almost cried tears of joy! I haven't seen her since July, and I missed her terribly! She also told me how much fun she had, and I felt guilty for being too busy during her visit, and neglectful towards her! We both laughed, and she promised to come over soon! My heart swelled with happiness, and I knew that nothing could ever change that moment. When I woke up this morning, I found myself in a panic - what if she hadn't even noticed? What if she never came over again? I thought about everything that happened yesterday and how happy I was right now. After some serious self-reflection, I remembered a text message I received earlier in the night from someone I used to date before I moved away for college. They were planning their first trip together (I was living abroad) and wanted to invite me along. I immediately agreed without hesitation! This was such a beautiful surprise! I was thrilled to have them join us, and the fact that they planned the whole thing was even more amazing! As we drove to the train station, I saw my best friend sitting alone on the bench by the window. She looked exhausted and sad, but I tried to keep my composure. I hugged her tightly, apologizing for not having been there for her, and promising to make sure she knows how much I love her. As we waited for the train, I couldn't help but feel grateful for everything that has happened in my life recently. There's always going to be moments where I miss people, but these memories will always remind me why I chose to live my life differently than most people. Now that I know what I've learned, I promise to cherish every single moment with her.

Text: My dad came home last night after being away at war for over three years. He arrived at midnight and I got him in bed by 3am. We were both exhausted, but excited. It was almost like losing him again.

      This past month, I have watched my dad suffer through some tough medical procedures. His condition improved enough that we could send him home with a little more hope than before. However, even though we are able to spend more quality time together, the reality of what he has gone through makes it harder for me to enjoy the moments we share. Even though I feel proud of him for fighting so hard, I know deep down inside that he is still dealing with pain and discomfort.

The sadness is mixed with gratitude. Gratitude for the fact that my dad is alive and healthy, grateful for the support he receives from family and friends, grateful for the love and care that my mom gives him. And yet, at the same time, there is sorrow for the loss of life and the trauma he experienced during such a significant part of his life.

This experience has brought us closer together as a family. Our conversations have become deeper, more meaningful, and fuller. As we sit down to eat dinner tonight, I realize that this will likely be the first Thanksgiving without Dad in our house. There will be tears, hugs, laughter, and memories shared. It's bittersweet. But I am filled with gratitude for having him in my life, and for the privilege of experiencing the holiday with him.

outputs: Text: I am currently on a solo trip to Europe where I have been staying in hostels all over the place. Last night I stayed in a hostel in Berlin that was really cheap (I think €10/night) and it ended up being a little too quiet, so I woke up around midnight and decided to walk down the street and check out some bars. After asking me if I wanted to join him for a pint, I said yes without hesitation! I guess the first step towards getting better is admitting you need help. This experience taught me that sometimes it takes a stranger to realize that we all struggle with our own demons and that there is no shame in seeking support.

Input:
outputs: Text: I've been working on a project for months now, and every day feels like it's taking forever. It's getting frustrating and stressful, especially when there are deadlines looming over me. But what really gets me down is how much work I need to do each weekend just to catch up. And when I think about all the things I could be doing instead, it makes me feel useless and worthless. That feeling only intensifies when I come across another person working through their own struggles - someone who seems more productive than I am. They seem to have a sense of urgency that drives them forward, while I sit here with nothing accomplished yet again. Sometimes, I wish I didn't have such high expectations for myself. Other times, I wonder why I bother trying at all. But sometimes, I find myself nodding along with people around me, knowing exactly where they're coming from. Whenever anyone talks about burnout, I know exactly what they mean. I remember sitting alone in my room last summer, unable to focus on anything except watching Netflix until dawn. My mind felt heavy, like I couldn't escape the weight of my responsibilities. Then came the realization that maybe, just maybe, these tasks weren't worth the effort. Maybe, just maybe, I wasn't meant to spend my entire life working towards some vague goal. Or perhaps, I was meant to enjoy life without worrying too much about work. I started thinking less about the end result, and more about enjoying the journey itself. If that means skipping work entirely and focusing solely on hobbies and leisure activities, then so be it. Because sometimes, all it takes is a little break to clear your head and start fresh.

Text: I have been working at this job since 9 am yesterday, now that I’ve hit the midnight shift. But when I got home tonight, there was no coffee left on the table. “What did you do?” I asked my boss. He replied, “I didn’t know how much more I could handle until 4am.”



“Why aren’t you getting any sleep?” I asked again. “Because,” he replied, “the office needs to stay open late today because of some new software that has come out.”

Surely enough, our manager came by around 3 pm to announce that tomorrow will be the last day of regular business hours before closing down shop completely. This means everyone here will be taking their leave today instead of tomorrow. And then another announcement later on, telling us all to prepare ourselves for what will happen tomorrow – the end of everything. We were shocked. It wasn’t even supposed to be announced yet.



This isn’t exactly news, but the way things happened made it feel worse than ever. Our bosses decided to close the doors of the company without giving us a chance to say goodbye properly. Even though we knew it wouldn’t change anything, we still felt sadness. That feeling was amplified when we heard the news about the closure. Everyone’s heart sank; none of us really expected it to happen.



But we didn’t let that stop us. We started brainstorming ways to make sure every employee gets paid, whether they worked during regular business hours or not. Some people took care of payroll while others organized fundraisers to help cover expenses. Others found other jobs and helped friends get them too. A few people actually managed to keep their jobs, despite having to quit in order to secure benefits such as health insurance and retirement plans.

The atmosphere became tense as we waited for the government to step in and save us from losing everything. People began discussing how to form unions and organize protests against management. Some even thought about starting their own companies to create jobs and revenue streams outside of the corporations.



It wasn’t easy, but eventually, something changed. As we gathered together once more, talking amongst each other and sharing our stories, we finally saw the light at the end of the tunnel. We realized that we weren’t alone anymore, that there were others out there fighting for justice just like us. Together, we fought for our rights and won.

We may never forget what happened to us, but it taught us valuable lessons about teamwork, resilience, and determination. And most importantly, it reminded us why we love our jobs and what makes life worth living.

outputs: Text: Today I went on a hike with my family and friends! It was such a beautiful day and we started our hike at 10am. We had been walking for about 45 minutes when we saw this little guy sitting on his porch eating his breakfast. He looked so happy and peaceful. So we decided to sit down beside him and enjoy his breakfast. Then he asked us what we wanted to eat and we told him we didn’t care. But then he offered us his eggs. He took them from the carton and cracked them into his mouth. After that he sat there for another hour watching the birds fly over and listening to the sound of the river flowing nearby. When we finished our breakfast, we thanked him and walked away feeling grateful for this wonderful experience. Later that evening, as we were packing up, I found this note stuck inside my pocket. “Thank You For Being A Friend” It made me smile thinking about how simple things like sharing food and friendship can bring joy and happiness to others.

outputs: Text: I was reading a book about ancient egyptian civilization. Suddenly I heard a loud noise outside my window. It sounded like someone breaking into my house. I thought "Oh no!" So I went downstairs to investigate. When I opened the door, I saw a group of guys dressed in leather jackets, black trench coats and bandanas covering their faces standing outside our building. They looked like they belonged to some gang or something. I screamed and started chasing them through the streets but they kept running faster than I could keep up. Finally, I managed to corner them near a street vendor selling spices. One of them reached for his gun, but before he could pull the trigger, I tackled him to the ground. We wrestled each other for a while until he finally gave up. I apologized profusely and thanked him for saving my life. He laughed and said, "Hey, remember that guy who broke into your place? Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

outputs: Text: A couple weeks ago I decided to take my dog for a walk along a trail that has several steep inclines, including a very large hill. We started our hike at a high elevation and climbed steadily through the trees until we reached the top of the hill. As we approached the crest of the hill, my dog began to sway uncontrollably, throwing us both off balance. I quickly realized that she had fallen behind and wasn’t able to regain her footing. At first, I thought maybe I could keep moving forward by carrying her down the slope. But after realizing just how difficult the terrain would become, I gave up hope of making it without assistance. Instead, I sat down and watched my dog struggle up the hill, occasionally yelling encouragement and helping her whenever possible. After what felt like an eternity, finally, she reached the summit. She looked exhausted and disorientated, and I could see that she hadn’t stopped shivering since we began our journey. To make matters worse, my dog’s panting increased exponentially, causing my breath to grow colder and colder. With each passing moment, I became more convinced that we wouldn’t reach the top alive. Finally, after what seemed like forever, we made it to the top! Exhaustion set in once again as we stood there, watching the sun slowly sink below the horizon. My heart ached as I took deep breaths to calm my racing thoughts. Just then, I heard a faint sound coming from behind us. It turned out to be a group of hikers who were also attempting to reach the summit. They saw my distress and offered to carry my dog down the rest of the way. Together, we worked together to get my dog back onto solid ground, where she soon found her bearings and resumed her usual pace. Despite the exhaustion, fear, and frustration, we were able to complete the entire trek safely, even though it was grueling and physically demanding. When we finally arrived back at the car, exhausted and relieved, I reflected on how grateful I was for those kind strangers who had helped us. And although the memory remains fresh in my mind, I will always remember their bravery and generosity towards someone else who may need them sometime too.

Text: It's been years since I last saw her, and then she suddenly dropped dead on stage during our gig at this bar. We were both crushed by the news.
It's been years since I last saw her, and then she suddenly dropped dead on stage during our gig at this bar. We were both crushed by the news. Her name was Sally. She was a great person who loved music more than anything else in life.
She was always smiling, laughing, singing along to every song. But tonight was different. When she took the stage, her voice shook like crazy, and her guitar started to slip out of her hands. A moment later, she fell over, unconscious. Our hearts broke apart in silence. As we looked down at each other, tears streaming down our faces, we realized what had happened. We had lost someone very special to us. We never imagined that she would die before our eyes.
Suddenly, the room became silent, except for the sound of our own breathing. Then, a man walked through the door. He was tall, broad-shouldered, and wore a suit jacket. He approached us, looking genuinely sorry. "I heard about your loss," he said softly. "Can I sit down?" We hesitated, but finally sat down next to each other. The man leaned forward, placing a hand on mine. "You guys need to talk," he said gently. At first, we didn't know what to say. How could we express what we felt? But slowly, words began to come out of us. And soon enough, we were crying together, holding onto each other tightly. Over the course of the night, we shared stories, jokes, memories, and laughter. Everyone was affected by Sally's passing in their own way, but somehow, we found comfort in each other's company. As the sun rose on the following morning, we woke up without Sally. She was gone. The rest of the week passed in a blur. We missed her terribly, yet also felt relieved that we weren't alone anymore. That day changed everything. Now, whenever we see a band playing live, we look at each other and think of Sally. We feel grateful that we were able to make it through such a difficult period, even though losing her was a tragedy beyond measure.

Input: Text: tifu. i was in line at the gas station, waiting to pay for my soda and gas, when i saw a quarter on the packs of gum directly in front of the counter. when it was my turn to pay i bent over and scooped up the quarter, and put it in my pocket, forgetting about it instantly. putting my soda on the counter and reaching for my wallet, i looked up and saw the cashier eyeing me with an angry glare. i was confused by this. was she mad at my choice of soda? (she could be one of those freaks that prefer pepsi) did i have an offensive t shirt on? (not unless she's offended by my obscure podcast shirt) 

i say "......$40 on 2 please." and she responds with "what's in your pocket?" 

"huh?" i stammer before finally understanding. "oh! i didn't steal anything!" and proceed to fervently pull everything out of my pockets, dropping change, and other things. i pick up the 25 cent culprit and thrust it to the cashier, as if it proved my story somehow, and explained that i had just seen the quarter on the gum and nabbed it.

 her face hadn't changed at all during the entire exchange. she finally just completed my transaction and said have a nice day. i'm not sure if she believed me or not, but i gathered all my stuff and hightailed it out of there.
Output: i found a quarter on a display of gum, cashier thought i was blatantly stealing gum right in front of her.

Or maybe it's because I don't want to spend years working towards a degree I might end up regretting. Whatever the reason, it feels like I'm drowning in indecision. It's like I'm holding onto something tight, hoping against hope that it will make sense eventually. But sometimes, things just don't make sense. Sometimes, they leave us feeling confused and lost.

This isn't the first time I've felt this way. When I was younger, I used to think I would become a famous author someday. Then I started writing poetry and realized that wasn't for me either. Now, I'm thinking of becoming a teacher, but I'm worried that teaching will be too demanding for someone who doesn't love kids. And then there's the whole thing with choosing between pursuing a career in fashion design or graphic design. Do I really want to devote my life to creating beautiful clothes and artistic designs? I don't know if I'll ever figure it out. Maybe I need more experience in both fields. Maybe I need to take some courses online. Maybe I need to try different types of workshops and classes.

The truth is, I'm scared of failure. Scared of disappointment. Scared of being unhappy. Scared of living a life where I don't truly belong. That fear has held me back for far too long. But now, I realize that fear needs to be taken seriously. It's a powerful emotion, but it also means taking risks and stepping outside of our comfort zones. If I want to achieve anything meaningful in life, I need to let go of my fear and step forward. So I'm going to start small. I'm going to take some classes in graphic design, and see where it takes me. Maybe it won't lead me down the path I originally thought it would, but that's fine. I trust that whatever comes next will be perfect. Because that's what I believe in.

Text: I don’t know if I’m ready yet to move past this, but there has to be more to this story than what I am seeing now.

I woke up feeling unwell last night, feeling weak and tired. When I checked my blood sugar levels earlier today, I saw that my numbers weren’t good. I knew something wasn’t right because I felt nauseous and dizzy every time I tried to eat anything. My doctor told me that I need to start monitoring my glucose levels again, and also advised me to try eating some vegetables first thing in the morning to help stabilize them.

My husband and I went grocery shopping yesterday afternoon, and I noticed that there were many options available for breakfast items, including cereals, yogurts, granola bars, etc. So I picked up some almond milk and oatmeal cookies, along with some fruit. We got home and started eating our snacks while watching TV. It took me a minute to realize that my breath smelled slightly metallic. I thought maybe I was reacting to the food, but when I looked down at my hands, I realized that they were covered in redness. I quickly reached underneath my shirt to feel my palms, and they were hot! I immediately pulled my hand away and looked at my skin, realizing that it was burning. This isn’t normal for me, so I called my primary care physician’s office, who sent us to the emergency room. They did a blood test and found out that I had hypoglycemia, meaning low blood sugar. That means I may not be able to take insulin effectively. After a few hours, they gave me medication to regulate my blood sugar levels until my next appointment.

Aside from the physical symptoms, I am struggling emotionally. Every day feels like a struggle. I keep asking myself why this happens to me? Why can’t I control these situations? I don’t understand why I always end up in this situation where I feel helpless and hopeless. How do you cope with emotional struggles related to diabetes?

Text: a lot of people have been talking about how their favorite team has failed miserably this season. I can't even count the number of times I've heard "the cowboys suck." It seems like every year someone starts saying this. This season may very well be worse than last years, but I refuse to believe it will be any worse.

I don't care what anyone else thinks, nor do I think it matters to them. What matters most is whether or not I enjoy watching football games. If you don't, then go watch whatever other sport you want, because I am not going to give a damn if your team loses, or wins. You aren't reading this article anyway. So why waste your time writing?

As much as I hate hearing about the Cowboys, it doesn't mean I won't watch the game tonight. Why would I want to sit around all day waiting for some random blogger who cares more about his/her feelings than the outcome of a game? And let's face it, no matter what happens, everyone will still talk about it tomorrow.

It's a free country. Don't worry about being liked by others, or how many followers you have. Just focus on having fun while enjoying the game.

That's right! I said it! Focus on having fun while enjoying the game. Because if you don't, then maybe you shouldn't be spending money on tickets, food, drinks, etc. That way you can spend those funds on something else. Something you actually enjoy. Like buying a used guitar or painting your house. Or both.

And besides, I have nothing against sports fans, or even the teams themselves. But please stop pretending that you know anything about sports, or life. We all make mistakes. And sometimes we lose. It's okay. It's better to learn from your mistakes, rather than dwelling on them forever.

So stop telling yourself that you're missing out by not liking your favorite team. Instead, embrace your love for football and enjoy the game without judgment. After all, isn't that what really matters?

For the beans:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F.
2. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
3. Add black beans, corn, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper to the pot. Stir to combine. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
4. Pour in water and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 10-15 minutes or until beans are tender.
5. Transfer the mixture to a blender and puree until smooth. Return to the pot.
6. If using fresh vegetables, add them to the pot along with any remaining liquid. Simmer for 10 more minutes or until the vegetables are slightly softened.
7. Serve hot.
8. Garnish with cilantro if desired.
9. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to three days.

Enjoy!

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

After checking everything, including my shoes, I decided to call it quits for the day and head inside to warm up.
