Text: I’ve been struggling with finding the right balance between work and family time for a while now. I know that some days feel like I am constantly pushing myself to try new things and expand my skills at work, while other days seem like I’m spending all day in front of the computer. I don’t always have time to cook dinner (or eat breakfast) every morning before heading out to work. This can sometimes lead to late night snacking and unhealthy eating habits. However, I also love being around friends and loved ones. Whenever possible, I will go out for coffee or grab dinner with them. It’s not always easy balancing these different priorities. Recently, I’ve tried making a conscious effort to spend more quality time with my husband and kids. Here are some tips and tricks that have helped us find a better balance.

1. Set aside specific times during the week for each person. For example, your husband might have Friday evening free to come over for dinner and maybe a movie. Your children may have Saturday afternoon free to play outside or hang out together. You can also set up a designated spot where everyone can gather once per month to plan events or check in on each other’s lives.

2. Make sure you both agree on what is expected of you. Whether it’s going out to dinner on Tuesday night or taking turns watching your kids for a few hours on Sunday afternoons, it’s crucial to communicate expectations clearly. If you have different schedules or responsibilities, you may need to compromise on certain activities or times.

3. Try small experiments. One way to avoid feeling overwhelmed by too much planning is to try experimenting with smaller projects. Maybe your husband has a project that needs to be done tomorrow, and you can help him out by helping him pick out paint colors or getting some plants for his office. Or perhaps your children ask for a particular activity or skill they want to learn – take them to a music lesson or join a sports team together. These types of activities give you the opportunity to bond and build relationships without feeling overwhelming.

4. Take breaks. Sometimes it’s hard to keep yourself motivated and focused when everything feels chaotic. Try setting aside some quiet time throughout the week for reflection or self-care. Maybe you could listen to some relaxing music, write down your thoughts or feelings, or simply take a walk outside. Even just five minutes can make a big difference.

5. Be kind to yourself. Remember that even though your priorities may shift occasionally, you are still committed to building strong connections with your loved ones. Give yourself permission to make mistakes or change course if necessary. And remember that no matter what happens, you can always choose to focus on what matters most.

Input:
outputs: Text: my boyfriend and I took our first trip out of town recently, and it wasn’t without its share of adventures! We visited some local farms where we picked fresh fruits, nuts, and vegetables, all while enjoying the beautiful scenery around us. But the highlight of our trip happened when we stopped at a quaint little cafe in the middle of nowhere. We sat down at their picnic table, sipped on some delicious homemade coffee, and watched the sunset over the rolling hills outside. As we finished our cups, my boyfriend asked if I wanted to join him in eating some cinnamon rolls he had brought along. My heart sank, because I am absolutely terrified of cinnamon rolls – the smell alone sends shivers down my spine. He tried his best to convince me, telling me how good they were, but I knew deep down inside that I wouldn’t eat anything more than a small piece before bedtime. Little did I know that my fears were going to come back to haunt me. As soon as I bit into one of those sugary-crispy treats, I felt my whole body start to tense up. It was like the entire world had suddenly gone dark, and everything started to feel very real and very scary. My boyfriend noticed my reaction, grabbed my hand, and gently pushed me towards the nearest chair. "Come on, baby," he whispered, "you can do this." And just like that, I surrendered to the moment. I closed my eyes and savored every single crunchy, buttery, sweet flavor. When I opened my eyes again, there she was - a perfect pink, fluffy cinnamon roll. She looked almost too pretty to eat, her flaky layers peeking through the warm dough, her soft center melting in my mouth. And that's when I realized what I had done. I had let my fear consume me completely. I had made the worst possible decision imaginable; to sit there and eat a perfectly good cinnamon roll. What followed next was nothing less than pure horror. I felt my throat tighten, my chest constrict, and tears well up in my eyes. This time, however, I didn't let the fear control me. Instead, I used the opportunity to laugh and joke with my partner. I joked about the fact that the only way to make sure I didn't end up having a stroke was to keep eating those cinnamon rolls until they fell apart. And finally, I allowed myself to take a bite. And this time, the experience was different. The taste was much better than I expected, and I couldn't help but smile at the feeling of satisfaction that came rushing over me. Looking back, I realize that sometimes, the best thing you can do in life is trust yourself. You may think your biggest fear will never happen, but sometimes, it does. And the best thing you can do is accept it and find a way to overcome it.

Text: I am writing this from my car, while sitting in traffic, because it has been raining heavily all afternoon. I am stuck at the stop light waiting for the rain to subside enough that I can safely make it home. This has been going on for over an hour now, and I’m getting pretty irritated.


The radio is blaring some kind of country song, which just makes everything worse. It seems like every other person in the world is either driving their cars around town, or sitting idly by watching TV. I don’t even know what I’d do without my phone, though. I check my email and find out that someone needs help fixing their broken air conditioner unit.


I feel like I could really use a cup of coffee, but I don’t want to get out of my car to go buy one. Instead, I decide to grab my keys and start heading down the road. When I reach the intersection where the rain is finally beginning to let up, I realize that there’s no signal.


“Wait,” I say aloud, “what? There isn’t any signal?” Everyone around me stops talking, looking at me expectantly. Finally, the first car starts honking its horn.


Suddenly, a black SUV pulls up beside mine. A man gets out, looks directly at me, and says, “Hey there, buddy.” He doesn’t sound angry, more like friendly. “So how far is your house?”


I think about answering, then suddenly remember why I’ve been stranded here for hours. “It’s probably closer than it used to be,” I mutter.


The man nods again, and continues speaking to his passenger. “Well, maybe I’ll meet you at your place. Just tell them to bring the car.”


Without thinking twice, I jump into the driver seat and start the engine. My heart feels like it’s going to burst out of my chest, but somehow I manage to keep calm.


As soon as we hit the freeway, I notice the man behind us has stopped. We’re both glancing nervously at each other before eventually resuming our conversation.


After what seems like forever, we finally arrive at my house. By the time I park and walk inside, I’m ready to collapse. But I hear the front door slam shut behind me. I turn around to see the man holding open the passenger-side window.


“Come on, let me give you a ride home,” he offers. “You might need a drink, or a snack, or anything else.”


For once, I’m actually grateful for him offering. I hesitate only briefly before agreeing, relieved to finally be able to relax for a moment.


When we finally pull up outside, I can barely contain my excitement. “Thank you so much!” I shout, pumping my arms in the air.


The man simply smiles and steps out of the vehicle, gesturing for me to follow. As we walk together to my front door, I’m filled with gratitude for having such a wonderful stranger in my life.

outputs: Text: I hate being stuck indoors with nothing better to do than watch TV. That’s why I decided to spend Saturday evening watching the new Star Wars movie! I mean really, what other activity can you do inside? It took about 2 hours before I realized that there isn’t anything else going on besides sitting in front of a screen. And then I started looking for ways to entertain myself. So I thought maybe I could make some popcorn and watch it later. But then I realized that would only last for about 15-20 minutes until I get hungry again. So I turned on Netflix and watched the latest season of Stranger Things (which is great) and then went back to sleep. When I finally opened my eyes Sunday morning, I noticed my husband already had his laptop open. “Hey,” I said, “What did you say?” He replied, “You know exactly what I said.” I rolled over onto my back, yawned, and stretched my arms above my head. My husband was right next to me, typing furiously. At first, I didn’t realize where he was because everything looked dark behind him. Then I saw his keyboard. And then I heard him typing. I couldn’t believe it – I had been sleeping for almost 8 hours straight. What the hell happened? After a few more minutes, I remembered that I had taken my daughter to her piano lesson. She had been playing for three hours nonstop, and I hadn’t even seen her. Now she was standing in front of the door holding her pencil case tightly, waiting for me to come pick her up. As soon as I walked into the room, she grabbed her bag and left. Maybe it wasn’t such a bad idea after all.

So we sat down and she picked out three different candies (chocolate covered pretzels, chocolate covered Oreos, and a red velvet cupcake). As soon as I saw those candies, I knew what I wanted. That's why I love dating Katie.

Text: hey guys, I know this isn't exactly news, but my dad has been struggling lately financially. He hasn't worked full time since his last job ended a few years ago and has only recently landed a part-time gig that barely pays him what he used to earn. It seems like every weekend he's either running low on money or having to take out loans just to pay rent. This has led to some serious stress and anxiety.

I think it's safe to assume that many people have gone through something similar - someone struggling to make ends meet, juggling multiple jobs, etc. My dad works in IT and I've always admired his dedication and hard work, but I never fully understood the level of pressure he faces until recently. His work hours tend to vary wildly depending on whether or not they need to attend events related to our company. If he attends an event, chances are good that he won't be getting paid for it. Sometimes he doesn't even get paid for the days he's working. And that's before he takes into account the additional costs associated with travel, lodging, food, etc. For instance, he spent $238 on gas alone during one month last year. When he first told me about these struggles, I was shocked. But now that I understand better, I can appreciate how difficult things are for him.

I also wanted to share with everyone how much my mom means to me. She's been married to my dad for almost ten years, and she's sacrificed her own career opportunities to help support their family. They both have very different careers - she's a nurse, while he's a software engineer. Yet despite the differences between their professions, they manage to balance everything quite nicely. My mom's job often requires her to work nights, and sometimes weekends, too. That means she'll spend a lot of time driving herself back and forth to various locations throughout the city. Last summer, she missed a wedding due to a conflict with work. It was devastating for her, and she couldn't bear the idea of missing another opportunity for her son to grow up with a father present. Her husband also went through some personal challenges, and they were forced to move from their home state. All of this added up to make things extraordinarily difficult for my mom. She had to relocate with my siblings and parents, leaving behind her entire network of friends and colleagues. Even though my dad and sister live close by, it felt isolating to have such a significant other far away. I know that my mom will continue to sacrifice for my dad and for our family, no matter what. I hope you understand why it's so important to recognize and appreciate the sacrifices others make for loved ones. Thank you all for your continued support.

outputs: Text: A few months ago I was driving down the highway, lost in thought, when suddenly, an ungodly amount of traffic stopped behind me. It seemed like every car behind me was also heading towards the exit, blocking our way out of town. At first, I tried to swerve around each car, hoping they wouldn't catch up to me. But as time passed, it became clear that these cars were headed straight toward me. Suddenly, I saw something - maybe it was a red light or some sort of sign - in front of me. It was a flashing yellow arrow pointing right towards me. This moment was both terrifying and exhilarating; I felt like I was racing against time, trying to avoid getting caught. As soon as I turned onto the interstate, the drivers ahead of me began honking their horns furiously. "We need to pull over!" I shouted over the din of noise. "We have to stop!" They followed suit. Finally, after what felt like hours, I finally came to a complete stop. As I stepped out of my truck, I couldn't help but laugh. That moment has stuck with me ever since. It reminded me of the absurdity of human behavior and the incredible power of humans to band together in moments of crisis.

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.

Input:
outputs: Text: I went on a road trip recently with my girlfriend. We drove from New York City to California and then back again. It was incredible! One day we stopped by a small town called Cuyahoga Falls, Ohio. There were these giant waterfalls right outside of town. As soon as we arrived, we saw them and were like "Wow!" But what made us go nuts was the fact that there were no signs indicating where they came from. We walked down to the riverbed and asked locals where the falls came from. They said they weren't sure, but it was a popular myth among locals that the falls come from underground springs. So we decided to take our chances and follow the stream. After walking for miles, we finally reached the top of the hill leading up to the falls. To our surprise, there were these huge rocks blocking the way. because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: I used to love the smell of freshly brewed coffee wafting through the house. But nowadays, all I can think about is the stench of rotting garbage. Every morning, the pungent odour of old carpets fills my nostrils, making me feel nauseous and disgusted. My heart pounds with anxiety whenever I step inside the kitchen sink because I know what lies ahead – an endless cycle of dirty dishes, leaking water, and stagnant water. It feels like every night, the same scene repeats itself, only worse than the previous night.

It's hard to imagine having someone else living next door who loves the scent of garbage. I hate it! Why does everything have to smell bad?

I can barely concentrate during dinner parties because I keep feeling queasy. The taste of food always makes me sick. Whenever I eat something new, I worry that it might turn out horrible. I never want to try anything again.

The smell of rotting vegetables in the fridge fills my nose, causing me to recoil involuntarily. Even though I try to ignore it, the memories of moldy food fill me with dread.

In my dreams, the stink of garbage seems even stronger. I hear myself snoring loudly, surrounded by discarded plastic bags and cardboard boxes. I often find myself curled up under blankets, trying to block out the stench of garbage.

One day, my friend suggested that we go for a hike in nature. I agreed eagerly. We set off early, hoping for a respite from our daily grief. As soon as we arrived at the trailhead, I noticed the stench of decay. It was thick and suffocating.

We trudged along the path, ignoring the acrid scent that clung to us like an invisible cloak. The air grew colder, and the ground became slicker beneath our feet. A sudden downpour sent chills running down my spine.

When we finally reached the forest, I couldn’t help but notice how much better the smells seemed compared to the city. Everything smelt fresher here. There was a faint hint of blooming flowers and the earthy fragrance of leaves. I felt alive once again.

But the smell of garbage stayed with me throughout the trip. Everywhere we went, I detected its presence. In the woods, we passed by a stream filled with debris. The riverbed was covered in rusty metal and bits of plastics. The water smelled of sewage and urine.

As we hiked back to civilization, I couldn't shake off the memory of the smelly garbage. I tried to focus on the beauty of nature instead, but my mind kept wandering back to the stench of garbage. It took me hours to finally leave the forest behind.

My experience has taught me to appreciate the small things in life. Instead of dwelling on the smell of garbage, I try to focus on the positive aspects of being surrounded by nature. And maybe someday, I will discover another way to deal with the smell. Until then, I hope I never encounter another smoky, stinking, and grossly decomposing garbage dumpster again.

outputs:
Text: I once tried making a salad dressing using only ingredients from my local grocery store. It turned out quite good, and it's always interesting to experiment with things like fresh herbs instead of store bought ones. However, the best part of the whole process was discovering that you can buy fresh squeezed lemon juice online! And it's amazingly affordable too. So, whenever I need to make something quick and healthy, I grab some lemons and a bottle of white wine vinegar and go to town. Here's a recipe for a classic Caesar Salad dressing that incorporates both of these ingredients. 

Ingredients: 
For Dressing: 
- 2 tablespoons white wine vinegar 
- 4 cloves garlic, minced 
- Juice of 1 large lemon 
- Salt and pepper to taste 

Instructions: 
1. In a medium bowl whisk together white wine vinegar, minced garlic, and juice of one lemon until smooth. 
2. Season with salt and pepper to taste. 
3. Taste and add more lemon juice if desired. Adjust seasonings accordingly. 
4. Store dressing in refrigerator until ready to use. 

To Use: Add the dressing to your favorite Caesar salad dressing mix and enjoy! 

I hope you find this helpful! Let me know if you try making this yourself - I love trying new things in the kitchen.

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

outputs: Text: I am currently reading "The Great Gatsby" by F. Scott Fitzgerald, and I have been fascinated by its themes of wealth, class, and power. This novel has challenged me to consider these topics in a new way, both in terms of its depiction of America during the Roaring Twenties and its exploration of themes of morality and corruption. However, despite my interest in these subjects, I find myself struggling to fully engage with the book due to several issues related to its structure and style. Firstly, the novel consists of multiple narratives told from different perspectives, each with their own unique voice and perspective. While this structure allows for a richness of detail and complexity, it also presents readers with a daunting amount of information to process at once. Secondly, the novel contains numerous allusions and references to other works, such as Shakespeare and Oscar Wilde, which may confuse or frustrate readers unfamiliar with these authors. Finally, while the novel's themes and ideas are complex and profound, they often feel contrived or forced. There are moments where characters seem to be acting in ways that simply don't fit within the context of their characterization, creating dissonance between what we are supposed to believe is happening and what feels arbitrary. Overall, I think that Fitzgerald's writing here falls somewhere between the strengths and weaknesses of his earlier work. It offers insightful observations on American society and culture, but it sometimes lacks clarity or nuance. At the same time, it is difficult to deny the impact of the author's prose, which creates vivid images and memorable scenes. Despite these criticisms, however, I remain committed to continuing to read and appreciate "The Great Gatsby."

Text: I am an artist living in a small town in the Midwest. This is where I live now. It’s called home. But at times I feel like I’ve been stuck here forever. There’s something about being in such close proximity to nature that makes me feel disconnected from it. It’s almost like we’re both pretending that everything outside our windows isn’t happening.



I have no idea what this poem means, nor does anyone else seem to care either. We sit around, staring blankly at each other. It’s like everyone wants to talk, but they can’t find anything interesting to say. We’ll watch movies and eat junk food and play video games until someone finally says “Hey man, do you think I should start writing poetry?”

We all nod, agreeing that yes, maybe it’d be fun to try something new.

Suddenly, the door opens, and in walks a woman. She looks like she’s seen worse things in her time traveling through space and time. Her eyes meet ours, and then she turns back to her bag. We exchange nervous glances before deciding to introduce ourselves.

Her name is Jane, and she’s from another planet.

Jane doesn’t know much about us, except that we all come from different parts of the country and that we’re kinda lonely. Soon enough, she tells us that she has some advice for us.

“Write,” she says, smiling kindly.

At first, none of us feels inclined to listen to her. Our problems aren’t exactly related to writing, or even art. But eventually, we decide to give it a shot.

As we begin to write, we discover that we’re all very talented writers. And that we love each other’s company. We spend hours sitting around talking, laughing, and sharing stories.

But as days turn into weeks, and weeks turn into months, we slowly lose touch with one another. We forget the reasons we originally came together, and instead become obsessed with our own ideas.

It’s only when we hear rumors about strange occurrences in our area that we realize how far apart we’ve truly become. And yet, somehow, we’re all still friends. We may have drifted apart physically, but we’ve remained connected by our shared love for words.

The world might spin wildly around us, but we keep reading books, watching movies, and playing games until we die. Because sometimes, it’s worth putting yourself out there – just to see what happens.

Text: I’ve been reading this great book called “The Alchemist” by Paulo Coelho. It’s about a shepherd boy named Santiago who goes on a journey to find his true purpose in life. So far, so good, except for one thing – I keep getting lost along the way. But then, I remember why I started. That’s because I want to become a shepherd myself.
Santiago meets several people on his path, including the Pharaoh, the wise old man, and even a magical bird who whispers secrets. Throughout the story, Santiago learns important lessons about himself, his dreams, and how he wants to live his life. One of the main themes throughout the book is finding your own unique path in life.

I read this last night and I love it! This has made me realize that sometimes, things happen to us for a reason, even though we may not understand it yet. And sometimes those reasons aren’t easy ones either. But I guess that’s what makes life interesting, right?

In terms of the protagonist, Santiago reminds me a lot of me. He starts out wanting to go where everyone else thinks he belongs, but ends up following his heart instead. He’s stubborn, impatient, and doesn’t give up easily. I think these qualities will serve him well wherever he ends up.

Another theme in the book is how small our lives truly are compared to the universe around us. We often focus on what we have done wrong, what we regret, or what we wish we could change. However, the world around us continues to exist regardless of our mistakes. Our choices shape the direction of our lives, but ultimately, we are part of a vast and interconnected web of existence.

As I finish this book, I feel lighter inside. It’s amazing how powerful words can be. Even though I haven’t completely understood the meaning behind the stories, I am grateful for their message.

What I learned from this book is that life isn’t all sunshine and rainbows. There are struggles and challenges along the way, both big and small. But what matters is how we handle them. Sometimes we have to face hardships head-on and others we have to choose between different paths. Either way, we learn from the experience and grow stronger through it.

This book has inspired me to take risks and follow my passions. To never stop learning and growing. And to appreciate the beauty in life, even in its imperfections.

Overall, I highly recommend this book to anyone looking for inspiration and hopefulness. It’s a beautifully written work of art that touches on many universal themes.

outputs: Text: I love pizza, especially pepperoni pizza. It has always been a family tradition for my grandma to make homemade pizzas every sunday night before church. But last weekend, I had no pizza sauce, so instead, I decided to use tomato paste to add flavor to our pizza dough. After shaping the dough into a ball, I placed it onto a cookie sheet lined with parchment paper. Once the dough was resting, I added the tomato sauce mixture over the top, leaving enough space for the cheese layer. Lastly, I spread the mozzarella cheese over the entire surface of the pizza, covering each slice with cheese. I put the dish in the oven for approximately 25-30 minutes until the cheese was melted and bubbling. During this process, I checked the crust regularly to ensure it wasn’t burning. When finished, I removed the pizza from the oven and let it sit for five minutes before slicing and serving. This recipe yields six servings of delicious, homemade pizza.

Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Text: oh man I've been missing my favorite food since last weekend...
the restaurant I go to every Sunday night has been closed down due to covid-19, so I've been craving their famous spicy fried chicken dish. But now, they're only offering takeout orders until further notice. It's a bummer because it means I won't get to try it tonight.

But wait! There's good news! A new restaurant called Chick'n Bite has opened up nearby. They offer delicious homemade chicken nuggets and wings. Plus, they're open seven days a week! That's great news, especially considering how many people work downtown and don't want to risk getting COVID-19 from eating inside a crowded restaurant.

I decide to give them a shot. When I arrive, I am greeted warmly by the owner, Mrs. Johnson. She hands me a menu and asks if I would like to order online. I hesitate briefly, then quickly agree.

Their website says they use fresh, high-quality meat, never frozen or precooked. And they guarantee their chicken is always crispy and juicy, no matter what temperature it's cooked to. Their sauces come straight from the oven, so you can taste each flavor individually.

And then I see it - the smell wafting through the air. The spiciness is already starting to set in, but I know it will only grow stronger once I start eating. As soon as I place my first order, Mrs. Johnson takes charge of my experience. Her friendly smile and gentle touch help calm any nervousness I may feel.

After my initial plate of wings arrives, I immediately begin trying out different dipping sauce options. My favorite is the ranchero, made with creamy avocado, tangy lime juice, and a hint of hot pepper. It pairs perfectly with the tender, juicy chicken pieces.

As I finish my second round of wings, I realize how much better these chicken nuggets are than any I've ever tried before. They're lightly breaded, crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside. Each piece is coated in a thin layer of batter that makes it easy to hold onto even though they're so large.

When I return to the table, I hear Mrs. Johnson calling my name. "Mrs. Smith," she says cheerfully. "Your chicken nuggets are done!" I jump up eagerly, hoping I haven't missed dinner yet.

My husband and I share our meals together while Mrs. Johnson watches us eat. We talk about life, family, and everything else in between. Even though we're physically apart, we're still connected through our shared love of chicken nuggets.

Overall, Chick'n Bite's chicken nuggets are worth the drive to their location. From the crisp texture to the perfect amount of seasonings, I can't stop raving about them. If you're looking for a satisfying snack that doesn't require taking your mask off, head to Chick'n Bite. You won't regret it.

This month, scientists have discovered something truly remarkable – a substance that could revolutionize medicine. It's called "nanoparticle therapy," and it involves using tiny particles to deliver drugs directly to cancer cells. So far, researchers have tested nanoparticles in animal models and found promising results. But now, the first human trials are underway.

The study, led by Dr. Sarah Kahn, Director of Cancer Biology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, took place in Boston last week. Twenty patients with advanced breast cancer received treatment with nanoparticles containing anti-cancer agents. One group received standard chemotherapy; another group received the same dosage of nanoparticles plus a second round of chemo. Both groups showed significant improvements in tumor size and survival rates compared to those receiving traditional chemotherapy alone.

Dr. Kahn says the study shows that these nano-based treatments may offer hope to people facing aggressive forms of cancer. She also notes that the treatment doesn't come with side effects such as fatigue or diarrhea. And she hopes that further studies will show that these nanosciences can help improve overall health outcomes.

However, critics aren't convinced. Some say the study's methodology was flawed, and others argue that the benefits of nanotechnology haven't yet been proven in humans. Still, Dr. Kahn believes that nanomedicine holds great promise.

"Nanoparticles have shown incredible efficacy against various types of cancer," she explains. "And I think this study demonstrates that they can be combined with existing cancer treatments to potentially provide even greater therapeutic benefit."

What is nanoparticle therapy and what are its potential applications?

outputs: Text: I woke up feeling exhausted from sleep deprivation, so I decided to take a nap. As soon as I opened my eyes, I felt dizzy and nauseous. After several minutes of struggling to stand, I collapsed onto the floor. When I finally managed to sit upright, I realized I had forgotten to turn off the lights. Suddenly, I heard a loud screech coming from above me. I quickly looked over my shoulder to find a large bird perched on the ceiling fan. "Sorry!" I muttered under my breath, trying to sound calm. It wasn’t until I stepped inside the room that I noticed the smell of urine and faecal matter. My stomach churned as I tried to think of what else could have been causing such disgusting odors. “What the hell?” I thought, realizing that the problem was probably somewhere nearby. A quick glance down revealed that my bedroom window was open. I closed it immediately, hoping that would fix things. But no sooner did I shut it, than another bird flew in through the window. This time, it was smaller and featherless. “This isn’t funny,” I muttered under my breath. And then it hit me – I had left the curtains drawn. I frantically searched the room, but couldn’t find anything wrong with them. I closed each one carefully, and then reopened them slowly, just to make sure nothing was broken. But it seemed like every time I closed the curtains, they slid further apart. They were now completely closed. “Well, maybe this is just a sign that I need to close my curtains,” I mused aloud. As I continued to ponder, I suddenly spotted a small piece of paper fluttering to the ground. Curiosity piqued, I picked it up and read the words written on it. “I hope someone sees this.” With those words, I took a deep breath and headed towards the door. But as I reached for the handle, something grabbed hold of me from behind. I turned around to face the source of the fearful noise, only to realize that the intruder was… A fly. Its tiny legs whisked across my cheek as it landed next to me. “Ow!” I exclaimed, letting out a sigh of relief. “It was just a fly," I said, shaking my head. As I walked away from the door, I glanced back once more to confirm that no other creatures had entered my home. However, upon returning to my room, I found a strange object sitting beside my bed. It was a small box, sealed tightly with twine. I hesitated for a moment, unsure whether to unwrap it or leave it alone. But curiosity won out, and I pulled aside the twine. Inside lay a single teardrop-shaped crystal, surrounded by delicate gold filigree. It was unlike any thing I had ever seen before. I examined it closely, marveling at its beauty. “Who owns this?" I wondered, reaching for the box. But as I lifted it, something caught my eye. It was a picture of my family. At first, I dismissed it as mere coincidence. But as I gazed deeper into the photograph, I realized that my family members were somehow intertwined within the frame. There was my father, standing proudly in his military uniform; my mother, holding a bouquet of flowers; and my younger brother, laughing and playing with a stuffed animal. All three images were faded, but still recognizable. I was astounded. For a brief moment, I lost track of time, unable to believe that these pictures could be real. Was this a dream? Or was this proof that our lives were connected in ways beyond my imagination? Whatever the case may be, I knew one thing for certain. I needed to tell my loved ones about this discovery. I spent hours pouring over my photos, searching for clues and meaning. Finally, I located a photo album hidden beneath my mattress. Inside, I discovered a series of letters between my great-grandparents. These letters detailed stories of their travels, their struggles, and their hopes for the future. As I read, tears streamed down my face. How many generations has it taken to connect us all? How far we have come since we were born? We were meant to be together, always.

Text: I woke up early today because I had a meeting scheduled at 8 am. As soon as I stepped out of bed, I realized that it was still dark outside. My alarm clock didn’t work correctly due to an issue with batteries. But that didn’t stop me from getting dressed.

As I reached for my shoes, I noticed a small piece of paper stuck between the sole of my shoe and the bottom of my pants. It read “Don’t forget to take your medication” – I always forget mine after a few minutes.

I looked down at the note and felt embarrassed. Why couldn’t I remember such basic things? This was only my third day working here. Maybe I needed to start practicing self-care.

Later that day, during our team meeting, I decided to share my struggles with managing stress and anxiety. When I finished speaking, I was met with stony silence. No one dared to say anything. We all sat in silence until someone finally spoke up.

“What was the topic?” asked one of my colleagues.

“Stress management,” I replied.

Silence fell once again.

The silence continued throughout the rest of the meeting. No one spoke, even though I kept talking. Eventually, one of my coworkers approached me.

“You seem stressed out,” she said.

“Yes,” I replied, feeling defensive.

She smiled kindly.

“It’s okay to feel stressed sometimes. Sometimes life gets crazy, and we need to learn how to manage those feelings.”

That was it. She opened up about her own struggles with anxiety and helped me see that I wasn’t alone.

By sharing my experience, I learned that it's okay to ask for help and support when we need it. And that maybe taking care of ourselves isn't weakness, but rather strength.

After the meeting, I found myself laughing at my colleague's words. They weren't mean, they were honest. And it gave me the courage to continue speaking up about what I needed.

My conversation with my colleague changed my perspective on stress management forever. Instead of seeing it as a negative trait, I began to appreciate its benefits.

And slowly but surely, I started to feel less anxious and more confident in handling difficult situations.

I looked into her eyes and knew then that I would do whatever it took to make sure she lived a long and healthy life.

Soon enough, I learned about another healthy option available at my favorite coffee shop – smoothies. Smoothies are often touted as being low calorie and nutritious alternatives to traditional breakfast fare. I tried a few different ones over the course of several months, each with its own unique taste and texture. But despite the plethora of flavors available, one thing remained constant throughout all of them – how delicious they tasted. Whether they were loaded with fruits, nuts, seeds, or protein powder, they always left me feeling satisfied and energized. My friends couldn’t believe how easy it was to transition to a whole-food, plant-based lifestyle after discovering this discovery. “I never thought I’d enjoy smoothies,” one of them exclaimed, “But man, they’re amazing!” With the addition of smoothies to my diet, I no longer felt deprived or hungry. Instead, I felt full and satisfied, leaving me feeling better than ever before. And since incorporating this healthier habit into my routine, I haven’t looked back.

Text: so here I am sitting in class, trying to write a paper about "The Effect Of Technology On Society" while also working on a group project involving social media marketing. My professor walks into the room, grinning from ear to ear. He says, "Hey guys, let's go over your papers tonight!"

My heart sinks. What did he think would happen? A disaster?

But then he adds, "And don't forget to bring in any examples of successful companies using social media."

I've been struggling with this assignment for weeks now. And suddenly, my anxiety levels spike.

We rush through the paper, my mind racing with ideas. But I can't help feeling like this might be a sign of things to come - that technology will consume us completely, leaving nothing behind except memories of glitchy Instagram stories.

When we finish, I feel relieved. It wasn't perfect, but at least we made progress.

Except...

That night, my phone buzzes. There's a notification for a new Tweet from @socialmediaexpert.

"Don't worry, kids," he writes. "Technology isn't destroying society. It's creating it."

The rest of the evening feels like a blur. We talk about his perspective, about the potential benefits of social media, and about the ways in which it has changed communication.

As we leave, I feel a sense of hope rising up inside me. Maybe we're right - maybe technology won't kill society, after all. Maybe we just have to learn to use it responsibly.

And then, a few days later, the next tweet comes through.

"Social media doesn't create anything. People create themselves."

It's from @realjessicaparker.

Her words ring true.

In the end, I don't know what happened. Maybe she's right. Or maybe it's just a fluke - a random occurrence of someone taking a stand against technology-induced societal destruction.

Regardless, it makes me realize something important. That despite the constant barrage of information flooding our screens every minute of every day, we still need to remember why we started using these tools in the first place.

Maybe we need to find ways to incorporate them into our lives instead of simply consuming them. Maybe we need to hold onto the values that brought us together in the first place - compassion, empathy, curiosity. Because even though technology may change the way we communicate, it's not going to change the human spirit.

Anger at how easily someone could gain access to such sensitive information. And anger at the fact that no action was taken against them before they did any damage.

Overall, the experience taught me a valuable lesson about trust, communication, and the importance of holding people accountable for their actions.

outputs: Text: I've always been fascinated by how plants grow and reproduce. One day, while wandering through our local botanical garden, I stumbled upon this plant with these weird flowers. They looked like giant dicks. At first, I thought it might be edible - I mean, what else could they possibly be? But then I realized that they were part of a symbiotic relationship between a parasite and its host. It turns out that these strange-looking flowers are actually the larvae of a moth species, and their purpose is to feed on the sap of the host tree. As I watched them transform overnight into tiny adult moths, I couldn't help but wonder about the ecological consequences of such a mutually beneficial arrangement. What would happen if those same moths suddenly disappeared from their hosts' trees? Would the entire forest collapse under their weight? Was there anything humans could do to mitigate this potential disaster? That question kept haunting me throughout the rest of the trip, even as I continued exploring the gardens and marveling at the beauty of nature.

outputs:
Text: I recently bought a new laptop with an intel core i3 processor, running Windows 8. My previous laptop had a AMD quad core processor, running Windows 7. I tried to install both drivers and applications and found nothing wrong with either, except for some apps won't run on Windows 8. After a few days of trying different solutions provided by Microsoft support, including updating the BIOS, I decided to upgrade to Windows 7 SP1. Here are some issues I encountered while upgrading:
1) One of my printers doesn't print correctly; instead of printing the right page, it prints multiple pages at once.
2) Some games won't launch, but others will open and close without any errors.
3) Many websites and programs won't load properly.
4) Sometimes, if I move my mouse cursor over certain areas of the screen, they appear briefly before disappearing again.
5) Whenever I click on a link, the browser window closes immediately.
6) Some software won't recognize any hardware devices, such as USB drives or network cards.
7) At least three different types of keyboard shortcuts fail entirely.
8) The Start menu doesn't always display the correct items, especially for newer versions of Office.
9) When I go to download a program, sometimes it takes several tries before I finally succeed.
10) Sometimes, when I log in, the user account picture disappears, leaving me with a blank image.
I also noticed that many programs seem to crash randomly, although there were some exceptions. To fix these problems, I installed the latest updates for each application, reset the registry, removed unnecessary files, and disabled some services. This may not solve everything, but hopefully it helps you identify what might be causing your problems.

Text: I just realized after I wrote that last line that "broken" isn't quite right. So, instead of breaking my back, I broke my neck. It's kind of weird because I don't remember falling...

      And then I woke up like this.
      A broken neck. No memory of falling. But somehow, even though it hurts like hell, I know I need to keep breathing. I need to keep moving.

      I can't explain it to anyone else. Not even myself. I can barely understand it myself sometimes. But I know deep down that it's true.
      This will happen again. Somewhere. At some point.
      Maybe it won't hurt as bad next time. Or maybe it won't come at all. Who knows? All I know is that I've been told that I'll never forget this experience, that it changed me forever.
      
  

I hope this helps!

Text: I woke up at midnight because my alarm clock rang at 3am. I spent the next hour lying awake, trying to fall back asleep without success. Then, suddenly, I heard something move outside my window. It sounded like a cat, maybe even a mouse, so I got up and opened the curtains to check. There, standing motionless on the sidewalk across from my house, was a giant rat. Its eyes were wide open, its tail twitched, and it seemed contentedly snoring.

I froze, paralyzed by terror. How had it come inside my home without anyone seeing it? Had it been hiding under the mattress? Was it planning some kind of attack on me? What could I do to stop it?

As the minutes ticked past, my mind raced with ideas. Could I call animal control? Would someone find me later? Maybe I should call the police? But then, something clicked in my brain. This wasn't a normal rodent. Something big and terrifying was lurking nearby. And I needed to figure out what it was and how to get rid of it.

I closed my eyes tightly and took deep breaths. When I opened them again, the rat was gone. It had vanished like a ghost, leaving behind nothing but the empty space where it once stood.

The experience left me feeling both frightened and exhilarated. On one hand, I felt grateful that I had escaped such a potentially deadly predicament. On the other hand, I wondered whether animals were truly invisible to humans - perhaps they simply weren't visible enough to bother us. Either way, I knew that if I ever encountered another creature like that again, I would know exactly what to do.

Her smile seemed genuine and heartwarming, like she knew exactly why I was feeling so grateful. I remember thinking that perhaps fate had intervened yet again to give us both something special that we wouldn't otherwise have been able to experience alone.

 Output: Neighbor invites author to meet after finding flower bouquet while walking home

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: A group of us were talking about what we could do to celebrate our friend's birthday next month. One idea was to make him his own cake, decorated with pictures of himself. Another was to send him a video message saying how much we love him and wish him a happy birthday.

The first idea seemed too difficult to execute. We talked about having some sort of potluck party where everyone brought something delicious to share. Then I thought, "What if we just made his favorite dessert?" That sounded easy enough!

I spent the next hour browsing through recipes for chocolate chip cookies, figuring that someone else might know exactly what I was thinking. Eventually, I settled on these instructions:

Ingredients:
- 8 oz semisweet chocolate chips
- 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
- 1 large egg
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 cup powdered sugar
- Confectioners' sugar, for dusting

Instructions:
1. Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. Melt the chocolate chips in a double boiler or microwave. Let cool slightly.
3. Using an electric mixer, beat the eggs together with the vanilla extract until frothy. Add the melted chocolate mixture, followed by the flour and powdered sugar. Beat until smooth.
4. Stir in the confectioners' sugar. If the dough seems dry, add more powdered sugar until it reaches your desired consistency.
5. Roll the dough into balls between 1/4" and 1/2" thickness. Place them on the prepared baking sheet, leaving space between each cookie. Flatten each ball slightly with the back of a fork.
6. Bake for 9-11 minutes, or until the edges are golden brown. Allow the cookies to cool completely on the baking sheet before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely. Enjoy!

We also came up with a funny video message using the same theme - a video of us singing Happy Birthday to our friend. It turned out quite hilarious, and ended up being a hit among the other participants.

Input:
outputs: Text: I hate going to bed at night. It's always been that way since I was a child. My mother used to make sure I got some exercise during the day and tried her best to keep me busy, but eventually, she realized I couldn't function without sleep. Nowadays, I've developed a bit of an addiction to Netflix. I don't know why exactly, but whenever I watch something, I fall asleep. And if I wake up early enough, I'll watch another episode, too. But what really annoys me? When people come over. They sit there and talk for hours, watching TV and talking about nothing. What's worse is when they start asking questions, and I feel like I need to tell them everything. About my dreams, my fears, my past mistakes. All kinds of stuff. Like, seriously, how many times has someone told you that they love your eyes? Or that they want to touch your hair? Why does everyone care so much? Because they want to look good? Is that all they're thinking about? "Oh, my God! You look beautiful!" "I love your earrings!" "Your hair looks great tonight." "You look amazing in that dress!" So what's wrong with wanting to be noticed? Doesn't anyone else find that kind of attention annoying? It makes me feel small. As though I don't belong. Even if I'm just sitting alone in my room, surrounded by books and blank walls, waiting for the world to pass me by. And yet, somehow, even when I'm lying awake staring at the ceiling, trying to figure out whether I'd rather be a rock star or a scientist, the urge to watch TV doesn't ever leave me. Not even when I know that my roommates are sleeping soundly next door. This isn't something that will disappear soon. There's no cure for a craving like this. No pill or therapy that could give me back my sanity. So maybe I should just accept that I'm an addict. That I can't control my desires. Maybe I should stop trying to convince others that I'm normal. That I shouldn't be afraid to admit that sometimes, I just want to curl up in a ball and cry.

Input:
outputs: Text: I hate when people talk too much while I eat dinner.  It's like they want to fill their whole mouth with food before starting talking again.  So what if they start talking anyway?  But then they stop mid sentence, look down at their plate, and continue chatting.  And I'm trying to concentrate on my food, so it seems like they're really busy.  If someone were to ask me how I felt during that conversation, I wouldn't know whether I liked them or not.  But if they said something funny, I could probably tell.  So maybe some tips for communicators: keep your voice low, avoid eye contact (except when looking at your food), don't interrupt other conversations unless absolutely necessary, and always finish your sentence first.

Text: I've been reading about how people use Twitter to spread fake news. Some of these stories are quite ridiculous! Here's an example from the Daily Mail (UK):

> A man has died after falling off his bike in Glasgow during a charity ride organised by a local charity. The cyclist fell over 20ft onto concrete slabs at the rear of the building. He sustained serious injuries and later died in hospital.

The article claims that the cyclist fell because he was trying to make the perfect video clip for social media, but unfortunately the cycling accident happened instead. It also states that the victim, named Jamie Smith, was raising money for his mental health treatment.

I immediately clicked'retweet'. I couldn't believe what I was seeing.

The headline read: Cyclist Falls Over Concrete Slabs During Charity Ride And Dies In Hospital.

As soon as I hit'reply', I got another message saying:

"This story is absolutely absurd. Who cares if someone fell off their bike? Why aren’t we talking about some actual tragedies happening right now? Get a life."

One person even called the article “misinformation” and accused me of being a liar. But the more I looked at it, the more I realized that something wasn't right.

There were other articles on the same page about a woman giving birth in a police station, and a man stabbing himself in a park. These stories weren't funny either – they were tragic and sad.

I decided to investigate further. After clicking'source', I found out that the original article was published by the Daily Record newspaper in Scotland. The report was based on a press release sent to the Press Association by the Scottish Police Authority, stating that Jamie Smith, who was in his early twenties, had suffered multiple broken ribs and pelvis injuries when he fell. However, the article failed to mention any details about why he fell or whether anyone else was hurt in the incident.

After investigating further, I discovered that the Daily Mail was paraphrasing the press release without actually quoting the full statement. They used quotes that sounded suspiciously similar to the ones originally provided by the Scottish Police Authority. This meant that the article had taken information directly from the source without checking its accuracy.

Social media was responsible for spreading this type of misinformation, which led to many innocent lives being put at risk. People believed that the headlines were true simply because they shared them on Facebook, rather than taking the time to fact check the sources themselves.

In conclusion, I urge readers to be cautious when sharing fake news stories on social media platforms. Fact-checking websites such as Snopes and Politifact offer reliable information that can help us identify falsehoods and prevent harm. By following these tips, we can ensure that social media doesn't contribute to the spread of fake news and protect ourselves and others from potential danger.

Text: yesterday I got a letter from my dad telling me that I won $500 on an online slot machine game! Wow, what does that mean?

The next few days turned into a whirlwind of excitement, anxiety, relief, happiness, and maybe even some jealousy. It felt good to finally have something positive happen after months of being a total loser. I was thrilled to share my good fortune with my family, especially my mom who has always been supportive despite her own financial struggles.

I spent most of the day savoring the news and taking pictures of myself with the winning ticket. Then, as the sun began to set over the horizon, I realized that I needed to make plans quickly if I wanted to claim my prize. My phone buzzed with notifications, and my heart skipped a beat when I read the message.

“Congratulations! You’ve won a grand prize of $250,000!” A smile spread across my face, and tears welled up in my eyes. “What else can I do?” I asked myself. “Take a picture of myself holding the ticket and send it to my parents.”

That night, I sat down at my computer and typed out the instructions for sending the photo. As soon as I hit ‘send,' my fingers clicked repeatedly on the keyboard, and the image popped up on my screen. It looked great, except for one thing – the quality wasn’t very good. I took another shot, hoping to improve upon the previous attempt. After multiple attempts, I finally received confirmation that my photo had been successfully uploaded.

Next, I decided to reach out to a friend whose father works at the same company as mine. He happened to know someone who might be able to help me win the money. To my surprise, he agreed to meet me at his office for a quick chat about the details of how the lottery worked. We talked about my story, how much I loved playing slots games, and why I deserved such a huge reward. He told me that sometimes, life gives us unexpected blessings, and I had definitely earned this victory.

As we exchanged pleasantries, I couldn't help but feel grateful for this chance encounter. My mind raced back to that day when I found the winning ticket. I remembered feeling relieved, excited, happy, and proud. But more importantly, I remembered the emotions that came along with it – fear, uncertainty, confusion, joy, and love. Those moments will forever remain etched in my memory.

In conclusion, winning a big jackpot isn't necessarily about having the best hand. Sometimes, it's about being lucky enough to catch the right combination of events. This experience taught me valuable lessons about perseverance, gratitude, and appreciation. Most importantly, it showed me that even small victories can lead to bigger ones.

Initially, I wasn't sure how to handle the sudden change in my life, but I knew I needed to keep moving forward. That meant taking some time off and figuring out what my next steps were. One thing led to another and before I knew it, I landed a new job at a startup. The culture there was really inspiring and challenging at the same time. I felt more confident than ever and was able to grow professionally while also maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Now, after working there for nearly a year, I feel like I've finally hit my stride. I'm making progress towards achieving my career goals and enjoying every moment along the way. My current role involves managing teams across multiple departments, and I'm excited to continue learning and growing in that area. I'm grateful for everything that has happened thus far and look forward to continuing to advance in my career.

The reason why I did not follow the company's policies was that I was tired after working full days and nights, and therefore couldn't keep up with the schedule. This also included having personal life responsibilities such as attending college classes during weekends, volunteering in my community, etc., that took most of my free time.

Furthermore, my bosses seemed more interested in maintaining their power rather than ensuring employee satisfaction. They constantly micromanaged us, which resulted in stress levels increasing daily. It became impossible for me to manage my time effectively since I was always juggling multiple tasks simultaneously.

I decided to quit my job without any hesitation. The decision wasn't easy; however, I knew that if I continued working under these conditions, I wouldn't be able to continue living a fulfilling life. Moreover, I wanted to focus on pursuing other interests and achieving academic success. Therefore, I decided to start over again, taking advantage of opportunities that presented themselves along the way.

Overall, I believe that quitting my job was the best thing that ever happened to me. It gave me freedom, allowed me to explore new possibilities, and provided me with valuable skills that I will use throughout my career journey.

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

outputs:
Text: I recently learned how to play the guitar! It's been years since I picked up an instrument and I feel like a kid again. 

Now fast forward to this weekend where I decided to start playing at a local jam session. As soon as I sat down, I felt like I knew what I was doing. I played a few songs and everyone loved them! But then something weird happened. My fingers were getting tired and I kept losing my rhythm. After a while, I stopped playing altogether and took a break. 

I couldn't believe what I was hearing. Everyone else seemed to be having fun, even though they weren't playing as good as me. And that's when I remembered what my friend told me - don't compare yourself to others. You may not sound exactly like someone else, but you might be better than their best song ever written. 

So I decided to focus on improving myself instead of comparing myself to other musicians. That's when the idea came to me. Why not write my own song? It wouldn't be perfect, but it would show people what I've learned and hopefully inspire some new ideas too. So I spent last night writing a rough draft and tonight I will perform it for the first time. 

Fast forward to next weekend and another opportunity to improve. This time I'll attend a guitar lesson where I'll learn some basic chords and techniques. It won't be easy, but I know I'll enjoy learning. And maybe someday, I'll become good enough to play at a concert. 

And before you ask "how did she know she wanted to play guitar?" I'll tell you. Last Christmas, my sister gave me a book called "The Guitar Method" by Michael Hedges. She knew I liked music and books related to it. I read it and it changed everything. I practiced every single day and within a month, I could hold a note. From that moment on, I never looked back.

Text: last night I decided to go for an adventure by driving myself over to the mountains to see some wildlife.

   I drove through the winding mountain roads, feeling the wind whipping past me and listening to the rustling leaves underfoot. As I approached the summit, the landscape changed dramatically - towering peaks, jagged cliffs, and vast expanses of snow-covered terrain.

The sun was setting, casting long, deep shadows across the valley below. I parked the car near a small stream and began walking towards it. It was then when I saw something moving in the bushes nearby – a group of deer! They stood motionless, watching me approach slowly.

As I got closer, I could hear the soft bleat of the young buck and his mother's heartbeats echoing in the air. A moment later, the male deer emerged from the brush and stared straight at me. Its large brown eyes seemed to pierce right through me.

I couldn't believe it; I was surrounded by these magnificent creatures! Their antlers gleamed in the moonlight, and their fur was a warm golden color against the dark winter forest. They stood perfectly still, waiting for me to pass before running away.

For a few moments, we stood there together, frozen in silence, each lost in our own thoughts. Then suddenly, the young buck turned its head and gave me a wide smile, while the mom grunted and moved her head slightly to indicate that she wasn't happy with me disturbing her territory.

My heart raced with excitement and fear as I watched the deer disappear into the woods. For the next hour, I walked alone along the path, taking pictures of the beautiful scenery and enjoying the peacefulness of nature.

Finally, after what felt like forever, I found myself returning to civilization. I stopped at a gas station to refuel my car, and when I looked up, I realized that the sky was starting to turn pink.

That day, I left feeling awestruck by the beauty of the natural world. And though I knew I wouldn't forget the experience anytime soon, I also knew that the memories would always remain vividly etched in my mind.

Text: I don’t know why I put up with him, but I did. I thought maybe if I kept him at arm’s length, he wouldn’t notice his own stupidity and stop asking for money from me. He never seemed to understand that I could afford to live without his help, but he always found ways to make himself useful – whether it meant cooking dinner for us, cleaning the house, or helping me write papers for college.
I’ve tried everything. But somehow he keeps coming right back. This time, though, something clicked inside me. It wasn’t enough to simply refuse him; I needed to confront him head-on. And so I did.
I called him out on his behavior, reminding him that I deserved better than to live like a slave. We talked for an hour, and I left feeling more free than ever before. That night, when I lay awake thinking about him, I realized something else too.
He doesn’t want to be alone. Not even close. He wants someone to love and cherish him, someone to share his life with. If he can’t find that person in me, then he will move on. But I won’t let him leave me empty-handed.
And so I stood by my decision. For the first time since I met him, I knew what I truly wanted. I’d taken a chance on myself, and I’d paid it off.

Text: 
"you know what? I don't even care anymore!" - Axl Rose



i used to hate being a rockstar when I first got signed by my label. It felt like an eternity waiting for them to make a decision about whether they wanted to sign us or not. But over time I learned to embrace the pressure. Now I live for it.






i always thought I could handle anything life threw at me. That was before I became a parent. My wife has been very supportive throughout her pregnancy, especially since she knows how much I love kids. She was there to help out during the delivery, hold the baby while I recovered, and keep everything together once the newborn arrived.






so I took a break from writing to spend some quality time with my family. We went hiking, swimming, and played board games. And although it wasn't exactly a vacation, it did feel like one. I miss being able to escape into stories and worlds for a little bit each day.





the thing is, I never want to stop writing again. Not ever. But I also realize that sometimes it takes more than just words to connect with people. Sometimes it takes heartache, pain, and even tragedy. Writing can help me process those experiences, but it doesn't change the fact that they happened. They hurt.

So I decided to write a book about grief. One that isn't necessarily about losing someone close to me, but rather exploring the emotions that come with letting go of something dear to your heart. Because in the end, it’s about finding hope and joy amidst loss.

I've known for years that I needed to find a creative outlet to cope with my own struggles. But I never knew where to start. Until recently, I thought that art was limited to visual forms. I mean, why would anyone create a story based on their own personal experience? It seemed too limiting.

But then I discovered poetry. For me, poetry allows me to express myself in ways that other mediums simply cannot. When I sit down to write a poem, I often forget that it's not just about words on paper. It's about feelings and emotions. It's about connection. It's about making sense of the world.

In creating this book, I found that writing poetry helped me explore these deeper emotional issues in a way that words alone couldn't. I learned to trust my instincts and listen closely to the messages that were being sent to me. I realized that writing is a form of self-expression, and that I have a voice that needs to be heard.

The book itself is called "Lost Ground". It's a tribute to the landscapes and people I've lost along the way. These places may seem small compared to the expansiveness of nature, but they hold memories and connections that are worth cherishing. Throughout the book, I draw upon the beauty of the natural world to inspire my writing. Each page holds a message of hope and resilience, reminding readers that despite the darkness, there is always light to be found.

And though the journey to publication was difficult, I wouldn't trade it for anything else. Creating this book gave me a sense of purpose and direction. It allowed me to tap into my own inner strength and to use my gift to help others. Whether I'm sharing my thoughts on social media, speaking publicly about mental health, or sitting down to write, I will continue to do what I do best – tell stories that matter.

Text: I hate the new way that stores charge for parking! It makes no sense why they would charge more than $2 for just parking. I don’t even park there anymore. If I need to go somewhere, I will walk unless I know someone who lives nearby.

Suggested Solution:
This could be turned into a humorous essay by adding some satirical elements to the story. Here's a possible revised version:

I Hate the New Way That Stores Charge For Parking!

It's frustrating when you can't afford to pay extra for a spot, especially during peak hour traffic. But then again, I never needed to pay extra for parking before. Not only does it make no sense, but it also takes away from the convenience factor. How convenient is it to simply walk to your destination instead of driving? Especially since most stores are located right next door to each other.

As soon as I saw the sign announcing the additional fee, I rolled my eyes. Why did they feel the need to charge such exorbitant amounts for basic needs? Maybe they think that customers are stupid enough to believe that paying extra for a parking space is worth the inconvenience. However, it doesn't seem like they understand that many people actually value convenience over price tags.

If I needed to use the store's services, I wouldn't mind shelling out a few dollars more. After all, the convenience of walking straight to the front entrance without worrying about finding a parking spot saves time and energy. Plus, I get to avoid the stressful process of navigating through crowded streets.

Moreover, some stores might argue that they offer free shuttle service to those who cannot walk to their location. While this may sound nice, it's often impractical and expensive for businesses. Who has the time or resources to chauffeur clients to and from their premises? Additionally, some locations require reservations, which means that people with mobility issues might miss out on their desired visit due to lack of availability.

To sum it up, charging for parking seems like a waste of money and an unnecessary burden on both the customer and the store. Instead, I suggest implementing a system whereby customers are charged according to distance traveled, rather than per-space usage. This would allow individuals to choose whether to spend more money or less on parking, depending on their specific needs. Furthermore, it would create a more equitable system that benefits both customers and businesses alike.

fuck me. i'm cringing.

Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Input: Text: tifu. i was in line at the gas station, waiting to pay for my soda and gas, when i saw a quarter on the packs of gum directly in front of the counter. when it was my turn to pay i bent over and scooped up the quarter, and put it in my pocket, forgetting about it instantly. putting my soda on the counter and reaching for my wallet, i looked up and saw the cashier eyeing me with an angry glare. i was confused by this. was she mad at my choice of soda? (she could be one of those freaks that prefer pepsi) did i have an offensive t shirt on? (not unless she's offended by my obscure podcast shirt) 

i say "......$40 on 2 please." and she responds with "what's in your pocket?" 

"huh?" i stammer before finally understanding. "oh! i didn't steal anything!" and proceed to fervently pull everything out of my pockets, dropping change, and other things. i pick up the 25 cent culprit and thrust it to the cashier, as if it proved my story somehow, and explained that i had just seen the quarter on the gum and nabbed it.

 her face hadn't changed at all during the entire exchange. she finally just completed my transaction and said have a nice day. i'm not sure if she believed me or not, but i gathered all my stuff and hightailed it out of there.
Output: i found a quarter on a display of gum, cashier thought i was blatantly stealing gum right in front of her.
