Text: This happened last night. I can barely remember anything that happened yesterday except for the fact that I lost my keys. But since I can only recall bits and pieces, here goes nothing:

I was walking home after dinner when I noticed something strange - the streetlight outside my house wasn't lit up properly. It seemed to be flickering, making everything seem very dark around me. At first, I thought maybe it was just the weather, but then I realized it wasn't; I couldn't see anything beyond a few feet in front of me. Panic set in as I tried to think of what could possibly cause such a disaster. Then, it hit me - I left my keys in the car overnight. I knew right then and there that I needed to check my keys before bedtime tonight, so I decided to walk back to my car instead of taking the elevator. As soon as I got inside, I turned around to see if anyone else had seen my keys lying on the ground next to the door. There was no one around. I quickly grabbed them and put them into my pocket. When I looked back out the window, I saw a group of people coming towards me. They stopped in front of my car, and I watched as they started to pull some kind of device out of their pockets. It sounded like a loud whine and humming noise. Suddenly, the light bulb above the key ring fell onto the floor, shattering into thousands of tiny glass fragments. I jumped backwards, feeling like I had just stepped into a minefield. I ran through the alleyway behind my building, trying to avoid any debris that may have fallen nearby. My heart was pounding in my chest as I reached my car. What had just happened? Had someone stolen my keys again? Was it possible that my keys had been taken by someone who had been following me all along? After driving for several blocks without seeing any sign of life, I finally pulled into a parking garage near my building. Once inside, I locked the doors and sat down, trying to calm myself down. The incident had made me feel extremely anxious, and I didn't know whether to stay inside or continue on my journey. Eventually, I decided to drive further, hoping to find someone who might have witnessed the crime. By the time I arrived at the intersection where I usually turn onto my usual route, I was exhausted. I had been driving for nearly four hours straight, and my headache had become almost too much to bear. I parked my car on the sidewalk, and I stood there, waiting for whatever would happen next. I listened intently as cars honked their horns, pedestrians passed by, and sirens waved frantically overhead. All around me, the sounds of chaos echoed, filling my ears. Suddenly, a woman appeared in front of me. She wore a bright red coat and carried a small bag with her. Her eyes were wide and concerned, and she approached me hesitantly. "Excuse me," she said softly. "Can I help you?" I nodded politely. "My name is Lena," she continued. "Do you live here?" I shook my head. "No, I live across town. I'm on my way to pick up some groceries." "Oh, okay," she replied, looking disappointed. "Well, good luck finding your way back!" With that, she walked away, disappearing into the crowd. I remained standing there for a moment longer, listening to the cacophony of traffic and footsteps until I finally made my decision. I drove slowly back toward my neighborhood, stopping frequently to examine each corner and make sure nobody was watching me. Finally, I arrived back at my own building. I opened the door, stepped inside, and breathed deeply, relieved that the worst had not happened. The sun began to rise as I returned to my usual routine. However, as I walked past the elevators, I suddenly remembered why I hadn't bothered to lock them earlier. Without thinking, I pressed the button marked 'elevator'. To my surprise, the elevator began moving, carrying me up to the third floor. I climbed aboard, and within seconds, the elevator doors slammed shut. I immediately pressed the button marked 'floor', and waited nervously for the doors to open. When they did, I stepped out into a room filled with bright lights and polished wood floors. A tall man with a shock of blond hair and piercing blue eyes greeted me warmly. He introduced himself as Mr. Johnson, the owner of the building. We talked for a while, exchanging pleasantries, before I left him alone to finish his morning business. From there, things became increasingly hectic. People kept knocking on my door, asking questions, demanding answers, or simply wanting to share their experiences with me. Some of them even showed up with flowers or small gifts. Despite these encounters, however, I never once felt unsafe or threatened. Everyone was friendly and welcoming, despite the circumstances. I even met a couple of friendly neighbors, who offered to show me around the block and introduce me to their favorite restaurants. Overall, I felt incredibly grateful for the experience. I learned a valuable lesson about being prepared and being aware of my surroundings. I am confident that I will always carry those lessons with me wherever I go, knowing that I am well equipped to handle any unexpected situations that may arise.

Input: Text: obligatory comment about this not actually happening today, and this being a throwaway account.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: "I can't believe I have to pay for college."

As soon as I stepped foot onto campus, I knew I would need to work extra hard if I wanted to make ends meet. But it wasn't until I realized that I needed a full-time job that I started feeling truly overwhelmed. It seemed like every other student was doing something to earn some cash; however, mine kept falling through the cracks. After several weeks of searching, I finally found an entry level position that paid $7/hour. I worked during the day, attending classes at night, and spent every spare moment trying to save up enough money to cover rent and groceries. It wasn't easy - working multiple jobs left no room for anything else. And yet, despite these challenges, I refused to let my financial burdens consume me. I continued to push forward, determined to achieve my goals. By taking on odd jobs here and there, I managed to save enough money to cover my living expenses for a semester. That's where things got tricky though. When the summer rolled around, I still hadn't saved enough to cover tuition fees. My family couldn't afford any additional debts, so I had to find alternative ways to pay for school. I began volunteering at a local hospital, where I could earn free housing and healthcare benefits. This allowed me to continue my education without worrying about costly expenses. Despite facing many obstacles along the way, I persevered. Through hard work, determination, and a little bit of luck, I eventually landed a full-time job. Today, I am able to support myself financially and pursue my dreams. Looking back now, I realize that having to work multiple jobs throughout college was a crucial part of achieving my educational goals. It taught me valuable skills such as resilience, resourcefulness, and independence.

Text: i got a phone call from my bestie yesterday afternoon asking if I wanted to go to the beach today. Of course! It's been months since I haven't gone to the beach. So naturally, I agreed.

But when I arrived, she had already booked a cab. And she wasn't even happy about it either. She insisted on waiting outside, despite the fact that I was supposed to meet her right here, inside the hotel lobby. I didn't care about her feelings, but the idea of being stuck in an empty hotel room alone during the heatwave sounded horrifying to me. I decided to take matters into my own hands.

I walked up to the reception desk and asked for a key to the room. After a brief conversation, I was able to get it. As soon as I entered the room, however, something strange happened. My bestie sat down beside me, still talking loudly to the other guests. I turned to face her, trying to find any signs of hostility, only to see her staring blankly ahead, as though lost in thought. This wasn't good. What kind of person is this?

The next few hours passed in a blur. We hung out, played games, and watched movies together. But every so often, she started to lose track of time. Whenever someone called her name, she would pause whatever she was doing, looking around for the source of the noise. At some point, I realized that I couldn't keep living like this anymore. I needed to make a decision, fast.

So, without warning, I grabbed my bag and left. Without saying goodbye, I stepped out onto the balcony. The sun beat down on us, and I breathed deeply, feeling alive once more. For the rest of the trip, everything else fell into perspective. I appreciated the little things, like the sound of waves crashing against the shore or the smells of fresh flowers wafting through the air. I learned to appreciate the simple pleasures of life, rather than always chasing after the big ones.

When I returned home, my bestie was surprised. I explained why I had to leave. She listened patiently, nodding along occasionally, until eventually, she too began to smile. We talked about how much we missed each other, and how grateful we were to finally be reunited. That night, we shared a warm meal and a bottle of wine, holding hands as we watched the stars twinkling above.

It was hard to say goodbye that evening, but I knew deep down that it was necessary. I never wanted to forget that summer, or the love I found in that small town. Maybe someday, we'll go back and relive those memories. Or maybe we won't. Either way, I know that I can handle anything life throws my way, as long as I remember to cherish the moments that matter most.

“The most powerful way to connect with customers is by telling stories,” says James Patchett, author of “Stories That Make You Think.”

Patchett’s book is packed full of examples, including a woman who learned her husband was dying and then wrote him a letter describing their life together; a traveler who lost everything in Hurricane Katrina and ended up saving $20 million in diamonds; and a businessman who created the “Made in America” slogan. He argues that companies need to find their own unique narrative, rather than simply repeating corporate messages.

In a recent interview with Forbes, Patchett explains why his approach differs from others in the field.

“It starts with the company culture,” he says. “When people know where they fit within the organization, they become more engaged, invested, and committed to making things better."

He also points out that storytelling isn’t only important for personal brands – it can help build stronger relationships between organizations and communities.

"Storytelling helps us understand each other," he adds. "If I tell you a story about my family, you may think differently about my politics. If I tell you a story about a customer service experience, you may think differently about the company I represent."

Patchett emphasizes that effective storytellers aren’t afraid to get emotional.

“They make themselves vulnerable and share their pain, fears, and hopes,” he says. "That’s the best kind of emotion anyone wants to feel. It makes them human, relatable, and authentic."

For example, consider a company that struggles to engage its customers online. By sharing stories of successful campaigns or moments of community building, it could show customers that it cares about their lives beyond transactions.

“You want people to care enough to stick around," Patchett notes. "By being true to yourself and showing that you care about your audience, you’ll create a loyal base of fans."

To learn more about storytelling, check out Patchett’s website at jamespatchett.com.

Text: I’ve always been fascinated by people who live off the grid, living completely self sufficient and being able to go without modern conveniences. For years I thought this was only possible for wealthy individuals, but after reading a few books on sustainable living I realized that anyone can do it! So far, I’ve lived for several months without any major technology, and it has been amazingly rewarding.
I think the hardest part of going “off the grid” is finding your own water source. It wasn’t too difficult to find somewhere nearby where the water was safe to drink – we just used a reverse osmosis system to purify it. Once we found a good spot, it was easy to install a solar panel to power our fridge/freezer, clothes dryer, and other basic appliances. We also built a rainwater catchment system using a simple plastic bucket filled with sand, rocks, and gravel.
The biggest challenge for us was learning how to grow food. Our garden is mostly herbs and vegetables, with some fruit trees scattered around. We started with nothing more than seeds and sticks, and within weeks, we had enough plants to start growing fresh produce. This was definitely the most challenging aspect of going “off the grid,” since we needed to learn everything from scratch.
Another thing that was very different was managing money. Since we didn’t have access to traditional banking systems, we created our own payment system based on bartering. Bartering allows us to exchange goods for services rather than buying things for cash. We started with bartering locally, exchanging supplies for items we couldn’t get elsewhere. As word spread, we began to offer services such as laundry, cleaning, and dog walking. We also offered gift certificates for local businesses, which helped to create a sense of community among our neighbors.
It was incredibly rewarding to know that we could provide for ourselves without relying on the standard consumer culture. Living off the grid taught me many valuable lessons about resourcefulness, independence, and mindful consumption.

Output: The next time you find yourself in a dangerous situation, don't hesitate to use your common sense and turn the damn thing off!

Writing this essay made me realize that I needed to prioritize self-care and seek help when I needed it. Input:
outputs: Text: I’ve been trying to get into shape since high school. It started off slow; I’d go jogging once a week during lunchtime. Then I added weight training, which required me to buy gym memberships and pay monthly fees. And then I realized that my body wasn’t changing. Maybe it wasn’t supposed to change, maybe it needed to shrink, but still, it didn’t feel good. So I stopped exercising altogether. Now, here I am, mid-forties, sitting at home with nothing better to do than watch TV. But I don’t want to watch TV. I want to run. Not fast, mind you—I’ll never break six miles—but steady, everyday runs around the block. Why now? Well, besides the fact that I’m getting older and less flexible, I have a job where I spend eight hours a day behind a desk. Running would help clear my head, reduce stress, improve my endurance. Plus, I could start small. Just five days a week. Five hundred steps. No problem. My wife thinks I’m crazy. “What are you thinking?” she asks, watching me walk through her neighborhood. “A workout,” I say, feeling foolish. “It sounds silly.” She looks up from her book and shakes her head. “This isn’t about being silly. This is about your health.” She gives me a stern look. "Okay," she says finally. “But let’s stick to running. You won’t gain any muscle. Weightlifting will only add bulk." I laugh. That’s why I love her. Because she’s right. And yet, I find myself starting to enjoy running. For the first few weeks, it feels awkward. I trip over things, fall onto my knee. But gradually, I get faster. And faster. By the second half of March, I’m doing fifty-minute runs. Twenty minutes longer each week. And I don’t even care. All those extra pounds aren’t going anywhere. Or rather, they’re falling off. One day, while I’m walking my dog, I hear the sound of metal against concrete. I stop to investigate. A man is throwing pots and pans. He’s standing next to his car, leaning over the wheel. “Four blocks to the station,” he says. “You can catch the bus.” I nod. I’ve lived in this town for years, and I know every corner. But still, it takes a moment for me to realize that I’m moving. The sunlight is warming my face. My breath comes in shallow gasps. I remember why I started running in the first place. I remember why I gave up exercise altogether. Because sometimes life gets in the way. Sometimes we forget to prioritize ourselves. But sometimes we also forget that we deserve to live a fuller life. And that includes taking care of ourselves physically and mentally.

Text: I am currently in college studying accounting and business administration. This semester has been nothing short of amazing, especially considering the fact that I have never even taken an accounting class before coming here. However, when I decided to major in marketing instead, I knew that I would need to learn about consumer behavior. And now that I’ve completed all 40 hours of required coursework, I finally got around to reading "The Consumer Behavior" by Robert Cialdini.

It’s a book full of fascinating research findings that explain why people buy certain products and behave in certain ways. It covers topics such as influence tactics, social proof, scarcity, and more. The author provides examples and case studies throughout the book to help illustrate his points. One thing I found particularly interesting was the concept of “social proof”. According to him, this refers to the idea that people tend to follow others’ actions rather than making decisions based solely on information alone. He uses a study where a group of people watched a video demonstration of a product being used by someone else. Afterward, some of those same people were shown pictures of similar products without any instructions or visual cues. When compared to those who saw no picture, the ones who watched the video demonstrated significantly higher levels of willingness to purchase the product. Another section covered the topic of “influence tactics”, which includes techniques such as the power of suggestion, authority, and reciprocity. This chapter also provided some great advice on how to create effective sales pitches. Overall, this book is well worth the read. If you’re interested in learning more about consumer behavior, I highly recommend picking up a copy.

Our drinks were being served from a separate station, and the server kept referring to our table as though we weren't even present.

At this point, I was starting to feel angry and frustrated. I knew I shouldn't have been upset - it wasn't fair that we needed to share a table with four other couples. But as I watched my date stare blankly ahead, trying to ignore the server's rudeness, I felt helpless. I wished I could just walk out of the restaurant and never return.

But before I could leave, the server returned with our dessert. She set a tiny glass of chocolate milk in front of my date, then turned to me and demanded, "What do you want?"

In that moment, I realized that I might never be able to eat a proper burger again.

outputs: Text: I've been feeling down lately. My girlfriend broke up with me last week, and I haven't talked to her about it yet. It feels like forever since we've seen each other. But I still love her. So why can't I bring myself to talk to her? Maybe it's because I feel guilty. Or maybe it's because I know I need to apologize sometime soon. I could always blame my feelings on being too busy, or too tired, or whatever else comes to mind. If only I knew what I needed to say to her. That's when I remembered something my grandfather used to say. He said that sometimes the best conversations start with silence. Like when you're driving your car and suddenly you hit a patch of ice and lose control. You stop and think before you react. Well, that's exactly what I did today. I stopped everything else and sat quietly in front of my girlfriend. She wasn't there, but I could hear her breathing next door. When I finally spoke, it was awkward. I couldn't quite put into words what I meant to say. We both looked at each other in confusion. Then, slowly, we started talking again. It wasn't perfect, but it was real. And it gave us time to process our emotions without anyone interrupting us. Afterwards, I drove home, thinking about how different our conversation could have gone. But instead, I found myself smiling, knowing that I learned something important about communication. Sometimes, all it takes is a little patience and willingness to listen. Output: sat alone in silence trying to figure out what to say to my ex-girlfriend, ended up learning about communication.

outputs: Text: I recently lost my job due to some personal issues and financial problems. My husband and I both worked very hard to make ends meet. We live paycheck-to-paycheck, but we never ever let anyone down financially. Our only debts were student loans and credit card balances. We always tried our best to pay them off every month and avoid accruing interest. Then everything changed. One day, my husband fell ill and had to take time off work. He couldn't continue his job search, and since I didn't want to quit mine, we ended up having to give notice. After months of searching for jobs, I finally landed an interview for a part-time position at a local restaurant. It wasn't exactly what I wanted, but it was enough to help support my family while I looked for something better. I started the new job on Monday and felt relieved that I was getting paid to eat dinner instead of eating leftovers. But things quickly began to fall apart. The first week, I received a call from my boss saying that they were laying off everyone except her department head. This left me feeling even more discouraged than before. The second week, I received a letter telling me that my salary was going to be reduced drastically. At first, I was angry. How could my boss expect me to sacrifice my own livelihood? However, I soon realized that this wasn't just about money. My health had been deteriorating over the past year, and my stress levels had become unmanageable. I knew that I needed to prioritize my mental wellbeing, so I decided to take a medical leave of absence. On the day I returned to work, I found that my boss had already laid off three employees. She informed me that she was implementing a "cutback" plan in order to save money. Needless to say, I was devastated. Not only had I lost my job, but I also lost my income. I struggled to come up with alternative sources of employment until I discovered that I could start my own business. My heart sunk again. Starting a small business meant taking on additional debt and sacrificing my savings for years to come. But I refused to let that stop me. With determination and perseverance, I set out to create a successful venture. Despite facing numerous obstacles along the way, I eventually opened my own cafe, complete with delicious food and friendly service. Now, six months later, I have been able to secure my dream job. I can't tell you how proud I am of myself. While there were certainly moments of struggle, I learned valuable lessons throughout the process. For example, I learned that no matter how much effort and dedication you put into your career, you will never truly achieve success unless you're willing to invest in yourself too. Another important lesson was learning to embrace uncertainty. Whenever I faced difficult situations, I reminded myself that failure isn't an option. Instead, I chose to approach each challenge with a positive attitude and creative solutions. Finally, I came to understand the importance of self-care. As much as possible, I sought out activities and hobbies that brought me joy outside of work. Whether it was volunteering at a local animal shelter or attending music festivals, these activities helped me maintain a sense of balance in my life. Overall, the experience has taught me to appreciate the little things in life. There may be ups and downs, but the key is to stay focused on your goals and remain resilient in the face of adversity.

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured. 

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Input:
outputs: Text: A few months ago I attended a conference where I spoke on stage. During the presentation, I made a mistake, and it didn't make it onto the recording. As soon as the presenter started announcing the next speaker, I felt a wave of nausea run through me. My heart began racing, and sweat dripped down my forehead. After the presenter announced our speaker, I walked over to her table, and asked her what happened. She replied that she had accidentally recorded the previous speaker instead of me. I quickly realized that my presentation was ruined, and I spent the rest of the day in tears. It wasn't until weeks later, after seeing the footage online, that I discovered that the video had been edited. Now, every time I hear the phrase "speechless" I think of this experience.

Input: Text: tifu. i was in line at the gas station, waiting to pay for my soda and gas, when i saw a quarter on the packs of gum directly in front of the counter. when it was my turn to pay i bent over and scooped up the quarter, and put it in my pocket, forgetting about it instantly. putting my soda on the counter and reaching for my wallet, i looked up and saw the cashier eyeing me with an angry glare. i was confused by this. was she mad at my choice of soda? Output: i found a quarter on a display of gum, cashier thought i was blatantly stealing gum right in front of her.

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Input: Text: obligatory comment about this not actually happening today, and this being a throwaway account.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: I bought some really good quality jeans online, they arrived last week and I am already loving them! However, I realized that I never wore the leggings with them before because I don't know how to put them on without making myself look ridiculous. I searched high and low online for instructions and finally found one. Here's what worked for me:
- Lay your legs flat across your chest
- Take a pair of scissors and cut along each leg (from the bottom to the top) until they meet in the middle.
- Slide both pieces downwards towards your knees. Make sure the cut line stays straight.
- Fold the shorter piece underneath the longer one, and bring the two sides together. Tuck the ends into the seam where they will sit when you put the pants on.
- Trim the excess fabric around the edges and press the pants firmly against your body.
I hope these tips help! They work perfectly every time. If anyone else has trouble putting on their leggings, try this method.

Text: I love hiking. It's a great exercise, gets me outside, fresh air, beautiful scenery...

but what I didn't realize was how bad it can get when I start packing too much stuff. When I finally reach the summit, all I want to do is collapse onto the ground, catch my breath, and enjoy the view. But when I open my backpack, I find myself covered in sandpaper and dirt, along with an assortment of sharp rocks, broken branches, and debris.

It wasn't until later that night that I realized how badly I messed up. As soon as I sat down to eat dinner, I noticed something odd happening in my stomach. It felt heavy, almost as though I was carrying around extra weight. My throat felt sore, and my eyes started to water frequently. I quickly took some antacids, hoping they would alleviate my discomfort. Unfortunately, they only seemed to make things worse. By the next morning, I was running on empty, feeling like I hadn't slept properly in weeks. I tried everything to try to feel better, but nothing worked. Finally, I found a local health clinic that specialized in treating hikers, and they diagnosed me with altitude sickness. After months of treatment, including prescription medication and therapy sessions, I am slowly recovering, but I will never forget the lesson learned. Don't pack too much gear!

Text: My cat died today. I didn’t know she would die today.


this has been a tough day.
I’m still crying over her loss.
The vet took her away early yesterday morning because she wasn’t responding well to pain medication. She passed peacefully this afternoon.


It’s hard knowing how much time I spent with her everyday. How many times did I hold her paw while she slept? How often did I rub her belly? What memories do I carry with me now?


My heart aches thinking about what I left behind, all those little moments where I just held her close and listened to her whimper. Now she won’t hear my voice again.


She was always there for me, no matter what. Whenever I was sad, scared, angry…she was always here to make everything better. And now, without her by my side, I feel lost.


But also, grateful. For having her, for loving her, for being able to spend countless hours with her each day. Even though it’s difficult, I am thankful for the precious gift she gave me.

Input: Text: i moved into my apartment in california a little over a year and a half ago, not thinking to see if the place had air conditioning. well, i quickly found out that it didn't and that my room would get hot as shit unless i had the blinds open for air flow. 

so why not just open the blinds?

because i sleep in the buff when it's really hot and more importantly, my neighbors window is directly across from mine. i didnt want to get on any list so i ended up buying one of those cheap tapestries off of amazon to use as a blind that would still let air/some light through but provided cover. i put it up and thought it looked great and just as i had hoped, i wasn't able to see through it. i figured the opposite was true so i opened the blinds and was greeted with a nice warm breeze and haven't adjusted closed the blinds since. 

fast forward to 5 minutes ago when i'm coming home and i realized that i left the light on which i'm usually 100% on. after looking up i realize the tapestry is actually semi-transparent and that got me started on  thinking about how i needed more stuff for my wall since it was pretty plain. 

then it fucking hit me. anyone could see me up there, especially my neighbor. granted, it was a bit blurred, but not anywhere near enough to make me comfortable.
Output: my neighbor probably knows more about my sex life than i do.

Text: today, I took a break from writing poetry (which has been taking up too much time) and went for a walk around our neighborhood. It's a quiet street, but sometimes you can hear the sound of cars passing by outside.

It felt peaceful.

I walked past some houses, and they all had flowers planted outside. I love flowers!

As I walked down the street, I noticed a small park where kids play basketball. A group of kids were playing, laughing, and having fun. They seemed to be enjoying themselves without being disturbed by adults.

Their energy made me happy.

I turned a corner, and I saw a mom carrying her baby in her arms. She was holding onto her baby tightly, rocking gently. Her hair was messy, but she looked content.

She was beautiful, no matter what.

When I reached the end of the block, I came upon an old man sitting on his porch. He was reading a book. His eyes were shut, and his head rested on his hand.

He looked serene.

I sat beside him and asked if he wanted anything to eat or drink.

"No thanks," he replied, "I've eaten already."

His words echoed throughout the street.

There was nothing else going on except us.

We talked about everything. About our lives, our dreams, and our fears.

At first, I felt uncomfortable talking to him because he appeared to be lonely. But soon, I began to feel connected to him, and it brought a smile to my face.

I learned that people are always ready to talk, even strangers.

My conversation with him helped me find peace within myself.

So next time you pass by an elderly person, stop and listen. You might learn something new.
Output: We talked about things we both knew, and eventually, he invited me to join him for coffee later.

Input: Text: i was drinking with friends from back home during the holidays like any other get together. we decided to get tequila, so of course we needed limes and a knife to cut them. after a few drinks i challenged my friend that i could cut a lime like fruit ninja if he threw them at me. the friend was concerned someone could get hurt, but i reassured him that i could it. standing about 8 feet apart, he threw the lime at me. i did not even see the lime, i did not even move, and it struck me right in the eye. i immediately had double vision and proceeded to throw up. the following days were met by a swollen eye and continued double vision, which i thought would go away after a few days. it did not. i then went to see a doctor, who said i would require surgery to fix this double vision issue. got the surgery and i still have double vision. the most expensive lime of my life.

outputs: Text: I've been on a journey through the deepest parts of the ocean floor, where nothing but darkness lay before me. It seemed like forever ago that I first stepped into those waters. But now, here I am, returning to the surface. The water around me was murky brown, with no visible signs of anything below. As I walked along the bottom, I began to notice strange patterns forming beneath me - they looked almost like land masses, yet completely out of place amongst the rocks and coral. They were unlike anything I had ever seen before; tall, thin structures that stretched towards the sky. Whenever I got close enough, I could see the intricate details etched onto their surfaces - small crevices, channels, and grooves all carefully carved out over millions upon millions of years. Each structure seemed to hold its own secrets, each different than the last. Suddenly, I felt a presence behind me, and turned to face what appeared to be a large sea creature, made entirely of glowing light. It seemed to be staring straight at me, its mouth gaping open wide. "What...are you?" I asked, feeling shaken by the sudden appearance of such an unknown entity. The creature seemed unsure of itself, its movements hesitant and uncertain. Finally, it spoke. "I am a being known only as 'The Shadow'," it replied. "You have come to our world seeking knowledge and understanding." "Why?" I asked, trying to sound confident. "Because," it answered, "you seek to destroy us." I couldn't believe what I was hearing. How could anyone want to harm the creatures living within these depths? And why wasn't there any warning signs, any indication that this might happen? For weeks, I explored deeper and deeper down, encountering new wonders and discoveries every day. I learned about the different types of marine organisms that lived among the dark, shadowy structures, how they communicated with each other using complex underwater languages. I found evidence of ancient civilizations, hidden in plain sight amidst the debris of old ships. I also discovered strange anomalies, such as underground cities that seemed to defy logic and reason. There were even rumors of alien encounters, stories passed down through generations of humans that described encounters with intelligent, advanced beings. I knew that I had uncovered something extraordinary, something beyond human comprehension. However, as I delved further, I realized that danger was closing in. A group of hunters had arrived on the scene, intent on capturing whatever precious treasures lay buried somewhere in these mysterious caverns. I knew that I had to act fast. With my newly acquired knowledge, I gathered a team of skilled divers and set off to locate the sources of the underwater energy that fueled these structures. Our mission became increasingly dangerous, as we encountered hostile creatures and unexpected obstacles. We faced waves of giant squids, whose tentacular appendages sliced through our lines with deadly precision. We battled against predators that darted across the walls of the caverns, hunting us relentlessly until finally, exhausted and battered, we emerged victorious. Despite the perilous conditions, we managed to recover a valuable artifact that contained information about the very origins of the underwater kingdoms. My discovery had led me to a vast network of ancient knowledge, hidden from view by centuries of ignorance. It was now clear that the true purpose of these structures lay far beyond mere entertainment or curiosity. Their power extended far beyond the confines of the earthly realm, reaching into the infinite expanse of space. From the depths of the oceans, to the far reaches of interstellar space, these structures held secrets that could change the fate of the universe. Yet, despite their immense importance, the creatures inhabiting these underwater kingdoms remained largely unknown to mankind. It was my duty to bring their existence to light, to educate the rest of the galaxy about the incredible things that existed within the boundaries of their watery homes.

outputs: Text: I’ve been trying to lose weight for over three years now, and while I haven't lost all the weight yet, I've definitely seen progress. Text: Background: I went hiking last weekend, and I got lost. It wasn’t too bad because I followed the trail signs (and yes, they were there) but when I realized I was lost, I felt really embarrassed. Luckily, I found myself and called out for help.

   So, my phone rang and I answered, "Hi." There was silence on the line for what seemed like forever before the person finally spoke. “I don't know where your cellphone is,” she said. “You might want to check the carrier.”

   Well, okay, maybe not exactly what happened, but basically, I asked her to look through her contacts list for my name, and sure enough, there it was! But apparently, it was blocked somehow? Either that or my phone had been rooted somehow, and I couldn't call anyone anymore.

The first thing I wanted to do was call my parents and tell them I was safe. However, since I was completely alone in the wilderness, I knew I wouldn't find an answer over the radio waves. Instead, I tried calling a local emergency number, and while they were able to connect me with some kind of dispatcher, I couldn't hear anything over the static. Eventually, though, a woman picked up the line and gave me instructions on how to proceed.

As I walked further and further away from civilization, I became increasingly frustrated. My phone battery had run out, leaving me with nothing more than a few flashlight batteries and my trusty headlamp. I was also running low on water, and although I could make it without much trouble, I knew I needed to find a source of clean water soon.

After walking for several hours, I stumbled upon a small stream that looked promising. I drank deeply from the stream, feeling a sense of relief wash over me. As I sat there, watching the sun set behind the mountains, I realized something incredible – I was actually alive. I had survived being lost, and despite everything else that had gone wrong, I was still breathing.

In conclusion, I learned the importance of being prepared and having backup plans. I will never forget the lesson I learned from being lost in the woods and the emotional impact it has on everyone involved.

Text: I woke up early today feeling great, but when I looked in the mirror I saw a huge gash on my forehead!
My boyfriend jokingly suggested "You might want to put some Vaseline on your face!"
I replied, "No way, I don't need vaseline on my face."
He laughed and walked off. Later that day, while grocery shopping, I found myself holding my head upside-down, trying to rub Vaseline into the freshly scratched wound!
After much frustration and curses, I finally managed to apply enough Vaseline to cover the wound completely. It seemed to work - my boyfriend didn't notice anything unusual until later in the night when he turned his head over mine and caught sight of the scratch. He couldn't believe it; it was like something out of a horror movie!
The next morning, he brought breakfast to my room and I sat up straight, expecting to find my reflection staring back at me. Instead, there was nothing! Just a big, red scar across my forehead. I tried explaining it to him, but he just shook his head and said, "It looks worse than before."
By the time dinner rolled around, everyone was laughing and enjoying themselves, unaware of my injury. By the end of the night, my entire body ached from laughter. I was sure I would never look the same again... But somehow, I had survived.

Output: Vaseline application worked, no visible injuries, happy ending.

Text: I recently found myself stuck in a conversation with an extremely boring person. At some point, I realized that I was starting to feel overwhelmed. "Are you okay?" I finally asked. She replied, "I don't know. But let's just say I can talk for hours." My mind raced with questions - why? What made her such a compelling speaker? And how could I possibly top that performance? So here goes...
10 years ago, I started teaching English abroad. It wasn't easy, but it gave me something to look forward to every day. That was until I lost my job. Suddenly, I was alone again, without any plans for the future. All I knew was that I didn't want to end up back where I started. One day, while walking through the park, I stumbled upon a group of students doing yoga. They looked different than anyone else I had ever seen. They smiled at each other, moved gracefully, and spoke softly. Something clicked inside me. This wasn't just another yoga class; this was something more. A connection between people, a shared experience. Afterward, I spent time talking with these students, learning about their lives, and discovering things about myself that I never knew before. I learned that sometimes, it takes stepping outside your comfort zone to find your true passions. Today, I teach English online full-time. It isn't perfect, but it's enough. I still remember those moments when I walked into the park, feeling lost and uncertain. But now, whenever I step onto the stage, I am filled with confidence and excitement. I've discovered something special within myself, and it has changed my life forever.

Text: My friend called yesterday saying he has a job offer from a company in San Francisco! I'm excited because it means we can finally afford a house there. But then his sister called us both crying and telling us her brother passed away last weekend. She asked us if we knew what happened and we didn't. We spent the rest of our day going over everything again and realizing we need to make arrangements ASAP.

We talked about how sad it was for her family and we promised to keep in touch and try to visit when possible. It brought tears to my eyes thinking about my grandpa passing away. I feel really guilty for not being able to help her more.

The next day, we received a call from the funeral home letting us know that the arrangements were completed and the body will arrive on Tuesday. They also sent us a map of where to pick up the car. It seems like forever ago that we were sitting in the same room discussing the details of my great-grandfather's funeral. I felt very helpless knowing that I couldn't make things better for her.

I hope these examples showcase different types of humorous situations that might arise in daily conversations.

a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it.

5 hours later a plethora of xrays and a catscan that is going to cost me probably around 6k, i find out i broke my back(compression fracture of my l5 vertebrae). now i'm home laying here in pain and unable to sleep.

 

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.

Text: I just stumbled upon these little black dresses on sale. They were only $7.99 each, but they were practically perfect in every way! The fabric was soft and flowy, and the style was chic yet simple. I immediately grabbed them without hesitation, knowing that I would wear them often enough to justify their price tag.

As soon as I opened the package, I knew something wasn't quite right. The dresses were incredibly small. I tried them on, and they fit perfectly - until I walked down the street. Then, they started to stretch unnaturally. My shoulders began to bulge underneath the material, and my legs felt shorter than ever before. It was humiliating.

The next morning, I woke up feeling embarrassed and disheveled. Everyone else seemed fine, though, and no one seemed to notice what happened to me. I couldn't believe how quickly I became invisible. How dare they treat me like this?

I tried to rationalize it away, telling myself that maybe I was wearing too much makeup or something. But it kept happening, and eventually, I realized that I needed help. So, I went online and searched for 'black dress size issues.' That's where I came across this website called www.sizeboutique.com.

They specialized in helping people find clothes that fit them correctly. After reading through their reviews, I signed up and received personalized recommendations for clothing sizes. Within days, I had a new pair of pants, a dress, and shoes that fitted perfectly. I also learned that sometimes, all you need is some extra time and patience to figure out what fits you properly.

Now, whenever I see someone who looks smaller than me, I remind myself of this experience. It taught me that sometimes, people will treat us unfairly because they don't understand our struggles. We shouldn't let that stop us from pursuing happiness and fulfillment.

Text: A comedic poem I wrote during a particularly bad breakup.

I fell in love once, oh how I did fall in love.
With a girl who was every man’s dream.
But alas, fate had other plans, and our love ended up fizzling out.
It wasn’t easy breaking up, but we tried our best.
We went through the motions, talked on the phone daily.
We met at concerts and shared stories of days gone by.
The world outside us seemed to pass by, without a care.
Then one day, he left town, without any explanation.
My heart sank, but I held onto hope.
Days turned into weeks, and finally into months.
When I saw him again, I felt an electric surge.
He looked different, but somehow familiar too.
Our conversations were longer, more meaningful.
But still, something felt wrong.

One evening, we met up at a coffee shop downtown.
As soon as we arrived, his face lit up.
“Hey, I know what’s bothering you,” he said.
“You don’t understand, it’s over.”
I couldn’t believe it; he was done with me.
And though I knew deep down it would hurt,
I couldn’t help feeling relieved.
We walked home together, hand in hand.
A warm breeze blew through the city streets.
Together, we danced under streetlights.
For a moment, everything felt okay.

Except, the next morning, I woke up with a start.
To find a note lying beside my bed.
It read “Forever yours” and signed off with a kiss.

Oh no, what does this mean?
Am I imagining things?
Or has he truly moved on?

Overwhelmed with emotion, I threw open the door.
Inside, I found him waiting, tears streaming down his face.
“Why do you look sad?” he whispered.
“I’m sorry,” I stammered.
He leaned close, put his arm around me.
"I miss you," he said.
“Me too,” I replied.

From that day forward, our lives became intertwined.
We spent countless afternoons exploring new places.
Our bond grew stronger each passing week.
Until one summer afternoon, I received a call.

“Mike,” he began, “I want to end our relationship.”
“What?” I cried. “Why now?”
“Because I need space,” he explained.
“Space from you,” I agreed.

After that conversation, I felt like nothing could ever be the same.
My life changed forever, and I was left alone.
Now, years later, I sit here writing these words.
I remember the way we used to talk,
How we used to laugh until we cry.
The moments we shared, that will always stay with me.
They brought me joy, they gave me peace.

So let’s celebrate the memories, and cherish the ones yet to come.
Let’s hold tightly to the ones we’re holding dear,
Lest we forget, and lose sight of where we came from.

Text: when my friend told me about her experience with a boy who had been stalking her online since high school, I immediately started thinking about how I might have fallen victim to something similar if I hadn't grown up too fast.

I felt sickened by the idea of someone watching over me every step of the way, constantly waiting for me to make a mistake or fall into their trap. It wasn't until later, after I had graduated college, that I realized just how much of an impact such a fear could have on our lives.

My heart raced whenever I saw him. He was always smiling, always seemingly friendly, but deep down I knew he was staring at me intently. And yet, somehow, I couldn't bring myself to look away. It was like a vicious cycle – each time I looked his way, I felt more trapped, more vulnerable.

It wasn't until I met someone else who shared my experiences that I began to see the extent of what I had gone through. We talked about our feelings, our fears, and how it all felt like a prison sentence. That conversation opened up a whole new world of possibilities for me, and allowed me to start rebuilding some of the trust and confidence that had been taken away from me.

In the end, I learned that sometimes, the most significant moments in life come not from external factors, but rather from internal ones. Sometimes, it takes courage to confront your own demons, and to find the strength within yourself to overcome them. But in the end, the price of self-discovery is often worth it.

Text: I recently read an article by Jared Diamond where he discusses how global warming will lead to a collapse of civilization. His argument is that the world's climate has changed many times throughout history due to natural causes, such as volcanic eruptions and solar flares, yet we continue to build cities and infrastructure despite these past events. He argues that our current technological advancements, combined with the rapid pace of urban development, make it difficult to adapt to changing climates. This is not necessarily true. Cities can be built to withstand extreme weather conditions. In fact, some cities have already adapted to extreme weather events through measures such as elevating buildings and installing green roofs. Furthermore, technology can help us prepare for future disasters. For example, satellites provide real-time data on severe storms and floods, allowing governments to better plan for emergencies. We need to focus less on trying to prevent global warming and more on preparing ourselves for its consequences.

In his article, Diamond also mentions the potential impact of human activity on other species. If humans continue to destroy ecosystems, it could eventually lead to the extinction of many animals. However, if we actively work towards preserving nature, we may be able to protect animal habitats and reduce their exposure to disease. Overall, Diamond suggests that we approach climate change as a problem rather than simply accepting its reality. It requires a collective effort to address this issue, including individual action and cooperation between nations.

Edit: [Diamond's response to critics](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xGHJQ8z7C6U). Edit 2: [Another perspective on the issue](https://twitter.com/jim_hoggan/status/905593454425413888). Input: Text: The most important thing I learned during my trip to India was that poverty isn’t just about money. Instead, it’s about having enough food, clean water, and access to education. These basic needs were present everywhere, but they weren’t always met. One family told me about living in a slum near Mumbai, where they had to walk miles each day to find clean drinking water. They spent their days scrubbing filthy streets and gathering firewood, leaving little time for anything else. Another woman showed me a classroom filled with students who couldn’t afford shoes. Despite working hard all day, they would come home hungry because they hadn’t been able to buy enough food to feed themselves. Poverty wasn’t just limited to hunger; it was also about illness. A young boy explained to me that he often missed school because he had to care for sick relatives. Whenever he came home, he was covered in sores and feverish, unable to concentrate on his studies. Finally, poverty wasn’t something only experienced by people in developing countries. My host family lived in a small town outside Delhi, and while they did receive government aid, they struggled to pay for essential items like food and medicine. My mother pointed out that many families in our community were struggling too – especially since the price of oil has skyrocketed. She asked me to consider the possibility that rising costs could hurt everyone equally, regardless of income level. Output: Got toilets installed in homes across India thanks to your support.

Text: so yesterday I went on an amazing adventure with my friend and we ended up in a completely random alleyway where there were no stores nearby. We were just wandering around trying to find something when we stumbled upon a group of kids playing tag. It wasn't much, but it felt like a victory nonetheless because it meant they weren't bothering us.

After a few minutes, we realized that these kids had set up a giant obstacle course made entirely of cardboard boxes. They started by having us run through them, then move on to climbing over them, then running backward through them. It was insane and exhilarating all at once. As we were finishing our loop, we heard a loud scream coming from down the street.

We looked down and saw a little girl crying. Her mother was frantically searching for her. Without thinking twice, we ran toward the sound, hoping to help her find her daughter. When we finally found her, we were greeted with tears and apologies. That moment solidified how incredibly lucky we both were to meet each other and experience such a unique and memorable moment together.

outputs: Text: "I don't know what happened yesterday." I said after looking at my phone during dinner. "My mom sent me an SMS message saying 'Hey, your sister called you tonight.'" My mom always calls us early. She usually gets home by 9pm and then hangs up without speaking. "It wasn't weird because she always does that," I explained. "She wanted to tell you something important," my mother replied. I couldn't believe how many times she did that over the past few months. We were getting worried. It wasn't like we hadn't talked yet; we just hadn't been talking very much lately. But we figured she might need some extra help managing everything. "Can you give me more details?" I asked. "Yeah," she replied. "She told me that your father died unexpectedly last month." Oh God. This was worse than any dream I could ever imagine. My heart stopped. What if she lied? Whenever my mother mentioned anything about him, it was almost like a trigger that reminded me that he was gone. Now I realized that she had probably found out through some sort of social media site or maybe even a friend of mine. That's when it hit me - we weren't friends anymore. I felt like a part of me had disappeared forever. My mind raced as I tried to figure out where to start. Wherever my parents lived, they wouldn't allow anyone else to visit them except family members. So that meant I was alone. I wondered how many people had known about my father's death. Was it possible that someone had spread rumors or leaked information to others, knowing full well that I didn't know? I tried calling my best friend Sarah, but she didn't answer. Her cellphone number was disconnected. I sat there for several minutes, staring blankly ahead. Then I remembered something. "Mom, I need to talk to you." I reached across the table and touched her hand. She looked surprised, but also relieved. "What is it?" "I want to ask you something," I said softly. "Is it true that your brother, David, has cancer again?"

Text: I'm a little bit embarrassed by how much time I spend on social media. It has become such an integral part of my life, and I don't want to let it consume me completely. Text: I recently found myself in need of a new laptop, and I don't know where to begin looking. It seems like every website has their own unique layout and design. So I thought I would try searching for laptops by category. But then I realized I wasn't sure what kind of laptop I needed.
So I decided to just browse them all. And lo and behold, the results were staggeringly confusing. Here's a sample search result: "Best Laptop Under $200".
I think you get the idea. My eyes glazed over, and I clicked "next" without even thinking.

Now, I know you want to hear more about my adventures in online shopping. But before we dive too deep into that, let me explain why I've been such a poor internet user. As someone who grew up on computers, I never really learned how to navigate websites properly.
I spent most of my time clicking buttons instead of reading content. It took me forever to figure out how to scroll down a page. Whenever I wanted to click a link, I had to keep tapping the same spot repeatedly until it lit up. This made me feel frustrated and confused, and I didn't learn anything useful from doing it.

This experience led me to believe that I was the only person in the world who could use web browsers correctly. But then I discovered Google Reviews. Sure enough, many other users had gone through similar experiences. They wrote reviews of websites they visited, explaining exactly how to use them. Suddenly, everything became clear.

My next step was to sign up for Gmail. I remember being amazed at how easy it was to create an account. I typed in my email address, hit enter, and boom, I was done. But then I started using Gmail regularly. At first, it felt like magic. I opened my inbox and saw a sea of emails waiting for me. Some looked promising, others looked terrible. Most of them were junk mail, though. After a few weeks, I noticed that I was getting fewer emails than I expected. I checked my settings and discovered that I hadn't enabled "mark as spam." These emails weren't worth wasting my time on anymore.

Next, I signed up for Yelp. I remember loving it at first. I liked seeing what restaurants near me were popular. Then I started to notice that there were no reviews available for these places. Nope, nothin'. That was weird. Finally, I remembered the Google Reviews thing. I Googled "Yelp reviews [restaurant name]" and read reviews from real customers. There were lots of bad ones, but there were also plenty of great ones. I decided to give one restaurant a shot - Sweetgreen. To my surprise, the reviews were mostly positive. One customer said she loved the salads and the atmosphere. Another mentioned that her server was friendly and knowledgeable. Those reviews helped me decide whether to eat there.

After those experiences, I realized that I needed to become more confident in navigating the Internet. So I started learning how to code. It sounds intimidating, but it turned out to be pretty fun. I started writing small programs to solve problems. For example, I created a program to convert Celsius temperature to Fahrenheit. Or another one to calculate pi. I enjoyed making things happen, and I began to feel more comfortable navigating the Web.

But even coding taught me lessons about navigation. Sometimes I accidentally pressed the wrong button or forgot to close a tab. Sometimes I didn't understand what I was supposed to do. But each mistake felt like a tiny victory. I felt more confident, more capable.

In conclusion, navigating the Internet can seem daunting. But once you learn how to make simple mistakes, you'll find yourself improving quickly. Try signing up for Gmail, finding your way around Yelp, and maybe even trying to code. You might discover that you enjoy the process, and soon enough, you won't even realize you're doing it.

Text: A friend told me I needed to eat some avocado everyday, but I never thought how easy it could be until now. Here's what I did today.

Avocados are loaded with health benefits like high fiber, vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. They're low calorie too. But they can sometimes taste a bit bland, especially when not used in their natural state. So, here's how you can make them tastier without any additional ingredients.

Step 3: Top With Fresh Veggies - Use fresh veggies like cucumber, tomato, red bell pepper, etc. For extra crunch and sweetness.

Ingredients:
- 4 ripe avocados
- Salt & Pepper
- Olive oil
- Toasted bread
- Fresh herbs (optional)

Instructions:
1. Cut open the avocado using a knife. Remove the pit and mash the flesh inside with a fork. Set aside.
2. Preheat oven to 180°C / Gas Mark 6.
3. Spread the mashed avocado evenly over each slice of bread. Season generously with salt and pepper.
4. Place the toasted side down onto a baking sheet. Bake for around 7-8 minutes, until the top is golden brown.
5. Serve hot with fresh vegetables and enjoy!

This version has added some greens and protein sources like eggs and nuts to give it a satisfying breakfast boost.

However, recently I came across an article about a restaurant called "French Fried Pig" located in a small town outside of Philadelphia. After reading their description of what they serve, I knew I had to check them out. So, I decided to drive down to visit.

Upon arrival, we were immediately welcomed by the owner, Tom, and his wife, Emily. They showed us around the restaurant and told us all about their menu items. After dinner, we decided to grab some drinks at the bar. I ordered a French 75 cocktail made with gin, lemon juice, honey syrup, and Campari. It was incredibly refreshing and perfect for the summer weather.

Overall, our experience at French Fried Pig was fantastic. The atmosphere was charming, the service was friendly, and the food was truly exceptional. I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for something unique and different to try while in Philly.

Text: A week ago I decided to join a fitness challenge group online, I wanted to make healthier choices in my diet and exercise routine. However, I quickly realized I needed to lose weight fast before the challenge started! My goal was to drop 20 pounds within 4 weeks! So far, I have lost over 18 pounds, but I haven’t seen any changes yet. Here’s why:
I’ve been doing cardio consistently (running, walking, cycling), and eating clean. But what happens when your body gets tired? It will store fat instead of burning it. That means you won’t see significant results right away. Now, I know you might be thinking “Why bother?” After all, losing weight isn’t easy, especially if you live alone. Yes, I can say that because I live alone, I struggle more than those who live in groups. Whenever I feel lazy, I just go to bed early and stay in bed until tomorrow morning, hoping to avoid exercising again. Well, I need to stop this bad habit. I know it sounds crazy, but trust me, it works. If you’re looking for quick results, then you may not even notice the difference between your pre-challenge and current weights. I remember watching my friends and colleagues gain muscles and losing their bodies fat. You see, when they joined the same challenge group, they didn’t experience any progress; however, mine did. They gained muscle mass, but I shed weight. And that’s where the magic happened. I became obsessed with tracking my food intake and calorie burn. This way, I could keep track of every calorie I consumed, and I wouldn’t exceed my daily caloric allowance. Tracking my food helped me understand my macronutrient balance. Every day, I would eat approximately 2000 calories per day. Based on my activity level, I aimed for around 1800-2000 calories per day. For breakfast, I usually consume protein powder mixed with water, along with almond milk. I also add a scoop of whey protein powder, sliced banana, chia seeds, and flaxseeds. Input: Text: so today was my sister's birthday party, a lot of my family was there, probably around 30 people or so. so my 7 year old nephew was talking about riding his bike and i proceed to tell him how awesome i used to be on a bmx. 
a little while later i put my money with my mouth is, jump on his bike and immediately start riding a wheelie. got about 15 feet and pulled to hard on the bike and flipped it. 

instantly i knew something was wrong. i landed on my butt/lowerback and couldn't move much at all. within 30 seconds i have my whole family and a bunch of the neighborhood kids standing around me freaking out. at this point i am going into shock and trying my best not to pass out. i eventually(with some help) managed to stand up. i tried telling everyone i was fine and not to call an ambulance, they did anyways. when they got there, i'm feeling a little better, but still trying not to feint from the pain. i ended up turning the ambulance away and having my brother drive me to the hospital, do to me not being insured.

sorry if my grammar and typing are a little off, i'm not the best.
Output: , tried showing off to a bunch of kids, broke my back and bruised my ego.

Text: I love being a waitress at Chipotle. They always make us feel welcome, even when we aren't really feeling anything.

As soon as our shift starts, the customers start coming. There's usually at least three lines, sometimes four, and every time I see them waiting outside, I smile. But as soon as they enter, their faces fall into disappointment.

One particular customer stood out to me. He was tall, thin, and dressed in black leather pants, boots, and a jacket. His eyes scanned the room, and he looked at me with a mix of disgust and curiosity. I tried to engage him in conversation, asking questions about his vacation plans, but he didn't seem interested. As we finished serving each table, he continued to stare at me, his eyes glinting with suspicion.

I could sense his dislike towards me growing, and I couldn't help but wonder what kind of person he was. Was he rude or intimidating? Did he have something against food?

But as we waited for the next group of customers to arrive, I noticed that he began to calm down. When the last order came in, he smiled at me again, this time without malice. It was then that I realized he wasn't the villain I thought he was.

He was simply a regular customer who needed assistance finding parking. And despite his initial hostility, I felt sorry for him, grateful that I had the opportunity to put a smile on his face.

From that moment forward, I learned that sometimes, even in the restaurant industry, it takes a little extra effort to make someone happy.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Input: Text: obligatory comment about this not actually happening today, and this being a throwaway account.

so like i said, this tifu didn't happen today, but instead happened a little less than a year ago, right before i graduated high school. at the time, i was pretty happy with everything in my life. i was just about to graduate from high school with a decent gpa and sat score, and had already been accepted to the university i wanted to go to. 

with all of this success, i decided it was about time for me to create a professional looking image for myself, which included creating a new email instead of continuing to use the one i made when i was like 12. after making this new email, i switched my phone and computer to only get messages from it, and none from my old email. 

however, in my infinite stupidity, i forgot to change the email i had on my university account to my new one. well around two months later, my parents (who like to be very involved in my life) asked me how much money in scholarships i was going to be getting from the university. i then remembered i had never switched from my old email, and rush to check it. lo and behold, i see 3 or 4 emails from the university telling me to apply for their scholarships, and gradually warning me that the deadline was only getting closer. 

unfortunately for me, i had missed the deadline by a few weeks... and missed out on the 30 grand they offered to students with my sat score. 


 

edit: word choices and better spacing.
Output: created a new email, forgot to switch my university account  from the old one, and obliviously stood by while enough scholarship money to buy a brand new car vaporized into thin air.

Text: I went to see my favorite band play live today, and it wasn't what I expected. It started off great, but then suddenly something happened.

I turned to my friend, and without even looking away, I asked her if she noticed anything different. She looked down at her feet and shook her head.

"No," she replied, "not really."

The next song came along, and once again, the same thing happened. This time, though, things took a turn for the worse. Suddenly, my friend began screaming incoherently. Her face contorted into a mask of agony, and her eyes rolled back into their sockets.

My heart sank as I realized that something terrible had happened. My best friend, who I love more than anyone else in the world, had fallen victim to a stage fright attack.

As soon as the show ended, I ran over to check on her. When I reached her side, I found her lying motionless on the ground. I tried CPR, but nothing seemed to help. I called the ambulance, and as soon as they arrived, my friend passed away.

It was a devastating loss, and it left me feeling completely broken. For weeks afterwards, I couldn't stop thinking about her. Every day felt like a new tragedy waiting to happen. But slowly, I learned to cope with my grief. I talked to friends and family, sought support from therapists, and even started writing songs about my experiences.

In the end, my friend became a symbol of hope for many others who suffered similar losses. She showed us that sometimes, the greatest pain can bring forth the strongest strength. And although our memories will forever haunt us, her memory lives on, as a testament to the power of human resilience.

Text: I've been working on this poem for months. It's something really important to me, and I feel like I can finally finish it. But every time I try to write down what I mean, I start crying. Why? Because I know that if anyone else reads this, they will see exactly what I'm feeling right now. And I hate that. I hate that my emotions are being shared publicly. I hate that my poetry feels more personal than anything else in my life. I hate that my heart feels exposed when I share these words.

The other person in the room nodded sympathetically.

"I feel the same way," they said softly.

Then another student chimed in.

"Yeah, sometimes it feels like nobody gets us."

And suddenly, everything clicked. We were talking about our own struggles with writing poems and how hard it is to find validation for our ideas. I felt relieved to hear those words coming from others too.

It was a relief to finally put pen to paper and say aloud what I was thinking and feeling. It wasn't easy, but I realized that sharing my thoughts was worth it because it helped me understand why I wrote certain things and allowed me to move forward.

We left class feeling grateful for each other's company and hopeful that we might connect over art sometime soon.

Later that afternoon, as I sat alone in my bedroom, staring at my computer screen, I couldn't help but wonder what kind of poem I could create if I didn't care about finding validation for my ideas anymore. Would I still love poetry? Would I still feel moved by its power? Or would I just use it as a tool to express my feelings without giving them meaning?

That's when I remembered the poem I started earlier today. Maybe it wouldn't be perfect yet, maybe it would need editing, but I wanted to show it to someone anyway. I typed it up and sent it to a friend who loves poetry.

A couple days later, I received an email back saying they loved the poem and that their mother read it to her children tonight and found it beautiful. That little exchange gave me such a sense of joy knowing that my work mattered enough to make someone happy.

Now I realize that poetry isn't always meant to be published, but sometimes it's okay to simply write down whatever comes to mind. Sometimes it's okay to admit that we're human and that our emotions aren't always logical or neat. Sometimes it's okay to be vulnerable and allow ourselves to be seen and heard.

Maybe it won't lead to publishing success, but maybe it will open doors for new connections and opportunities. Maybe it will even inspire someone else to pursue their own creative dreams. Whatever it leads to, I'll take it.
